# Bugs

Known compiler defects: incorrect output, crashes, miscompiles, rejection of valid code, missing diagnostics for unsafe code.

For missing features and language design gaps see `TODO.md`.

Each entry's first line is a **[priority size]** tag plus a one-sentence summary; the full description follows on the next lines. Priority is one of:

- `IMM` -- users hit this in their first non-trivial program (or basic Python idioms);
- `HIGH` -- users hit this regularly in non-trivial programs / stdlib work;
- `MED` -- specific patterns or advanced features;
- `LOW` -- latent / quality / hardening, no current user impact.

Size is one of `small` (hours-1d), `medium` (1-3d), `large` (~week), `xlarge` (bigger).

Entries may carry an immutable **slug** in brackets right after the headline (e.g. ``[`union-nocopy-field-store`]``) -- a stable anchor for pointing at one entry out of hundreds. Add one when an entry is first referenced (from source, a test, or another entry); new entries get one up front. Every reference, in code comments and inside this file alike, is spelled ``BUGS.md#<slug>`` -- an anchor-style token that cannot collide with ordinary prose, so one grep finds every reference. A slug never changes once assigned, even if the headline is later reworded, and `tpyc/test_bugs_slugs.py` fails on a reference whose entry is gone -- so a fixed entry cannot be deleted while a stale pointer to it survives. **What that check does NOT cover:** it validates `BUGS.md#<slug>` citations only. Around 150 source and test files still mention `BUGS.md` as a bare file reference, which cannot dangle but also cannot be resolved to an entry, and nothing counts them down. The backlog this convention has to work through is therefore the REFERENCE side, not the entry side -- an un-slugged entry costs nothing, an un-slugged reference is the thing that sends a reader to an 829-entry file.

Entries tagged `deferred: MIR` are gated on the THIR/MIR migration (see `docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Open Questions 9/11/13) and must NOT be patched in the current AST/sema model -- the clean fix lands in the IR. Do not select them for `/tpy-next` or `/tpy-fix-bug`.

## Compiler bugs

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Slice assignment on a user record with a slice-keyed `__setitem__` is rejected outright.** [`record-slice-assign-rejected`]
  `g[0:2] = 9` on a record whose `__setitem__` takes `slice` fails at sema with `Slice assignment not supported for type 'Own[Grid]'`, while the plain `g[0] = 5` resolves and CPython runs both. The rule predates the dunder lookup; a slice key should resolve through `__setitem__` like any other. Found while closing the `@dispatch` `__getitem__` operator gap (2026-09-10).
- **[MED small] (unlocated diagnostic; ill-formed C++ inside a tuple) A `bytes` value at a `bytearray` PARAMETER never reaches the located cross-buffer rule.** [`bytes-at-bytearray-param-unlocated`] `def f(b: bytearray)` called as `f(p)` with `p: bytes` rejects at `call.arg_shape.record_nonf1`, and the tuple form `def f(t: tuple[bytearray, int])` called as `f((p, 1))` is accepted by sema outright and fails in the C++ toolchain -- codegen emits `std::tuple<ByteArray*, ...>{&(p), ...}`, taking the address of a `bytes` value for a `ByteArray*` slot. A `bytearray` is a reference type, so its parameter takes the reference/pointer form and the argument never routes through the value-bind check the rule lives on; the OWNING sinks of the same direction (a local, a field, a return) do reach it and give the `write 'bytearray(...)' around it` message. Pre-existing and unchanged by the tuple-element fix (verified against a detached worktree at 578932992e: identical on both). The fix is to route the reference-typed parameter bind through the same check, not to add a second one. Met 2026-09-10 while sweeping the recursive arms of `_check_compat`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Reading an `Optional` element back out of a container does not lower.** [`optional-container-element-read-unlowered`] With `d: dict[str, bytes | None] = {"k": b"ab"}`, `v = d["k"]` rejects at `stmt.var_decl:subscript.elem.optional` and `for v in d.values()` at `stmt.for_each:iter.method_call_shape`, while the STORE and `len(d)` both lower; CPython reads it back with no ceremony. The `list[bytes | None]` sibling rejects at the same tag. It is the VALUE-typed payload that fails, not Optional elements in general: the reference-typed `dict[str, R | None]` reads back and runs. Pre-existing and unrelated to the cross-buffer rule (no bytearray is involved in any witness); met 2026-09-10 while pinning that rule's wrapped face, which is why `tests/cases/bytes/bytearray_copy_into_bytes_sink` observes its copy on an Optional LOCAL and only counts the dict one.

- **[LOW small] (message quality; the rejection itself is correct) The container-LITERAL element seam rewrites every targeted diagnostic raised under it, so the remediation is lost.** [`literal-elem-seam-swallows-remediation`] `_analyze_list_literal`'s contextual arm wraps its per-element `check_type_compatible` in `except SemanticError` and re-raises a fixed *List literal element N has type X, incompatible with annotated element type Y*. Any rule that fires INSIDE that call and carries a fix -- the mismatch's conversion hint *write 'bytes(...)' around it*, `_check_polymorphic_slicing`'s *use `Box[Throwable]`* -- is replaced by the generic text, so the user is told what is wrong but not what to write. The dict/set literal arms wrap the same way. Pre-existing (the slicing hint has been swallowed there since it was added); surfaced 2026-09-10 when the bytearray-at-an-owning-bytes-sink rule reached the literal face. The fix needs a way for a targeted diagnostic to survive the wrapper (a marker on `SemanticError`, or the seam asking `_check_compat` first and framing only its `CompatError`) -- a shared-diagnostic change, so it is filed rather than improvised. `tests/cases/bytes/error_bytearray_in_bytes_literal` pins the seam's text as it stands. The same wrap-and-swallow shape recurs at the LAMBDA-RETURN check (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~4180-4188), so a general fix should cover both rather than unwrapping the literal arm alone. A third face is the CONTAINER-INVARIANT path (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` ~1199/1354/1375), which does not wrap a raised diagnostic but builds its own `CompatError` from the element pair and so never reaches the hint: `d2: dict[int, bytes] = d1` over a `dict[int, bytearray]` reports *expected bytes, got bytearray* and the `list` twin *expected list[bytes], got list[bytearray]*, both correct rejections with no *write 'bytes(...)' around it*. Verified identical at 305c187198, before the hint became data, so it is pre-existing there too; the fix shape is the same -- let the element check's own error through instead of re-forming one. A fourth face: an owning UNION-typed sink (`bytes | Indexed` field written from a bytearray) rejects through `_check_compat`'s union member loop, which asks the row veto per member but computes the *write 'bytes(...)' around it* hint only for the direct pair, so the message arrives without it. Same fix shape.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Own[bytes]` parameter takes only a bytes LITERAL: every other source rejects.** [`own-bytes-param-takes-only-a-literal`] With `def take(b: Own[bytes]) -> int`, `take(b"ab")` lowers while `take(bytes(x))` (a call rvalue), `take(name)` (an owned `bytes` local) and the `BytesView`-typed local all reject at `call.arg_shape.own_bytes`; the constructor twin `H(bytes(x))` / `H(name)` rejects at `call.ctor_arg.own_bytes` while `H(b"ab")` lowers. The `Own[bytes]` CONTAINER-ELEMENT slot (`xs.append(bytes(x))`) takes all of them, so the gap is the non-element `Own[bytes]` slot rather than the payload: `_bytes_owned_slot_arg` / `_bytes_owned_name_arg` / `_bytes_owned_call_rvalue_arg` in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` are reached from the element seam only. Pre-existing (no bytearray is involved in any witness). Found while pinning the bytearray-at-an-owning-bytes-sink rule; `tests/cases/bytes/bytearray_copy_into_bytes_sink` covers the element face and says why the other two are absent.

- **[HIGH small] (silent UAF, reads by luck) An RVALUE at a `readonly[T]` generic slot is not hoisted into a caller temp, so a generator factory's capture dangles.** [`readonly-tparam-slot-skips-arg-temp`] `def use_ro[T: Sized](obj: readonly[T], count: Int32) -> Iterator[Int32]` called as `for t in use_ro("ro", 2)` emits `auto __src_0 = use_ro<std::string>("ro", 2);` with no `std::string __tmp_N`, while the same call at a BARE `T` slot hoists one. The factory binds `const T&` to a temporary materialized for the call, whose lifetime ends with that declaration statement, and the peephole captures `[&obj]` into a lambda the for-loop pulls afterwards -- the exact shape `_borrowing_frame_callee`'s temp exists to prevent (BUGS.md#simple-generator-captures-open-t-param-by-reference). It reads back correct values at -O0, so no suite instrument sees it. Cause: the argument gate's temp rows sit under `if isinstance(ptype, TypeParamRef)` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`), and a `readonly[T]` param's raw type is a `ReadonlyType`, so the whole branch is skipped -- even though `_generic_arg_slot`, which the branch consults, already unwraps readonly and answers `needs_temp` correctly for it. Pre-existing and identical on master (same guard, and master spells that slot `const T&` too). Fix shape: key the branch on `_is_type_param_slot(ptype)`, the predicate that already means "bare `T` through the readonly / Ref wrappers", and re-bin the snapshot churn over every `readonly[T]` generic slot. `tests/cases/iterators/gen_generic` feeds its `readonly[T]` sections a NAMED local for exactly this reason. Found pinning the readonly borrow-frame slot 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A simple generator YIELDS a bare `T` by value, so a reference-typed instantiation loses every mutation made through the yielded value.** [`generic-generator-yields-open-t-by-value`] `def rep[T: Appendable](obj: T, n: Int32) -> Iterator[T]: obj.append(1); while ...: yield obj` consumed as `for v in rep(b, 2): v.append(10)` leaves `b.total == 1` in TPy and `21` in CPython: the peephole renders `::tpy::make_generator<T>` with `std::optional<T>` and `auto __val = obj;`, a COPY, because the yield form is decided on the open `T` whose `is_value_type()` is False-but-unknown. The MONOMORPHIC twin is correct -- `def rep_mono(obj: Bin, ...)` renders `make_generator<::tpy::val_or_ref<Bin>>` and prints `20` like CPython -- so this is the same "form decided on the open `T`" family as BUGS.md#simple-generator-captures-open-t-param-by-reference and the same `generic-equals-monomorphic-twin` rule in `docs/PITFALLS.md`. The mutation made through the PARAMETER is visible (the slot is a reference at every instantiation); only what the consumer does to the yielded value is lost. Pre-existing: the yield render is `gen_generators.py`, untouched by the distinct-C++-types unit, and the shape compiled on master. Fix shape: spell the yield type through the same instantiation-keyed trait the monomorphic path uses (`val_or_ref_t<T>`), not the bare `T`. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/stringtype_impl/probe_move/protomut.py` (generic) and `.../yieldcopy.py` (the twin). Found verifying the borrow-frame parameter form 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A single-yield generator iterating a `str` or `bytes` PARAMETER does not compile.** [`peephole-view-param-iter-decltype`] `def chars(s: str) -> Iterator[Char]: for c in s: yield c` emits the simple-generator peephole `[s = std::string(s), __beg = decltype((s).begin())(), __end = decltype((s).begin())(), __init = false]`: the init-capture copies the view into an owned buffer, but each `decltype` is evaluated in the ENCLOSING scope, against the `std::string_view` parameter, so the members are `const char*` while `__beg = (s).begin()` inside the body yields `std::string::iterator` -- g++ reports *cannot convert ... to 'const char*' in assignment*. The bytes twin is the same shape (`::tpy::BytesView` iterator vs `::tpy::Bytes` iterator). TWO yields compile: the resumable route stores the owned buffer in a frame member, so its iterator type is taken from the member. The render is `gen_generators.py`'s capture list, untouched by the distinct-C++-types unit, and the fix is to take the `decltype` from the capture (`decltype(std::declval<owned&>().begin())` or an explicit owned-iterator spelling). Reproducer `/tmp/agents/stringtype_impl/probe_move/peep.py`. Found by the merge hunt 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A generic record that INHERITS its `__init__` cannot be constructed at a view-family instantiation.** [`inherited-generic-ctor-view-arg`] `class Derived[T](Base[T]): pass` over `class Base[T]` with `def __init__(self, value: T)` rejects `Derived[str]("hi")` at `expr.call:call.ctor_arg.generic`, while `Base[str]("hi")` lowers through the same argument and `Derived[Int32](5)` lowers through the same route -- so it is the pair (inherited `__init__`, view-family instantiation), not either alone. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/stringtype_impl/probe_move/derived.py`. Found by the merge hunt 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) Indexing a string LITERAL directly is ambiguous in C++.** [`str-literal-index-ambiguous`] `print("xyz"[1])` renders `::tpy::__getitem__("xyz", 1)` with a `const char[4]` argument, and `dunder.hpp` offers `__getitem__(const std::string&, int32_t)` and `__getitem__(std::string_view, int32_t)` -- two user-defined conversions of equal rank, so g++ reports *call of overloaded '__getitem__(const char [4], int)' is ambiguous*. Binding the literal to a local first (`s = "xyz"; s[1]`) compiles and runs, and the SLICE form (`"abc"[0:2]`) compiles because `str_slice` takes the view alone, so it is the index form on a bare literal only. `__len__` already carries a `const char*` overload for exactly this reason; the fix is the same one line for `__getitem__`. Pre-existing and identical on master (probed at 561766ec7e in a detached worktree). No case in the corpus indexes a bare literal. Found probing subscripts after the dispatch-split merge 2026-09-10.


- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple literal cannot contain the Char produced by string indexing.** [`char-tuple-literal-admission`]
  Inside a narrowed `case str()` arm, `one = (x[0],)` rejects at `decl.tuple_literal_shape`, while the scalar `x[0]` and the byte-valued tuple sibling compile. `_value_tuple_element_ok` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` excludes Char; the nested value-tuple and tuple-declaration gates inherit that exclusion before lowering the element expression. This predicate and its explicit Char exclusion predate the master merge at `987d04c5`. CPython's string-index result is a normal one-character string and can be stored in a tuple. Fix shape: assess Char element construction, storage and reads across tuple positions together, preserving the scalar element's value semantics. Found while adding scalar/tuple controls for narrowed indexing; the passing regression uses the byte-valued sibling. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A comparison whose operand is a SUBCLASS of the record dunder's declared parameter is rejected.** [`record-eq-subtype-operand-rejects`]
  With `class Puddle(Dog)` and `Dog.__eq__(self, other: "Dog")`, `d == p` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:binop.shape.==.record`; CPython runs it (`True` when `Puddle` inherits the dunder, `False` when it overrides it -- Python gives a SUBCLASS operand's method priority in BOTH operand orders). The reject fires whether or not `Puddle` overrides `__eq__`, so it also refuses the shape where the upcast is plainly right. Same row as `BUGS.md#derived-ne-unchecked-operand`: `_record_dunder_operand_pair` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) gates the operand on sema's arg-compatibility predicate, which pins the operand to the declared parameter type rather than admitting a derived one. The explicit `d.__eq__(p)` spelling is accepted (and misbehaves -- see the entry below). **The fix's constraint:** admitting the upcast is only correct when the subclass does NOT override the dunder, or under `@dynamic` dispatch. Records are not polymorphic here, so an admitted upcast static-dispatches to `Dog::__eq__` and silently ignores `Puddle.__eq__` -- which is exactly the divergence the entry below measures at the spellings that already compile. So this reject is the only thing keeping the direct spelling off that divergence: fixing it alone WIDENS the silent one, and the two must land together. Probes `/tmp/agents/puddle/main.py` and `/tmp/agents/refunion_impl/puddle2/main.py`. Found while reviewing the reference-union storage form 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning, two spellings) A record `__eq__` overridden in a subclass is bypassed at every comparison that compiles, and an explicit dunder CALL picks the subclass's where Python does not.** [`record-eq-subclass-static-dispatch`]
  With `Dog.__eq__(self, other: "Dog")` returning `self.n == other.n` and `class Puddle(Dog)` overriding it to `False`, over `d = Dog(1)` and `p = Puddle(1)` (both fields `1`): `d.__eq__(p)` answers **False** where CPython answers True, and `takes(d, p)` / `takes(p, d)` with `def takes(a: Dog, b: Dog): return a == b` answer **True** where CPython answers False. Two different causes, one root -- C++ overload resolution standing in for Python's method lookup: (1) the explicit dunder call renders as the operator (`(d) == (p)`), and C++20's REVERSED candidate makes `Puddle`'s hidden friend `operator==(const Puddle&, const Dog&)` an exact match on both parameters where `Dog`'s needs a derived-to-base conversion, so the subclass's method wins a call that Python defines as unreflected; (2) through base-typed parameters both operands are `const Dog&`, the friends are non-virtual, so `Dog::__eq__` is called and the override is ignored -- Python would give the `Puddle` operand priority. No warning on either. CPython prints `True False` where TPy prints `False True`. Probe `/tmp/agents/refunion_impl/puddle4/main.py` (prints the fields, both explicit-dunder orders and both base-param orders). Sibling of `BUGS.md#record-eq-subtype-operand-rejects`, which is the reject that keeps the DIRECT `d == p` spelling from reaching cause (2); fix shape must decide how a record dunder dispatches when a subclass overrides it (virtual dispatch for an overridden dunder, or a rejection at the spellings that cannot honour Python's rule) rather than widening the operand gate first. Found while reviewing the reference-union storage form 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A type alias whose body names an IMPORTED type alias is rejected as an unknown type.** [`imported-alias-member-in-alias-body`]
  `from tpy import Float64` then `type Mixed = Dog | Int32 | Float64` fails with `Type alias 'Mixed' references unknown type 'Float64'`, and so does the bare `type Alias = Float64`. The same type spelled inline in a signature (`def f(x: Float64 | str)`) compiles, and a SAME-module alias-of-alias (`type Money = float` then `type A = Money | str`) compiles -- only the imported alias fails. `_validate_type_alias_members` in `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py` accepts a member `NominalType` only when it carries a `_module_qname` or resolves in the record registry; an imported alias binding has neither at that point, so the validator refuses a name it merely has not resolved yet. Reachable from the stdlib today because `Float64` is itself an alias (`type Float64 = float` in `lib/tpy/tpy/__init__.py`) and from any user module that exports one (`from m import Money`). CPython accepts every spelling. Workaround: spell the underlying type (`float`) or write the union inline -- `tests/cases/union/reference_union_storage_eq` cites this entry and takes the `float` spelling for that reason. Repro `/tmp/agents/refunion_impl/alias5/`. Fix shape: resolve imported alias bindings before the alias-member validation, or let the validator consult the alias table sema already holds -- the same check-runs-before-the-name-is-bound family as the cycle re-export entries. Found spelling the record-beside-numerics pack for the reference-union storage compare 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Value-union boundaries reject a bytes member even though its signature and match body can lower.** [`bytes-value-union-boundary-rejects`] When these boundaries widen, the `bytearray_to_bytes` coercion's `identity` disposition (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`, the `_coerce_disposition` row) has to grow an arm: it assumes the only reachable `bytes` slot is the span view a `bytearray` satisfies bare, but at a union slot the alternative is `const ::tpy::Bytes*`, so an identity pass would render `::tpy::Union<..., const ::tpy::Bytes*>{&ba}` -- ill-formed C++, loud but unlocated. A materialize or a located reject belongs there before the admission widens.
  For `x: bytes | Int32`, `if isinstance(x, bytes)` rejects at `stmt.if:cond.call`, before the body reaches subscript lowering. A local `data: bytes | Int32 = b"abc"` likewise rejects at `decl.slot_type`. `_eligible_value_union` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` admits str/StrView but omits bytes, and `_builtin_value_member` explicitly excludes the BYTES category. The union is value-form, so pointer-union admission cannot rescue it. The isinstance rejection reproduces before the master merge at `987d04c5` and after the match-subscript repair; the local gate uses the same unchanged eligibility predicate. The `bytes | Indexed` pointer-union sibling accepts a bytes-literal call and runs the same indexing body. Fix shape: settle bytes storage/view conversions across value-union construction, arguments, returns and extraction together, rather than widen one consumer. The exact value-union match body remains compile coverage in `tests/cases/match/narrowed_subscript`; its pointer-union sibling supplies native/CPython execution coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A union with a `BytesView` member does not lower its `isinstance` arm.** [`bytesview-union-member-rejects`] `def f(u: bytes | BytesView)` / `Span[readonly[UInt8]] | BytesView` with `if isinstance(u, BytesView):` rejects at `stmt.if:cond.call`, where the same shape over `str | StrView` lowers. The widened union member class (`_ptr_union_member_wide`, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) admits `str`, `bytes`, containers, value tuples and `Span` and has no row for the bytes view, so the isinstance narrowing over such a union never reaches the variant machinery. The signature itself renders (`tests/cases/bytes/distinct_spelling_union`, the view pair). Since 2026-09-10 the pair spells distinct alternatives (`::tpy::BytesView` is its own type), so admitting the view is a member-class row, not a spelling question; `tests/cases/bytes/error_bytesview_union_isinstance` pins the reject. Found 2026-09-10 converting the duplicate-spelling error case.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Two union operands of ONE type reject unless they were borrowed the same way.** [`ref-union-loop-var-vs-borrow-compare`]
  A union at a borrow position compares (`union/reference_union_borrow_eq`), but one union type has three C++ renders and none converts to another, so a pair drawn from two of them rejects at `binop.shape.==` although both operands are spelled `Pet` in the source. The three: the STORAGE element a `for e in xs` / comprehension variable binds (`::tpy::Union<Cat, Dog>`), the mutable borrow (`::tpy::Union<Cat*, Dog*>`), and the const-pointee read borrow (`::tpy::Union<const Cat*, const Dog*>`, taken by a `readonly[...]` annotation, by a param the callable only discriminates, and by a local lifted out of a const container). So `[e == u for e in xs]` rejects (at `expr.list_comp`). The two const-side pairs this entry also listed -- `def f(a: readonly[Pet], b: Pet): return a == b` and `def f(xs: list[Pet], u: Pet): a = xs[0]; return a == u` -- now compile: a non-mutating union parameter borrows const pointees, so the annotated and the inferred slot are one render and the const local is that render too. What is left is the STORAGE side. `_ptr_union_compare_pair` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) requires the two renders to agree rather than emit a compare that does not build; before the borrow form was its own type every one of these rejected at the same tag, so nothing regressed -- but CPython runs all three. Fix shape: lift the storage side at the compare, the way an argument at a borrow slot lifts it (`to_const_ptr_variant`) -- a form decision, not a gate widening. `tests/cases/union/reference_union_borrow_eq` cites this entry and takes two parameters in its comprehension section for that reason; its `readonly mixed` and `const local` sections pin the two pairs that now compile. Found landing the borrow-form union type 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A union whose members are all `Ptr[T]` reaches codegen at one position only.** [`ptr-member-union-unreachable`]
  `type PtrPet = Ptr[Dog] | Ptr[Cat]` renders its alias and a parameter signature (`const ::tpy::Union<Cat*, Dog*>&`) and nothing else: the call that would build the argument rejects at `call.arg_shape.union`, an annotated local at `decl.slot_type`, a return at `return.slot_type`, a field at `ctor.mil_field.union.name`, a container literal at `expr.container_literal`, a compare at `binop.shape.==` (`_eligible_value_union` excludes `Ptr` members, and `_eligible_ptr_union_wide` wants non-value members), and `isinstance(u, Ptr[Dog])` at "Generic type 'Ptr' cannot be used as a value". Identical on `cba2f6df73` and after the borrow-form type landed, so nothing regressed -- but every one of these runs in CPython. **What this entry protects**: such a union is the SAME C++ type as any other union's borrow form -- `::tpy::Union` over a pointer alternative pack -- at every position, owning ones included, because its members are already borrowed references; the consequence is that when it does compare it compares POINTEES, not addresses. It needs no carve-out in the renderer to get there: the alternatives carry the fact. That was decided with the borrow-form type (analysis fork 2.4 answer (i)) and must not be silently re-decided when these gaps close. `tests/cases/union/ptr_member_union_spelling` pins the two spellings that do render. Probes `/tmp/agents/ptrunion/ptrmix/`. Found probing the all-`Ptr` route for the borrow-form union type 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `bytearray` member keeps a union element from being read out of a container at all.** [`bytearray-union-element-read-rejects`]
  `a = xs[0]` with `xs: list[bytearray | Int32]` rejects at `stmt.var_decl:subscript.elem.union`, with no narrowing or comparison involved; the same read over `list[list[Int32] | Int32]` or `list[Dog | Int32 | float]` lowers and runs. So the union element path is reachable for record, container and scalar members and blocked by the `bytearray` member specifically. CPython runs it. Same `bytearray`-in-a-union family as `BUGS.md#bytes-value-union-boundary-rejects`, and the fix should settle the two together rather than widen one consumer. The third member of the family -- the whole-union deep-const argument bridge, which skipped its wrap because the same narrow member class excluded a zero-type-arg `bytearray` -- is fixed: that consumer now keys on the wide class. Repro `/tmp/agents/ptrunion/cell2.py`. Found spelling the borrowed-value-members section for the borrow-form union compare 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) Any protocol bound satisfies a `Copyable` requirement, so the bound check accepts a non-copyable type.** [`marker-bound-satisfies-copyable`] `def inner[T: Copyable](v: T)` called from `def outer[T: Stringable](v: T): return inner(v)` is accepted, and so is the end-to-end program that instantiates `outer` at a non-copyable class (a `__del__`, which deletes the generated copy ctor) with `__str__`. `protocols.py` correctly refuses an UNBOUND type param (pinned by `tests/cases/generics/error_copyable_marker_unbound_t`), but when the param HAS a protocol-typed bound the check delegates to that bound, and the `Copyable` marker arm (`tpyc/sema/protocols.py:437`) asks `not is_type_non_copyable(<the protocol type>)` -- False for any protocol, so the negation reports conformance. Today the owning-slot copy contract (`tpyc/sema/own_copy.py`) still catches the program with a located error, so the consequence is a bound that does not mean what it says rather than a build failure; it becomes a libstdc++-spew class for any future rule that leans on the bound check alone. Fix shape: the marker arm must ask whether the BOUND is (or extends) `Copyable`, not whether the bound type is copyable. Probes `/tmp/agents/bound/p14_any_bound_body.py` and `p15_hole_e2e.py`. Found measuring the explicit-bound fork for the generic copy contract 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Sibling of the unslugged bare-annotation entry further down (`x: Box[Rc[Int32]]` is unchecked for the same reason) but a different site: the base list is resolved in `tpyc/sema/registration.py`, which classifies parents without consulting `record_info.type_param_bounds`. Fix shape: validate a parent's substituted type args against the base's bounds where the parents are classified, mirroring the construction-site check. Probe `/tmp/agents/bound/p7_record_base_decl.py`. Found measuring the explicit-bound fork for the generic copy contract 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) `copy()` of a non-copyable type is not diagnosed, in a generic body or a monomorphic one.** [`copy-call-of-noncopyable-undiagnosed`] `xs.append(copy(v))` with `v: Pinned` (non-copyable: it defines `__del__`) passes sema and fails the C++ build with `use of deleted function 'Pinned::Pinned(const Pinned&)'` at `xs.push_back(::tpyapp::Pinned(v))`; the generic twin `xs.append(copy(v))` at an open `T` instantiated at `Pinned` fails identically at `xs.push_back(T(v))`. Same class as the `heapq` entry below, whose prescribed fix (add `T: Copyable` bounds) does not cover the monomorphic half. Fix shape: check copy-constructibility at the `copy()` call itself, so the hatch reports what it cannot do. Probes `/tmp/agents/bound/p17_copy_nomove.py` and `p18_copy_nomove_twin.py`. Found measuring the explicit-bound fork for the generic copy contract 2026-09-09. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

The genexpr's element type never carries `ReadonlyType`: `_resolve_comp_iterable` (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py:3552`) strips the container's outer readonly (`inner = unwrap_readonly(iterable_type)`) before asking for the element type, so `yield_borrow_slot_cpp` spells the yield slot `val_or_ref<Box>` (holding a `Box*`) while the lambda drives the source's `const_iterator` and `*__beg++` is a `const Box&`. The consumer half already reads the const off the source root -- the loop var binds `const auto&` via `gen.const_loop_var` -- so only the slot disagrees. The def-generator twin compiles, because its `Iterator[readonly[Box]]` annotation carries the readonly to the slot, which then spells `val_or_ref<const Box>` (`tests/cases/generators/gen_varargs_param`'s `points`); the leak is on the genexpr path, where no annotation restates the element type. - **[HIGH small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) A container-element union name at a MUTABLE union parameter slot does not compile.** [`storage-union-element-at-mutable-borrow-slot`]

No lowering arm wires `to_ptr_variant()` onto a storage-bound container-element name reaching a pointer-variant slot -- the CONST half of the same shape works, because the const wrap asks how the source is bound and answers `to_const_ptr_variant`. Two things are wrong at once and a fix has to settle both: the missing mutable lift, and the element binding itself -- mutation through a loop element is not credited to the container, so `xs` binds `const std::vector<...>&` and no mutable borrow of `e` exists to take. CPython runs it. Pre-existing: `231114b18e` renders the same signature and the same bare argument. No case in the corpus reaches it. Repro `/tmp/agents/constptr/storage_src.py`. Found probing the mutable-slot residual of the union const-pointee flip 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Since a non-mutating union parameter borrows const pointees, BOTH signatures are `::tpy::Union<const A*, const B*>` -- the call would compile and mutate nothing. The readonly rule reads the ANNOTATION, not the rendered form, so it cannot see that the callee's inferred verdict already gives the guarantee the annotation asks for. CPython runs it. `tests/cases/union/error_union_readonly_param_pass` and `error_union_readonly_method_param_pass` pin today's rejection, so lifting it changes two committed diagnostics and is a DESIGN decision, not a cleanup: the rule would have to consult the callee's const verdict (available only after Phase-2) at an argument check that runs earlier. `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` records it as a limitation. Found closing the union const-pointee flip 2026-09-10.

Cell(tpy::BytesView)`). - **[LOW small] (silent generated-code change from an unrelated fact) Reach analysis walks every `__dict__` a statement can reach, so a new `FunctionInfo` field holding types changes the emitted includes.** [`reach-walk-picks-up-any-functioninfo-type-field`] `_iter_typed_children` (`tpyc/sema/reach_analysis.py`) recurses into any object with a `__dict__` reachable from a statement node -- including a call's `resolved_function_info` -- and treats every `TpyType` it finds as a module the generated code references. Adding the owning-slot copy obligations to `FunctionInfo` (types of the SLOTS a callee's body stores into, a diagnostics-only fact) therefore added four transitive includes to `tests/cases/generics/generic_arg_temp_instantiated_slot`'s header until the two field names were listed in the walk's skip set beside `enum_member_of`. The skip list is a denylist: the next field to hold a type is picked up silently, and only a snapshot diff says so. Fix direction: walk an explicit allowlist of the fields whose types the generated code actually names, so a new field is invisible until it opts in. Found while landing the per-instantiation owning-slot copy verdict 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container FIELD read at a generic callee's composite `list[T]` slot rejects.** [`generic-composite-slot-field-arg`] `has_item(self.labels, k)` with `self.labels: list[str]` and `def has_item[T](xs: list[T], v: T)` rejects at `call.generic_arg_shape`, while the same read bound to a local first (`xs = self.labels; has_item(xs, k)`) lowers and renders the member read bare. The generic family's pass-through rows for a substituted composite slot (`_container_pass_through_arg`) are NAME-only; the still-OPEN composite slot already has its field twin (`call.generic_open_slot_field_composite`), so only the substituted side is missing the row. `tests/cases/generics/generic_slot_view_form_positions` binds the local for exactly this reason. Found while covering the positions for the view-at-a-generic-slot fix 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) An `Own[T]` CONSTRUCTOR parameter whose payload is `@nomove` does not compile.** [`own-nomove-ctor-param-cpp-error`] `def __init__(self, v: Own[Pinned])` storing `self.val = v` emits the member init `val(std::move(v))`, which needs the move constructor `@nomove` deletes; the toolchain reports it at the generated line, with no TPy location. This is a `@nomove` gap, not a generic one: the same program fails identically at `Holder[Pinned]` (`explicit Holder(::tpy::own_param_t<T> v) : val(std::move(v)) {}`) and at a hand-written `TwinHolder` whose field is a plain `Pinned` (`inline TwinHolder::TwinHolder(Pinned&& v) : val(std::move(v)) {}`). Fix: sema rejects `Own[@nomove]` at a constructor parameter that initializes a field (or the field init itself) with a located message, or the member init constructs in place rather than moving. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/generic/p4_own_ctor.py`. Found while auditing the generic-form class 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A VIEW or an ENUM value at a generic slot is refused by the lowering.** [`generic-slot-view-enum-arg-rejects`] `echo(bv)` with `def echo[T](v: T) -> T` and `bv: BytesView` rejects at `call.generic_arg_slot`, and `Cell(bv)` at `stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type`; an enum member at the same free-function slot (`has_item(xs, k)` with `k = Color.RED`) rejects at `call.generic_arg_slot` too, though the enum reaches a generic RECORD's slot fine. The generic argument rows admit scalars, `str`, records, containers, tuples and `None`; the other value-type families -- the views (`BytesView`, `Span`, the dict views), `Range`, the slices, and enums at a free-function slot -- match no row and fall through to the reject. Distinct from the str/bytes view at a generic slot, which the lowering does admit and now materializes an owned temp for (`tests/cases/generics/generic_slot_view_form_positions`): here nothing is emitted at all. Both the C++ obstacle (the runtime's value-type trait was made to match the registry, 2026-09-08) and the str/bytes admission are gone, so what is left for THESE families -- the borrowing views with no owned counterpart, `Range`, the slices, and enums at a free-function slot -- is admission rows: they need no materialize, only a bare pass-through row. `tests/cases/generics/generic_value_form_instantiation` pins the shapes that do lower and names this entry for the one that does not. Found while pinning the value-form instantiation 2026-09-08.


- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A BORROW-returning call at a generic FREE function's `T` slot is refused, where the same argument at a generic RECORD METHOD's `T` slot binds bare.** [`generic-free-call-borrow-return-arg-rejects`] `f(h.borrow())` with `def f[T](v: T) -> None` and `Holder.borrow() -> Cell` (a `T&`-returning getter) fails at `expr.call:call.generic_arg_slot`, reported on the call line; `b.m(h.borrow())` with `class Box[T]` and `def m(self, v: T)` compiles and renders the bare bind `b.m(h.borrow());`, which aliases the holder's field exactly as CPython does. So this is not a temp-versus-no-temp difference between the seams -- neither builds a temp -- but a missing ADMISSION row at the free-call seam: its prologue (`_pre_generic_slot_family`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) admits a CALL at a substituted non-value `TypeParamRef` slot only when `is_rvalue_source` holds, and a borrow-returning getter is not one. The method and marker ladders carry the row this needs (`borrow_ret_record_marker` -- a `T&`-returning F1-record call at a plain record ref slot binds in place, no temp, no copy); the generic free-call ladder has no analogue. Fix direction: mirror that row in the generic-plain family, and pin it with a case that MUTATES the holder and prints through both handles, so the bare bind is proved to alias rather than copy. The reject itself is bound-independent -- the shapes above use an unbounded `Box[T]` / `f[T]` -- but a mutation-OBSERVING pin needs a bounded `T` (an unbounded one cannot touch a member), which is why the happy case spells `Bumper[T: Bump]`. Neighbouring entry for the other source shapes refused at the same slot: `generic-slot-view-enum-arg-rejects`. Pre-existing (identical on `4346504539`); found by review probes while folding the three generic seams into one verdict 2026-09-09. Pinned by `tests/cases/generics/error_generic_free_call_borrow_arg`, whose happy twin `tests/cases/generics/generic_method_borrow_ret_arg` runs the method seam's accepted form.

- **[LOW small] (spurious diagnostic) A generic method returning its own `T` PARAMETER warns about a temporary when the argument is a borrow.** [`generic-return-through-param-spurious-temporary-warning`] `def bump_it(self, v: T) -> T: v.bump(); return v` on `class Bumper[T: Bump]`, called as `got = b.bump_it(h.borrow())` where `Holder.borrow() -> Cell` returns a `T&` alias of a live field, warns *Result borrows from temporary argument 'v'; the temporary is destroyed at end-of-statement* on the binding line. The argument is not a temporary: it aliases the holder's own cell, which outlives the statement, so the borrow the result carries is sound and the warning is noise on valid code. The same call at STATEMENT position (result discarded) warns nothing, so the verdict is taken at the binding. Fix direction: the temporary-argument check should ask whether the argument expression is a temporary (a borrow-returning call is not) rather than treating every call-shaped argument as one. Pre-existing; re-probed 2026-09-09 (`/tmp/agents/sdb2/t3.py`). This is why `tests/cases/generics/generic_method_borrow_ret_arg` keeps its method `-> None` and observes the alias through the mutation instead of through the returned handle.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Reassigning a `T`-typed parameter inside a generic body is rejected where the monomorphic twin is accepted.** [`generic-param-reassign-rejected`] `def bump[T](v: T) -> T: v = v` (any reassignment of the parameter) fails with *Cannot reassign parameter 'v' of type 'T'; assign to a new local variable instead*, while `def bump_concrete(v: Float32)` reassigning its parameter compiles and runs; CPython accepts both. The guard stands in for the parameter's C++ form: `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` is a mutable `T&` at a reference-type instantiation, where a reassignment would write through the caller's object rather than rebind a local. It fires on every instantiation, including the value-typed ones whose slot is `const T&` and where a local copy is exactly what a concrete parameter already gets. Fix: decide it per instantiation (or emit the same local-copy the concrete path emits for a `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` type) instead of refusing on the open parameter. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/generic/p5_float32_mutate.py` and `_twin.py`. Found while auditing the generic-form class 2026-09-08. The same `_check_nonvalue_rebinding` guard rejects a range target of open type `T`: `def count[T: AnyFixedInt](stop: T)` with `for i in range(stop): i = 10` fails with `Cannot reassign loop variable 'i' of type 'T'`; CPython runs all three iterations at `stop=3`. An attempted `Int32(stop)` bound also rejects, at `call.type_ctor.scalar_arg`; its separate witness is `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_generic_cast.py` and the full-fixture diagnostic is `range-case-frontend-9.log`. The passing range regression instead takes `values: list[T]` and uses the concrete integer bound `len(values)`, with parameter mutation observed by the caller; this does not admit an open-`T` counter. Verified in `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_generic_rebind.py` (`range-generic-rebind-frontend.log`, `range-generic-rebind-cpy.log`); the shared sema guard is unchanged at session base.


- **[LOW small] (test-harness parity gap) `isinstance(x, Int32)` answers differently under the CPython stubs.** [`isinstance-int32-cpy-stub-subclass`] `lib/cpy/tpy`'s `Int32` is an `int` SUBCLASS, so a plain literal reaching an `Int32 | str` slot is not an `Int32` instance under CPython (`isinstance(3, Int32)` is False) while TPy, whose default int IS `Int32`, answers True. A four-line probe with no other construct shows it. Any case that branches on `isinstance(x, Int32)` with a literal source therefore prints differently on the cpy phase; the `tpy.dispatch` runtime in `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py` sidesteps it for the common shape (a plain `int` argument matches any fixed-int annotation it fits), leaving user-written `isinstance` checks and one residual dispatcher shape -- two same-arity fixed-int variants that both fit a literal go to the first declared under CPython where the compiler picks the narrowest; the shape became reachable when the value-union arg temp in an `and` right operand started lowering (2026-09-07). Fix in the stub layer: make the stub's `int` the default fixed-int type for `isinstance` (or map `isinstance(x, Int32)` to an `int` test when the case's default_int is Int32), not in the compiler. Found while fixing the conditional-operand argument copy.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `@nomove` rvalue at the FIRST comparator of a chained comparison rejects.** [`nomove-first-comparator-chained-compare`] `a < take(Pinned(11)) < 99` with `take(p: Pinned) -> Int32` and `Pinned` `@nomove` rejects at `call.arg_shape.optional`: pair 0 of a chained compare lowers with no flush right, so the optional-pointer constructor face has nowhere to hoist its temp, while the same call as an `and` operand or at the second comparator lowers (those positions carry a conditional region). Pinned as the reason the `@nomove` warn case's inverse uses an `and` left operand. Fix: give the first comparator of a chain the same flush right the later comparators have (their region machinery), keyed on the position, not the operator. Found while fixing the conditional-operand argument copy.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An UNSPELLED argument temporary in a conditionally evaluated operand is refused instead of deferred.** [`cond-operand-unspelled-arg-temp-rejects`] `return b or use(Src(7))` with `use(r: Reader)` a structural-protocol slot rejects at `argtemp.cond_defer`; so do the sibling rows that declare their temporary `auto` on purpose -- the container-literal / record-rvalue / range marker-protocol arms, the coroutine-factory, str-literal, iterator-rvalue and generator-expression protocol temps, and the generator-factory reference slot (eight rows in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`; two further rows there spell a type but record no movability -- a protocol-argument spec and a `@dynamic` adapter spelling, neither a type whose movability can be asked -- and reject the same way). The temporary has to be un-spelled so the protocol's concept deduces the concrete type, and the deferred form needs a spelling (`std::optional<T>` cannot name `auto`), so the conditional-operand gate refuses rather than hoist the build ahead of the guard -- which is what it did before 2026-09-07, running the constructor in a branch CPython skips. Binding the value to a local ahead of the expression compiles. Closing it needs the deduced type reachable at lowering for those rows (the concrete init type rather than the protocol slot), not a change to the gate. Pinned by `tests/cases/operators/error_cond_operand_protocol_arg`. Filed while fixing the eager owned-argument copy 2026-09-07.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code) Binding the result of a generic method whose readonly-ness was INFERRED emits a non-const local against a const-qualified return.** [`generic-method-inferred-readonly-return-binding`] `class Box[T]` with `def keep(self, v: T) -> T: return v` -- no `@readonly` annotation, so Phase 2 infers it -- called at a reference-typed instantiation and bound to a caller local (`got = b.keep(c)`) emits `Cell& got = b.keep(c);` against the emitted `::tpy::val_or_cref_t<T> keep(const T& v) const`, and g++ rejects it: *binding reference of type 'Cell&' to 'const Cell' discards qualifiers*. The front end accepts the program; the failure names a generated line. Cause: at the CALLER's lowering the call node's `resolved_function_info.is_readonly` is still the pre-Phase-2 value (False), so the local is spelled mutable. `_sync_inferred_const` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) copies the inferred verdict back onto the callee's own `TpyFunction` -- which is what makes the SIGNATURE const -- but nothing re-syncs a call site's cached `FunctionInfo` for a generic instantiation; the non-generic twin (`def keep(self, v: Cell) -> Cell`) reads True and binds a const local. **Second shape, same seam:** with an explicit `@readonly` the local binds const correctly, and then a MUTATION through it (`got.n = 42`) is not diagnosed by TPy at all -- it surfaces as *assignment of member 'Cell::n' in read-only object* from the C++ compiler, in the non-generic twin too, so the readonly enforcement gap at a readonly-bound local is independent of genericity. Fix direction: re-ask (or re-sync) the readonly verdict where the call site spells the binding, and give the bound local's mutation a located TPy diagnostic. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/sdtail/probe1.py` (generic, inferred), `probe6.py` (non-generic control), `probe5.py` (explicit `@readonly`); pre-existing on `4346504539`. Found by the tail review of the generic-seam fold 2026-09-09, while pinning why `tests/cases/generics/generic_method_borrow_ret_arg` cannot bind the method's return.

- **[MED small] (silent copy, no diagnostic) A borrow-returning call at a GENERIC generator's YIELD slot is not diagnosed, and the monomorphic twin does not compile at all.** [`generic-own-slot-borrow-call-unwarned`] `def stream[T](h: GHolder[T]) -> Iterator[T]: yield h.borrow()` copies the payload into the yield slot with no diagnostic -- mutating the source while the yielded value is live prints the pre-mutation value, where CPython prints the mutation. Root: `yield_uses_borrow_slot` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) excludes a `TypeParamRef` element from the borrow slot, so the yield is a copying slot that the owning-slot borrowed-source check (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py`, the `isinstance(expected, OwnType)` arm) never sees; the exclusion is justified in its docstring on RENDERING grounds (avoiding a double `val_or_ref` wrap), not on ownership. The concrete twin `def stream_twin(h: Twin) -> Iterator[Cell]: yield h.borrow()` cannot be used to compare: it rejects at lowering with `res.yield_type`, so this shape is a generic-equals-twin divergence in BOTH directions. **Second witness of the same asymmetry** (2026-09-08): a borrow-returning getter feeding an owning CONSTRUCTOR slot compiles when the payload is an open `T` (the shape `tests/cases/generics/warn_generic_own_slot_borrow_call`'s `GBox.dup` pins) and is refused at lowering with `method.ret_type` when the same body spells `Cell` directly -- which is why that section has no twin beside it. The four concrete spellings measured (`sink(t.borrow())` at an `Own[Cell]` param, the same bound to a local, `Twin(t.borrow())` at a ctor slot, `CBox(self.get())` with an `@auto_readonly` getter) all reject; a free borrow-returning call rejects as `call.ret_type.record_borrow`. The sibling owning slots -- container insert, `Own[T]` parameter, `Own[T]` return -- were closed 2026-09-08 (the entry originally covered all four); pinned by `tests/cases/generics/warn_generic_own_slot_borrow_call`, which omits a yield section for exactly this reason. Re-measured 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, unlocated) Awaiting a GENERIC method of a GENERIC class spells the sub-coroutine frame with only ONE of its two template arguments.** [`generic-class-generic-async-method-template-args`] `class Box[T]` with `async def with_label[U](self, u: U) -> Int32` emits `template <typename T, typename U> struct __coro_Box_with_label`, but the awaiting frame declares its slot as `std::optional<__coro_Box_with_label<int32_t>>` -- the class parameter's argument only -- and g++ rejects it with `wrong number of template arguments (1, should be 2)`, followed by cascading `'<expression error>' in namespace 'std'` and undeclared-slot errors in the .cpp. Unlocated: the front end accepts the program and the failure names a generated line. **The local-bind framing this was first reported under is refuted**: both spellings fail identically and neither is rejected at sema -- binding the coroutine to a local first (`c = b.with_label[Int32](7); await c`) emits the bad slot as `c`, and the inline `await b.with_label[Int32](7)` emits the same bad slot as `__sub_0` (measured 2026-09-08, probes `/tmp/agents/generic4/async_method_probe.py` and `async_method_inline.py`). Site: the sub-struct spelling in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py` builds the frame type from the OWNER's type args and drops the method's own. Distinct from the inherited generic-async entry above (that one is about an ancestor's args being unbound and rejects cleanly at sema; this one is a method's own params being dropped and does not reject at all). Found by the tail review of the unit-4 closing fix 2026-09-08.

- **[HIGH small] (silent copy, no diagnostic) A call through an `Fn`/`Callable` VALUE bound to a BORROW-returning function copies at every owning slot with no diagnostic.** [`callable-value-borrow-return-copies-unwarned`] With `def identity(c: Cell) -> Cell: return c` and `f: Fn[[Cell], Cell]`, both `out.append(f(c))` and `return f(c)` at an `Own[Cell]` copy the payload: TPy prints `1` where CPython prints `99` after the source is mutated past the boundary, and no warning fires at either slot (probes `/tmp/agents/tail/fn_alias_probe.py` and `fn_alias_return_probe.py`, measured 2026-09-08 against master `2bd8dec8b6` as well as the fix branch -- pre-existing, unchanged). The same call spelled directly (`out.append(identity(c))`) DOES warn, so the divergence is the callable-value indirection, not the callee. Cause: the synthetic `FunctionInfo` that `analyze_callable_value_call` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) builds carries the `Fn` type's declared return, but every reader treats the callee as opaque -- `is_rvalue_source` (`tpyc/value_category.py`) has no registry entry to consult and falls through to its rvalue default, so `returns_borrow` says no and the owning-slot check never runs. Fix direction: the declared return on that synthetic FI carries the borrow fact as faithfully as a declared function's does, so `returns_borrow` should read it the same way -- but an `Fn` whose declared return is a reference type then borrows at EVERY owning slot in the corpus, so the radius must be measured (`rpytest --no-exec`) before the arm lands; it is its own unit. Note the interaction with the twin rule: the GENERIC leg `Fn[[T], K]` must reach the same verdict as its monomorphic twin, which is why the opposite classification is currently spelled as an explicit `is_callable_value` exclusion rather than left to fall out. Found by the tail review of the unit-4 fix round 2026-09-08.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) A generic body cannot return its own `T | None` parameter, because the RETURN position is still committed to `T*`.** [`generic-optional-return-committed-to-pointer`] `def echo[T](o: T | None) -> T | None: return o` compiles the template but fails at a value-typed instantiation: the parameter is `::tpy::opt_param_t<T>` (`std::optional<int32_t>` at `Int32`) while the return is `T*`, so g++ reports *cannot convert `std::optional<int>` to `int*` in return* inside the instantiation, with no TPy source location. The monomorphic twin `def echo(o: Int32 | None) -> Int32 | None` compiles and runs. The parameter form is now decided per instantiation (`opt_param_t<T>`), but the return keeps `force_pointer_repr` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) so a `T | None` return can alias the field it reads (`return self._val` renders `optional_to_ptr(this->_val)`, a pointer INTO the record) -- an optional return would copy there. Closing it means the return taking a trait of its own (`std::optional<T>` at a value T, `T*` at a reference one, with a matching lift at the field read) and the receiver local taking the natural substituted form, which retires `force_pointer_repr` entirely -- the flag's own docstring names conditional-ABI templates as the exit. The same shape was already ill-formed before the parameter changed (the call site built the value form against a `T*` slot), so this is the residue of that fix, not a regression. Found while making the `T | None` parameter a runtime trait 2026-09-08.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic hygiene) A return-type mismatch on a coroutine value prints the same type on both sides.** [`coro-return-mismatch-prints-same-type`] `def make(c: Cell) -> asyncio.Cancellable[bool]: return probe_async(c)` reports `Type mismatch in return value: expected Cancellable[bool], got Cancellable[bool]`, which tells the reader nothing -- the two types differ in something the `__str__` does not render (the coroutine struct's identity behind the `Cancellable[T]` wrap). Dropping the annotation reports `expected None, got Cancellable[bool]`, so the check itself fires correctly; only the rendering collapses. Whatever the real distinction is, the message has to name it (or the check has to accept the return). Found 2026-09-08 probing whether an async frame holding a borrowed param can escape its caller -- this reject is one of the two things that stop it, so it is load-bearing for the resumable-frame borrow family above. Repro `/tmp/agents/gu3/c9_escape3.py`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A value-repr `Int32 | None` local passed to a generic `T | None` slot rejects.** [`optional-value-local-at-generic-slot`] `none_int: Int32 | None = None` then `probe_gen(none_int)` on `def probe_gen[T](val: T | None) -> bool` rejects at `stmt.expr_stmt:call.generic_arg_shape`, where the reference-typed twin (a `Cell | None` local into the same slot) lowers. A bare int LITERAL at the same slot (`probe_gen(2)`) rejects the same way, where a binop of the same type (`probe_gen(n + 1)`) and an explicit `Int32(2)` both lower. The generic call's argument gate (`_generic_plain_arg_ok`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) enumerates argument shapes against a bare `TypeParamRef` slot and has no row for an `Optional[TypeParamRef]` one, so the shape that would now render as a bare pass-through (both sides are `std::optional<Int32>` after the parameter-form fix) is refused before it gets there. Pre-existing: reproduces unchanged on the branch base with the old pointer parameter form. Repros `/tmp/agents/gu3/b6_optlocal.py` (the local) and the `probe_gen(2)` line of `tests/cases/generics/optional_param_trait_form` (the literal, which the case spells `Int32(2)` for that reason). Found while making the `T | None` parameter a runtime trait 2026-09-08.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Every body shape over a `ValueType`-bounded `T | None` PARAMETER is unlowered.** [`bounded-optional-param-unrouted`] On `class BoundedBox[T: ValueType]`, `def probe(self, val: T | None) -> bool: return val is not None` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.is not.tparam`, `def echo(self, val: T | None) -> T | None: return val` at `stmt.return:name.optval_read`, and `def __init__(self, val: T | None): self._val = val` at `ctor.mil_field.optional.name`. A bounded `T` is a value at every instantiation, so the slot is the plain `std::optional<T>` the concrete twin uses and every one of these renders exists for the concrete inner -- the value-optional predicate family (`_value_opt_scalar` and siblings, `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) enumerates concrete inners and never admits a bounded `TypeParamRef`. The bounded RETURN position lowers (`tests/cases/generics/generic_optional_value_bound`); only the parameter is blocked. Pre-existing: reproduces unchanged on the branch base. Repro `/tmp/agents/gu3/b7_bounded.py`. Found while making the unbounded `T | None` parameter a runtime trait 2026-09-08.

- **[HIGH small] (silent CPython divergence) `Any == Any` across two different contained types is always False.** [`any-eq-compares-typeid-not-value`] `a: Any = Int32(1)` and `b: Any = Float64(1.0)` compare False where CPython prints True (`1 == 1.0`), with no diagnostic. `tpy::any_eq` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/any.hpp`) answers False on a typeid mismatch, and `docs/ANY_TYPE_DESIGN.md` records that as a design decision -- but it is the same question the value union settled the other way (a value union now compares by value because it renders `::tpy::Union`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/union_type.hpp`, whose operators own the rule), so the two type-erased forms disagree. Fix shape: `any_eq`'s cross-type leg dispatches to the same per-alternative-pair leaf the union uses (`tpy::detail::py_eq`, called by `::tpy::Union`'s `operator==`), and `docs/ANY_TYPE_DESIGN.md` drops the "type-mismatch False" clause; ordering on `Any` needs the same pass. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq/s31_any_eq.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) An `int` compared against a `Float64` is compared as a double, so a value beyond 2**53 compares equal to a float it differs from.** [`int-float-compare-rounds-bigint`] `big: int = 9007199254740993` against `f: Float64 = 9007199254740992.0` prints True where CPython prints False: the compare renders `(static_cast<double>(big) == f)`, which rounds the arbitrary-precision side to the nearest double before comparing. No diagnostic. Not a union bug -- the monomorphic `int`-vs-`Float64` compare has it -- but the value-union leaf is defined as the twin's answer and so inherits it (`tpy::detail::py_eq`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/value_compare.hpp`, which `::tpy::Union`'s operators visit down to), which is why fixing it means fixing both together: CPython compares exactly, by decomposing the float. Also affects the ordering operators. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq/s35_mixed_sign_and_exact.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) An `int` compared against a `UInt32` does not compile.** [`bigint-vs-uint32-compare-ill-formed`] `def eq(a: int, b: UInt32) -> bool: return a == b` renders `(a == ::tpy::BigInt(b))`, and `BigInt(uint32_t)` is ambiguous: `BigInt(int32_t)`, `BigInt(int64_t)` and `BigInt(uint64_t)` are all integral conversions of equal rank, so the toolchain reports the error at the generated line with no TPy location. The sibling widths are fine (`UInt8`/`UInt16` promote to `int32_t`, `UInt64` matches exactly), so only the 32-bit unsigned spelling is affected -- on either side, and for the ordering operators too. Fix: the BigInt wrap spells the widened form (`::tpy::BigInt(static_cast<uint64_t>(b))`), which is what the value-union leaf already does for the same pair (`tpy::detail::vc_to_bigint`, `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/value_compare.hpp`). Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/twins.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) A container or recursive-alias compare over a record that defines no `__eq__` fails in the C++ toolchain with no TPy diagnostic.** [`container-compare-record-without-eq`] `def eqd(a: dict[str, Plain], b: dict[str, Plain]) -> bool: return a == b` with `Plain` defining no `__eq__`, and `def cmp(a: list[Expr], b: list[Expr])` over `type Expr = Lit | BinOp` with neither record defining one, both fail at the generated line: sema admits the container pair (the element's equality is never required) and the emit reaches a comparison the element type does not have. CPython runs both -- `dict.__eq__` and `list.__eq__` fall back to identity, so `eqd(a, a)` is True and `cmp(xs, ys)` is False for distinct objects -- so this is a rejects-valid divergence, just a loud one. The message depends on the shape: a union alternative pair reaches a named `static_assert` inside the leaf ("comparing two values of one TPy type that defines no equality") -- a REFERENCE union's container element too, since its storage form is `::tpy::Union` as well -- while a plain record element reaches `no match for operator==` at the container's own line. Both are unlocated toolchain errors. Fix: sema requires the element type to conform to `Equatable` at a container/wrapper compare and says so with a TPy location, or the identity fallback is emitted. Probes `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/r1/vu_dict2.py` and `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/r1/probe3/main.py`. Cannot be pinned as a case (an `error_` case needs a front-end diagnostic; this one is a C++ error). Found by the review of the value-union equality fix 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, unlocated) A NON-generic recursive alias with a fixed-width numeric member renders the TPy type name into C++.** [`nongeneric-alias-member-spelling`] `type V = Int32 | Float64 | list[V]` emits `using variant_type = std::variant<Float64, int32_t, std::vector<V>>;` -- `Float64` is a TPy name with no C++ declaration, so the header does not compile ("'Float64' was not declared in this scope"), unlocated. The same alias spelled with `int | float` builds, and the signature of a function taking `list[V]` spells the members correctly AND in a different order (`std::variant<int32_t, double, std::vector<V>>`), so the wrapper struct's member rendering and the signature's have drifted apart -- two renders of one type that must agree. Independent of the equality work: `git show master:tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py` differs from the current `_gen_recursive_union_struct` only in the `operator==` lines. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/r1/nongen_alias.py` with the `Int32 | Float64` leaf. Found by the review of the value-union equality fix 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A value union has no equality at the TYPE level, so every consumer that asks for one rejects.** [`value-union-no-equatable-conformance`] Sema resolves no `__eq__` for a `UnionType` (`resolve_binop`, `tpyc/sema/operators.py`) and gives it neither `Equatable` nor `Hashable` conformance (`classify_protocol_conformance`, `tpyc/sema/protocols.py`), so six ordinary Python shapes are refused although the same-type union compare itself works: a union against one of its own members (`u == 1`, `binop.shape.==`), a direct `tuple[union, ...]` compare (`binop.shape.==`), `needle in xs` / `xs.count` / `xs.index` over `list[union]` ("requires element type ... to conform to 'Equatable'"), a union as a dict KEY or set element ("not hashable"), and `sorted` / `min` / `max` over `list[union]` ("does not satisfy 'Comparable'"). Every one of them runs in CPython. The runtime answers already exist -- `::tpy::Union`'s own operators (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/union_type.hpp`) and `::tpy::Union`'s (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/ptr_union.hpp`) are what the same-type compare reaches at a storage and a borrow position respectively -- so this is conformance plumbing plus a hash that agrees with the new equality, i.e. a feature (`/tpy-add-feature`), not a fix. A union of RECORDS used to be listed here too; it compares now that the borrow form is its own type (`tests/cases/union/reference_union_borrow_eq`), and the conformance is still what the six shapes above wait on. The missing conformance also makes the union path LOOSER than its twin in one direction: ordering two members that define no ordering (`a < b` on `Fixed | Zone`, both `@dataclass(frozen=True)` ValueType records) compiles and raises `TypeError` at runtime, which is CPython's answer, while the monomorphic `Fixed < Fixed` is a located sema error ("Comparison '<' on 'Fixed': no '__lt__' method defined"). A `Comparable` check at the union compare is where both would agree; `tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq` pins the runtime raise as the current behaviour. Probes `/tmp/agents/unioneq/s04,s07,s08,s09,s41`, `p04`, `p05`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (message divergence) The runtime `TypeError` for an unorderable pair names the TPy type where CPython names the Python one.** [`union-order-typeerror-names-tpy-type`] `a < b` on an `Int32 | str` holding an int against a str raises `'<' not supported between instances of 'Int32' and 'str'`, where CPython for the same source says `'int' and 'str'`; on a user record it is `'__main__.Fixed'` against CPython's `'Fixed'`. The message comes from `tpy::type_name<T>()` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/type_name.hpp`), which deliberately spells TPy names so diagnostics never leak C++ ones -- the same convention every other runtime message follows, and `Int32` IS the type the user wrote. So this is a house-convention divergence, not a defect in the message: recorded because a program that prints `str(e)` sees different text under TPy and CPython, and `docs/PITFALLS.md` requires a test to print a stable token rather than the message for exactly that reason (`tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq` does). Fix only if TPy decides runtime exception TEXT should match CPython's, which is a wider decision than unions. Found by the review of the `::tpy::Union` redesign 2026-09-09.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `Own[]`-wrapped value union at a compare does not lower.** [`own-union-compare-rejects`] `def eq(a: Own[Int32 | Float64], b: Own[Int32 | Float64]) -> bool: return a == b` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.==`, where the same parameters spelled bare or `readonly[]` lower and render `(a == b)` (`tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq`). `Own[T]` on a value type transfers nothing, so reading one to compare it is the same value read; the compare gate's own `Own` leg (`_tparam_value(_unwrap_own(...))`) admits only a type parameter, and the value-union pair is checked after it on the unwrapped type only for the RENDER. Fix: unwrap `Own` before the union pair's admission too. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq2/own_readonly.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Reading or comparing a UNION-typed FIELD does not lower.** [`union-field-read-rejects`] With `v: Int32 | Float64` as a record field, both `c.v == d.v` and `a = c.v` reject at `field.result_type`; the same union in a local or a parameter lowers everywhere (`tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq`). This also keeps the `@dataclass`-generated `__eq__` chain from ever reaching a value-union field, so `@dataclass` over such a record does not compile. Ordinary Python, loud. Probes `/tmp/agents/unioneq/s23_field_read.py`, `s24_field_cmp.py`, `s42_dataclass_union_field.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A comprehension whose body holds a value-union compare does not lower.** [`list-comp-rejects-value-union-compare`] `[a == b for a, b in pairs]` over value-union operands rejects at `expr.list_comp`, where the same compare lowers at the eleven other positions of `docs/PITFALLS.md#same-construct-every-position` (`tests/cases/union/value_union_cross_alternative_eq` covers those). Pre-existing and not specific to the compare -- the comprehension lowering has no row for a value-union operand. Ordinary Python, loud. Probe `/tmp/agents/unioneq/s25_comp.py`. Found while fixing the value-union equality 2026-09-09.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A list comprehension RVALUE at a borrow-form container slot rejects at `expr.list_comp`: a `-> list[T]` return (`return [x for x in xs if x > 1]`, even over ints) and a constructor's `list[T]` parameter (`Flat([d[k] for k in names])` with `__init__(self, data: list[bytes])`); the `Own[list[T]]` constructor slot rejects at `call.ctor_arg.own_container` instead.** [`list-comp-rvalue-at-borrow-slot`] The same comprehension bound to a local lowers, and the `Own[list[T]]` RETURN lowers, so the gap is the sink, not the comprehension: a borrow-form slot has no storage for the fresh container, and the reject names the comprehension rather than the slot. For the return the language answer is a located sema diagnostic asking for `Own[list[T]]` (sema has one for a view returned over a temporary, `compatibility.py`) or the owned form inferred; for the constructor argument the free-function call arm's comprehension temp (the comprehension-argument-temp entry in `TODO.md`) is the render to reuse. Blocks `../tpy-examples/shedskin/doom` (`engine.py:446`, the next blocker after the bytes membership one closed). Pre-existing on master `d80d7e10d2`. Found 2026-09-10. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic hygiene) A `match` subject diagnostic spells an internal type name.** [`match-diagnostic-spells-intliteral`] `match 1:` reports `match subject must be a union, enum, primitive, record, or Optional type, got 'IntLiteral(1)'` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`, interpolating `effective_type`). `IntLiteral` is not a type a user can write, so this is a `docs/PITFALLS.md#no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` hit; the leak is `IntLiteralType.__str__`, so any other message interpolating a type that may still be literal-seeded carries it too. Fix: resolve the literal to its default int before rendering, at `__str__` or at each interpolation site. Found incidentally while probing the value-union compare positions 2026-09-09.


- **[MED small] (spurious warning on valid code) A comprehension's `if` clause does not narrow the element it tests, so a filtered optional access warns.** [`comp-filter-none-test-not-narrowing`] `[item.x for item in items if item is not None]` over `list[Foo | None]` warns `Potential None access on optional value; generated code adds runtime null check` at `item.x`, although the filter retains only non-None elements; the same test written as an `if` STATEMENT around the access narrows and stays silent. Root: comprehension `if` clauses do not feed `tpyc/sema/narrowing.py` the way an `if` statement's condition does, so the element read keeps its declared optional type and takes the checked deref. Loud (a warning plus a runtime check), never wrong output. Pinned as the current behaviour by `tests/cases/optional/comp_filter_unproven_optional_access`. Found by the pitfalls review 2026-09-07.

- **[MED small] (hidden allocation) An already-owned `str` at an `Own[str]` slot is copy-constructed into a temp and the temp moved, where the record twin moves the source itself.** [`own-str-slot-temp-copies-owned-source`] `xs.append(t)` with `t` an owned `std::string` local (a concat result), and `self.kept.append(v)` with `v: Own[str]`, both render `std::string __tmp_1{t};` followed by `xs.push_back(std::move(__tmp_1));` -- a full copy-construct plus a move of the copy -- while the same shape over a record renders `xs.push_back(std::move(v));` with no temp at all. Two separable parts: the temp itself is pure noise (`push_back(t)` costs the same one copy and is what the slot wants), whereas ELIDING the copy needs a last-use fact the lowering does not have at that slot. Root: `_own_lvalue_temp_slot` / `_own_move_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`) exclude value types from the temp-free move row, and the str-family carve-out in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` forces the temp path at every `Own[str]` slot regardless of whether the source already owns its buffer. Invisible to every test: the temp and the direct copy print alike. Pinned as the current render by `tests/cases/list/append_owned_str_local` and `tests/cases/str/own_str_arg_temp_in_while_condition`. Found by the pitfalls review 2026-09-07.

- **[LOW small] (diagnostic hygiene) Every THIR reject message ends in its internal reject tag, and one arm spells a THIR node class name into it.** [`reject-tag-reaches-the-user`] The message reads `... not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:binop.shape.+)`, and `_record_source_reject_detail` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, the fall-through `f"return.record_source.{type(v).__name__}.{slot}"`) puts a node class name inside it: `tests/cases/pointers/error_readonly_ptr_at_mutable_return`'s committed `diag.txt` reads `return.record_source.TpyCoerce.borrow`. The `no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` entry in `docs/PITFALLS.md` counts reject-reason codes as internal names, so the whole tag is in scope, not only the node name. Dropping the tag is not the fix: it is what the reject queue in `scripts/thir_migration/review/` and about 370 `error_` cases key on. Fix shape: a user-facing sentence per tag family naming the Python construct, with the tag kept in a trailing bracket (or behind a verbose flag) for the queue and the case annotations. Found by the pitfalls review 2026-09-07.

- **[LOW small] (silent resource leak) A consuming method on a type with `__del__` that RAISES before its transfer completes never runs the receiver's destructor.** [`consuming-method-raise-skips-del`] Codegen sets `this->__tpy_owned_ = false` unconditionally at the ENTRY of every consuming method (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`, the `__del__` suppression that prevents a double free of the moved-from receiver), so if the body raises before the move (a `finally` that raises after `return self`, or any raise ahead of the return) no object ever takes ownership and the one-time cleanup is skipped -- not a double destruction, a dropped one. Reproduces on master without any `finally`: any consuming method on a `__del__` type that raises before its `return`. Fix shape: clear the flag at the MOVE (the `THIRMove` of the receiver, `ret.self_move` / the finally-deferred capture), not at method entry, so an aborted transfer leaves the receiver owned. Found by the safety review of the consuming `return self` move 2026-09-07.

- **[LOW small] (hidden copy, perf) A last-use write of a reference-typed local into an `Any` field copies the payload once.** [`any-field-write-copies-source`] `h.payload = n` with `n: Node` at its last use renders `h.payload = std::move(::tpy::make_any(n));` (`tpyc/thir/lower/field_write.py`, `_lower_any_field`): `make_any(T value)` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/any.hpp`) takes its argument BY VALUE, so `n` is copy-constructed into the parameter and the outer `std::move` acts on a prvalue, which is inert. `_is_move_source` already proves `n` is dead after the write, so the fix is to move the source into `make_any` (`make_any(std::move(n))`) -- one render change, no semantic change (the source is never read again). Invisible to every test: the copy and the move print alike. Pinned as the current render by `tests/cases/dynamic_attrs/any_field_write_last_use_moves`. Found by /tpy-review 2026-09-06.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) Returning a module-global `Record | None` at an `Optional[record]` return emits the dereferenced global.** [`global-optional-record-borrow-return`] `_r: Rec | None = None` plus `def find() -> Rec | None: return _r` emits `Rec* find() { return (*_r); }` -- the global slot's read is dereferenced where the pointer-repr optional return wants the pointer -- and g++ rejects it (`cannot convert 'Rec' to 'Rec*' in return`). A PARAM or a LOCAL of the same type returns fine (`return x` renders the pointer), so it is the module-global slot specifically; the same global compares fine against `None` at a call site, so only the return position is affected. A module-level optional record with a lookup function that returns it is ordinary Python. Related to the value-Optional global narrowing entry below (same "the global slot's read is not recognized by the optional rows" family) but a different consumer -- there the reject is loud and front-end, here the front end accepts and the C++ does not build. Repro `/tmp/agents/i1/p/bug1.py` (20 lines). Found 2026-09-06 while converting the THIR resumable unit pins to cases -- the unit test string-matched the emitted `(find() == nullptr)` and never compiled the program. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
