- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, toolchain-caught) Awaiting a `Task[T]` whose payload is a VIEW assigns the view into an owning frame field.** [`await-task-view-payload-frame-field`] `async def sub() -> BytesView` plus `t = asyncio.create_task(sub()); r = await t` gives the frame field `r` the OWNED type (`std::vector<unsigned char>`) while the await's result stays the view (`tpy::own_return_t<std::span<const unsigned char>>`), so the resume assignment `r = std::move(__r0).value();` has no matching `operator=`. Awaiting the coroutine directly (`r = await sub()`) is not affected -- it is the `Task[T]` hop that loses the view spelling on the way to the frame slot. `print(len(await t))`, which never binds a local, compiles and runs. Loud, not silent. Repro `/tmp/agents/i1/p/bug4.py` (18 lines). Found 2026-09-06 while converting the THIR resumable unit pins to cases -- the unit pin asserted a face witness on the lowered THIR and never built the C++. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A BORROW-returning `__add__` whose payload is a CONTAINER has no render at an `Own` return slot, in either spelling.** [`dunder-borrow-container-own-return`] `def __add__(self, o: Pool) -> list[Int32]` then `def f(p: Pool, q: Pool) -> Own[list[Int32]]: return p + q` rejects at `stmt.return:binop.shape.+.record`, and so does the explicit `return copy(p + q)` -- the binop's own lowering declines a RECORD operand at the borrow-bind read the copy-construct tail takes. The RECORD payload of the same shape lowers (`tests/cases/returns/warn_return_record_borrow_dunder`), so the two families disagree on one operator spelling; sema warns the copy at both. Pinned by `tests/cases/returns/error_return_container_borrow_dunder`. Found while downgrading the Own-return borrowed-source error to the owning-slot warning 2026-09-06.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) A read of a module global BEFORE the same body's local assignment to that name resolves to the global instead of raising.** [`read-before-local-shadow-resolves-global`] Python makes a name assigned anywhere in a function a local for the WHOLE body, so `y = gate.x` ahead of `gate = Gate(1)` raises `UnboundLocalError`; TPy resolves the early read to the module variable and prints a value. Same family as the `match`-capture and post-handler `except`-capture entries: TPy's local model is block-scoped where Python's is function-scoped, so closing it means the same bind-then-mark-dead change, not a local patch. Pinned (as the compiler's current behaviour, with `no_cpython.txt`) by `tests/cases/globals/global_record_read_before_shadow`, which is the only remaining shape reaching the dedicated global-record-receiver lowering arm. Surfaced while converting the THIR unit pins to cases. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `copy()` over a CALL source at a ctor MEMBER-INIT field write rejects at `ctor.mil_field.{record,container}.call`.** [`copy-call-source-ctor-mil`] `def __init__(self, h: Holder): self.q = copy(h.brec())` rejects, while the same write in an ordinary method (`s.q = copy(h.brec())`) lowers, and so do the setitem, container-literal-element, `Own[T]`-arg and return sinks -- every one of them classifies its `copy()` source through `copy_construct_source` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`), which keys on the source's value form. The ctor member-init driver is a separate gate that still keys on the source being a bare NAME, so the two-step (`p = h.brec()` then `self.q = copy(p)`) is the only spelling there (`tests/cases/records/copy_call_source_sinks` pins it). Route that gate to the same classifier. Found while widening the `copy()` source shape 2026-09-06.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A TUPLE element at a reference BORROW return slot rejects, where the same element off a list/dict returns bare.** [`tuple-elem-at-ref-borrow-return`] `def first(self) -> list[Int32]: return self.pair[0]` on `pair: tuple[list[Int32], list[Int32]]` rejects at `return.record_source.subscript.borrow` (`tests/cases/returns/error_return_tuple_elem_borrow`), while `return self.rows[i]` over `list[list[Int32]]` routes. The reject is SOUND as the gate stands: a borrow-form tuple stores element POINTERS, so `std::get<N>` hands back a `T*` that no `T&` slot can bind -- and `_container_elem_lvalue_subscript` excludes every tuple receiver because the binding's form is walk state it cannot see. The storage-form tuple (a field, as in this repro) does yield the referent and could return bare, so what is missing is the form split, not the render. Whoever adds it must keep the borrow-form leg rejecting: the return ladder's `elem_sub_ok` guard exists precisely because the prechecked subscript lowering below it would otherwise emit the pointer into the reference slot. Found 2026-09-05 while merging the record and container return arms.

- **[LOW small] (wrong value-category answer, latent) `call_returns_cpp_ref` answers True for a VOID-returning method, so a builtin container's constructor call reads as a borrow-returning lvalue.** [`void-method-reads-as-borrow-returning`] `bytearray(b"z")` resolves to `bytearray.__init__` -- a native METHOD whose `fi.return_type` is `VoidType()` and whose `fi.is_constructor` is False -- and `call_returns_cpp_ref` (`tpyc/value_category.py`) only excludes a value type / `TypeParamRef` / `Own` / `Optional` / `Union` / protocol return. `VoidType.is_value_type()` is False, so the predicate reports "returns `T&`" for every `__init__` spelled this way. A user record's ctor is unaffected (`fi.is_constructor` short-circuits above the return check), so the hole is the builtin `__init__` shape. The shared classifier `is_rvalue_source` answers correctly for the same expression (a call whose callee names a registered record is an rvalue), which is why nothing miscompiles today: every consumer that pairs the two is safe. The reference if-expr arm pairs them deliberately -- admitting `bytearray(b"z")` as an lvalue ARM renders a prvalue `?:` that silently COPIES the other arm (probed: TPy prints 97 where CPython prints 90). Fix shape: answer False for a void return in `call_returns_cpp_ref`; it is a shared predicate, so the whole-corpus render sweep is the gate, not a unit. Found while merging the record and container if-expr arms 2026-09-05.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `match` class pattern capturing a `set` FIELD rejects where the `list` and `dict` fields of the same class bind.** [`match-capture-set-field`] `case H(d=m, s=q)` on `class H: d: dict[str, Int32]; s: set[Int32]` rejects at `stmt.match`; drop the `s=q` sub-pattern and the dict capture binds and mutates fine, and a `set`-only class pattern rejects on its own. `_match_capture_field_ok` admits all three families, so the block is downstream of the admission -- the set leg's capture render, not the gate. Re-verified 2026-09-05 against the original reproducer and against a set-only class pattern: a LOCAL subject and a PARAM subject both reject at the front end (`stmt.match`), with or without a mutation through the capture, while the `list` twin routes at both spellings. Found while folding the container family onto the reference axis 2026-09-05.

- **[LOW small] (inconsistent gate; the admitted leg is correct) The consuming self-field return excludes list/dict/set/Array by enumeration but admits `bytearray`.** [`consuming-self-field-return-admits-bytearray`] `_csf_pair` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` fences the identity move `return std::move(this->f);` off the container families with the comment "their consuming renders differ", but the enumeration omits `bytearray` and `_resolved_bytes_value` deliberately excludes it too, so a `bytearray` field DOES reach the move. Reachable and correct: `def take(self: auto_own[Self]) -> auto_own[bytearray]: return self.buf` emits `return std::move(this->buf);`, runs, and matches CPython, while the `list[Int32]` twin rejects at `return.consuming_self_field`. So the exclusion looks over-broad rather than the admission unsound -- the fix is to decide the render once for the whole reference axis, admitting the other four families or fencing bytearray with them. Found while folding the container family onto the reference axis 2026-09-05.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A VIEW-typed `str` / `bytes` source into a pointer-variant union slot rejects.** [`ptr-union-view-source`] `text: str | dict[str, str] | None = None; text = s` with `s` a `str` PARAM (a `std::string_view` at runtime) rejects at `decl.ptr_union_source`: the union's `str` member is an owned `std::string` behind a `std::string*`, and a view has no owned buffer to point at. The owned-rvalue sources (a call, a method call, a literal) route since 2026-09-04 through a function-scope value-variant slot (`tests/cases/union/union_ptr_variant_value_member_call`); the view source needs materialization into that slot (`std::string(s)` / `bytes_copy(s)`), the same family as the value-Optional view walrus rung. Found by the user's batch-3 review.

- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output, pre-existing) A record WITH bases whose fields are all class-annotated is not reordered by `__init__` assignment order, so a member-init reading an earlier-assigned field initializes in DECLARATION order and reads garbage.** [`based-record-fields-not-reordered`] `class Derived(Base): b: Int32; a: Int32` with `self.a = 5; self.b = self.a + 1` emits `: Base(), a(5), b(this->a + 1)` over a `b`-then-`a` layout and prints `5 32765` where CPython prints `5 6`, silently under the default build (`-Wreorder` fires only under the harness's strict flags). `reorder_fields_by_init` runs from `tpyc/sema/registration.py` only when the record has INFERRED fields, and the parser-side reorder covers base-less records only. Since the 2026-09-04 member-init ordering gate consults the emitted field order, this shape is a located reject instead of garbage; the fix is to apply the reorder to based records too (member order is a per-record fact sema owns). Found by the batch-3 closing review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (warned, not rejected) A constructor member-init source that CALLS a method on `self` may read a field not yet initialized.** [`ctor-mil-self-method-source-unready-field`] `self.a = self.size()` in `__init__` before `self.n = n` hoists into the member-init list and `size()` reads `n` before it is set; sema warns `instance method called in __init__ before all fields are initialized`, and the 2026-09-04 member-init ordering gate (`mil_done_fields` in `tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`, which rejects a direct read of a not-yet-hoisted own field) deliberately does not treat a `self.method()` source as a read of every field, because that would turn every warned ctor into a hard reject. Whether the warning is enough is a language call; the gate is the place to escalate it.

- **[LOW small] (loud divergence) A slice bound that is a `BigInt` outside the Int32 range panics `Int32 overflow` where CPython clamps.** [`slice-bound-bigint-outside-int32-panics`] `xs[2:1000000000000]` reads and, since 2026-09-04, slice-assigns narrow the bound with `to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`, so an out-of-range bound is a runtime panic rather than a clamp to `len(xs)`; the read path always did this, the write path previously rejected at compile time. Fix shape: clamp a BigInt bound to the container length before narrowing, as the runtime's `BasicSlice` does for in-range values. A second face: a BigInt STOP variable with a list RHS on a slice ASSIGN emits ill-formed C++ (`template argument 2 is invalid`) rather than a panic.

- **[HIGH small] (dangling pointer, no diagnostic) A record RVALUE bound to a `const T&` parameter whose address the callee STORES dangles.** [`const-ref-arg-temporary-stored`] `h.keep(V3(3.0))` where `keep(self, v: V3)` does `self.ref = v` into a `Ptr[V3]` field: the param stays const-inferred (a stored address is not a mutation), the ctor rvalue binds the temporary to `const V3&`, and the stored pointer outlives the full expression. Pre-existing through the ctor leg on master; the 2026-09-04 batch widened the same admission to any record-returning free or method call (`h.keep(b.muls(3.0))`) in `_method_ctor_rvalue_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`). Fix shape: sema must treat a param whose address escapes into storage as non-borrowable-from-a-temporary (an escape fact on the param), and the arg row should then reject an rvalue there. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A subclass of a builtin container that declares no `__init__` emits `using <base C++ type>::<PYTHON name>;`.** [`inherited-ctor-using-spells-the-python-name`] `class MyBA(bytearray): pass` emits `using std::vector<uint8_t>::bytearray;`, which g++ rejects ("'bytearray' has not been declared in 'class std::vector<unsigned char>'"). `_cpp_base_name()` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) does not consult the TypeDef's `cpp_formatter`, so for a formatter-carrying builtin base the injected-class-name half of the `using` is the PYTHON name; the record emitter's comment (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py`) says it derives that half "from the C++ side", which holds only for `@native`-renamed records. Only `bytearray` reaches it today: its zero-argument constructor makes `MyBA()` legal to sema, while the `list`/`dict`/`set` flavours stop earlier (sema demands the base constructor's argument and the call then rejects at `call.ctor_arg.protocol.static`). A subclass that declares its own `__init__` emits no `using` and builds -- that shape is `tests/cases/calls/stub_receiver_shapes`. Pre-existing (identical before the bytearray receiver fold, which only changed which reject the method CALL got); found 2026-09-05.
- **[MED small] (loud runtime panic on valid code) `sum()` over a `bytearray` accumulates in `uint8_t` and panics on the first overflow where CPython returns the exact sum.** [`sum-over-bytearray-overflows-uint8`] `sum(bytearray(b"\xff\xff"))` panics `UInt8 overflow in addition` where CPython prints `510`: `builtin_sum<T>` deduces its accumulator from the ELEMENT type and `add_check<uint8_t>` traps, so any bytearray whose bytes total more than 255 is unusable. The accumulator should widen the way CPython's does (an `Int32`/`BigInt` result for a narrow integer element), which is a stub/runtime signature question, not a lowering one. `bytes` has the same shape. Pre-existing for the bare NAME spelling; the FIELD spelling (`sum(self.buf)`) became reachable 2026-09-05 with the native-Iterable arg rows. Loud, not silent. Found by /tpy-review of the container-family fold. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) `bytearray(n)` with a runtime `BigInt` size emits `::tpy::bytes_from_size(n)` against a fixed-int parameter.** [`bytearray-size-bigint-unnarrowed`] Same family as the slice-bound narrowing closed in batch 3: a BigInt at a fixed-int native slot needs `to_fixed_check<int32_t>()`. Found 2026-09-04 in the doom example.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) `.copy()` on an `Array[T, N]` receiver emits `::tpy::list_copy`, which has no `std::array` overload.** [`array-copy-dispatches-to-list-copy`] `xs = [3, 1]; ys = xs.copy()` -- the unmutated literal resolves to `Array[Int32, 2]` and the method resolves to the `list` stub, so g++ reports `no matching function for call to 'list_copy(std::array<int, 2>&)'` with no TPy location. Both spellings are affected: the assigned one is identical on master, the DISCARDED one (`xs.copy()` as a bare statement) reached a located `method.ret_type` reject on master and reaches the same broken call since 2026-09-05. The fix is the receiver's method resolution -- an Array receiver needs the array copy render, or the resolution must refuse the list stub -- not a family re-check at the result-shape row. `tests/cases/list/discarded_container_result` keeps its receiver a `list` on purpose (it appends) so it does not sit on this. Found by /tpy-review of the container-family fold. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) `self.pixels = make(n)` -- a FREE-CALL source for a `bytearray` field in a constructor -- rejects at `ctor.mil_field.nominal.call`; `list(b)` on a bytearray rejects at `call.inst_arg_shape`.** [`bytearray-ctor-field-and-list-conv`] Adjacent bytearray rows met while pinning the bytearray return; neither has an oracle problem, they are plain missing arms. Found 2026-09-04. The third row is CLOSED since 2026-09-05: the TYPE-constructor spellings (`bytearray()`, `bytearray(seed)`, `bytearray(n)`) route, because `_container_storage_field` no longer demands type arguments and so admits the one non-generic reference container (`tests/cases/records/container_ctor_field_init`, with `error_bytearray_ctor_field_call` pinning the free-call half that stays). A fourth row, the same seam: a buffer CONSTRUCTOR at a `bytes` field member-init -- `self.data = bytes(src)` in `__init__` -- rejects at `ctor.mil_field.nominal.call`, while the identical store in an ordinary method lowers. It rejected one tag over (`.native_call`) while the buffer constructors named a factory; once the owned type constructs from its own view the two rows became the SAME reject. Not bytearray-specific (`bytes(src)` from a plain `bytes` param rejects the same way); met 2026-09-10 while pinning the bytearray-at-an-owning-bytes-sink rule, which is why `tests/cases/bytes/bytearray_copy_into_bytes_sink` puts its field sink in a method (`tests/cases/records/error_ctor_bytes_native_call` pins it; its NAME predates the tag move).

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A str LITERAL default at `dict.setdefault(k, default)` breaks the runtime template's `V` deduction.** [`setdefault-default-literal-deduction`] `d.setdefault(k, "1")` on `dict[str, str]` emits `::tpy::dict_setdefault(d, k, "1")` and g++ reports *no matching function ... `(ordered_map<string, string>&, string&, const char [2])`*, with no TPy location: `dict_setdefault(m, const KeyArg&, V def)` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dict_ops.hpp:127`) deduces `V` from the map AND from `def`, so a `const char[N]` is a second, conflicting deduction. Same for a BigInt-valued dict with an int literal (`dict[str, int]`, `def` renders bare `1`). The `Own[V]` slot's own row renders the literal bare, correctly for every sink whose type is spelled rather than deduced -- so the fix belongs at the deduced-slot end: either target-type the literal at a native free template's slot, or give `dict_setdefault` a separate `DefArg` template parameter like its `KeyArg`. `dict[str, Int32]` with an int literal is fine (`99` renders `int32_t`), which is why `tests/cases/dict/dict_setdefault` never saw it. It is the DEFAULT's slot, not the key's: reproduced with an owned-local key and unchanged by the key's form. Found 2026-09-05.

- **[LOW small] (CPython stub broken) `lib/cpy/tplib/requests.py` fails to import under the current CPython.** [`cpy-requests-stub-import`] `from http.client import _Connection` raises `ImportError` (the private name is gone), so no program importing `tplib.requests` -- `examples/net/curl.py`, the landing `requests_demo.py` -- can run under CPython for a parity check. Found 2026-09-04 while making curl compile.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) An UNMUTATED list literal local returned inside a tuple at an `Own[list[T]]` element slot spells its Array.** [`array-literal-in-own-tuple-return`] `def f() -> tuple[Own[list[float]], Int32]: a = [1.0, 2.0]; return a, 1` -- `a` resolves to `Array[float, 2]` and the return emits `std::tuple<std::vector<double>, int32_t>{std::move(a), 1}` from a `std::array`, which g++ rejects; sema accepts the Array-to-list-slot pairing. The same resolution-sink family as `copy-array-literal-into-list-slot` (a tuple return element slot is one more sink that should force `list`). Found 2026-09-04 while closing the owned-container tuple return for the adatron example. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[HIGH small] (latent use-after-scope, both paths) A pointer-variant union local first bound to `None` and reseated inside a BLOCK reads a destroyed slot after the block.** [`union-inline-slot-block-scoped-reseat`] `pet: Dog | Cat | None = None; if flag: pet = Dog("rex")` then `pet.name` after the `if`: the `UNION_INLINE_SLOT` reseat declares its value-variant `__slot_N` inside the block while the pointer-variant local it feeds outlives it, so the post-block read dereferences a dead slot (it happens to print correctly today; the frame memory is still intact). Pre-existing on the F1-record member leg and byte-identical on the pre-deletion emitter; the 2026-09-04 widening of the ptr-union source row to owned-buffer members (`bytes`/`str` from a call) extends its reach, and `examples/net/curl.py` has exactly this shape. Fix shape: at a None-literal-init ptr-union decl whose name is in `prescan.rvalue_reassigned`, pre-declare the function-scope rebind slot -- the `OPT_PTR_SLOT` sibling in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` already does -- so reseats take `UNION_RVALUE`; this moves existing snapshots (e.g. `union/union_ptr_variant_none_write`) and diverges from the oracle, so it is its own change. Distinct from the rebind-slot drop-timing entry. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Since 2026-09-04 `examples/net/curl.py` compiles to exactly this shape.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud; deliberate) `zip(h.xs, ys)` -- a FIELD (or any non-name lvalue) container argument to `zip` -- rejects in a comprehension over reference elements.** [`comp-zip-field-arg-over-reject`] At function scope the field selects `zip_direct_iter` and lends correctly, but inside a method whose `self` is inferred readonly the container arrives `const` and `val_or_ref_t<Node>` (a `Node&`) cannot bind, so the pre-deletion emitter produced six C++ errors for `zip(self.xs, ys)`; the lowering types are identical for both spellings (`NominalType(list[Node])`, no readonly marker), so telling them apart needs the receiver's const verdict from sema. Until that fact reaches the row, `_source_arg_copies` admits plain NAMES only. Same day as the fence (2026-09-04).

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A comprehension over `d.items()` whose VALUE type is a reference type fails the build.** [`comp-dict-items-ref-value`] `[v.bump() for k, v in d.items()]` over `dict[Int32, Node]` emits `auto& __tup_1 = *__beg_0;`, binding a non-const lvalue reference to the view's rvalue `std::tuple<const int&, Node&>`; g++ rejects it. `d.items()` is not a combinator source, so the 2026-09-04 combinator fence does not see it; the unpack head needs `auto&&` (or the `tuple_elem_ref` normalization the for-statement uses). Found by the batch-2 closing review while probing the fence. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) `zip` / `enumerate` over an ITERATOR argument yields COPIES of reference elements, so `for a, b in zip(filter(pos, ns), xs): a.v += 10` leaves `ns` unchanged.** [`nested-combinator-yields-element-copies`] TPy prints `[1, 2]` where CPython prints `[11, 22]`; same for `enumerate(filter(...))`, `zip(reversed(...), ...)`, `zip(ns, [10, 20])`, `zip(ns, range(2))`, `zip(mk(), ns)` with `mk() -> Own[list[Node]]`, `zip(gen(ns), xs)`, and `filter(pos, gen(ns))` -- in a plain `for` as well as a comprehension. Runtime cause (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/itertools.hpp`): `builtin_zip` / `builtin_enumerate` pick the owning flavor (`owning_zip_iter`, `std::tuple<Ts...>`) over the direct flavor (`zip_direct_iter`, `std::tuple<val_or_ref_t<Ts>...>`) whenever ANY argument is an rvalue, and the owned tuple copies each element out; `builtin_filter` / `builtin_map` branch on `detail::has_begin_end<Iterable>` -- a container of either value category goes to the direct `val_or_ref<T>` flavor, anything else (a generator, another iterator) to `filter_iter` / `owning_filter_iter`, whose `next_iter_mixin<..., T>` returns `T` BY VALUE. Only the direct-container flavors lend. Since 2026-09-04 the comprehension route rejects every copying spelling for reference elements (see `reversed-yields-element-copies` for the exact rule); the `for` route is untouched because `for a, b in zip(...)` is everyday and a reject there is a language decision. Sibling of `reversed-yields-element-copies`: both are the runtime yielding by value where the forward path lends. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud; was a use-after-free) `iter(<temporary>)` as a comprehension source rejects.** [`comp-iter-rvalue-source`] `[v for v in iter(mk())]` printed garbage on both paths: `::tpy::__iter__` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/dunder.hpp`) has no owning overload -- it binds `const std::vector<T>&` and returns a span over the destroyed temporary -- where every other combinator owns its rvalue source. Since 2026-09-04 the comprehension route rejects it (`_iter_rvalue_source`, `tests/cases/list/error_comp_iter_rvalue_source`); the real fix is an owning `__iter__` overload in the runtime.

- **[MED small] (accepts-invalid, silent) A NESTED def drops the keyword-only marker, so a positional call CPython rejects compiles and runs.** [`nested-def-kwonly-marker-dropped`] `def outer(): def kwonly(x: int, *, k: int) -> int: ...; kwonly(3, 2)` -- CPython raises `TypeError: takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given`; TPy accepts it. Same root as `nested-def-default-ignored`: the nested-def `ParamInfo` carries no signature metadata (defaults, kw-only, arity) beyond the positional list. Found 2026-09-04 while adding the ignored-default warning. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, both paths) A hook-mode `match` capture of a REFERENCE type into a resumable frame slot is an emplaced COPY, so a mutation through the capture across a suspension never reaches the caller.** [`resumable-match-capture-frame-emplace-copies`] Anchor for the "Resumable-path variant" paragraph of the match-binding entry further down, which carries the shape, the `13 3` vs `13 13` witness, what THIR fences today and the fix shape (a pointer frame slot, borrow form). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong data / double free, accepted on master) A comprehension whose element is a movable or record NAME at its last use moves it INSIDE the loop, so iterations 2..N use a moved-from object.** [`comp-element-move-inside-loop`] `ls = [b for i in range(2)]` with `b` a `Box` compiles, then aborts with `free(): double free`; with a plain record `r` it prints `9 1` where CPython prints `9 9`; `return std::move(b)` is emitted per iteration. The list-repeat path already guards this one-source-N-slots hazard with `suppress_move`; the comprehension element path does not. Pre-existing (identical on the pre-deletion emitter), found by the batch-2 review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (segfault on valid code; the warning lies) A plain declaration from an element of an Optional list of Optional records -- `r = xs[0]` on `xs: list[Rec | None] | None` with no `is not None` guard -- drops the receiver's `deref_check`.** [`optional-list-elem-decl-drops-deref-check`] The render is `optional_to_ptr(::tpy::__getitem__((*xs), 0))` (exit 139 on a None receiver) while sema warns "generated code adds runtime null check" for that very line; identical on the pre-deletion emitter. The walrus spelling had the same drop through a private lvalue proof; batch 2 routed it through `_container_elem_lvalue_subscript` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`), whose `needs_optional_runtime_check` guard turns it into a located reject (`tests/cases/control_flow/error_walrus_optptr_optional_recv`) because no THIR arm spells `deref_check(recv)[i]` for a subscript on an unproven-Optional receiver (the general read rejects as `subscript.optional_check`). One row closes both spellings: a checked-deref receiver render at the element-lvalue predicate; until then the declaration arm should take the same reject rather than crash. Sibling of `unnarrowed-optional-subscript`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent drop, now warned) A parameter DEFAULT on a NESTED def is ignored: the lambda takes every argument, and a call relying on the default is rejected with an arity error that never mentions the default.** [`nested-def-default-ignored`] `def outer(): def scale(v, k=2): ...; scale(5)` -- identical on the pre-deletion emitter. Since batch 2 sema warns that the default is ignored (`tests/cases/nested_def/param_default_unused`); the fix is either to honour the default at closure call sites or to reject the def. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (accepts a shape it then cannot render; sema asymmetry) Keyword arguments to a NESTED class constructor are not normalized into positional order.** [`nested-ctor-kwargs-unnormalized`] `Inner(v=1)` is normalized by sema; `Outer.Inner(v=1)` is not, so the THIR ctor arm has nothing to render and rejects (`tests/cases/calls/error_nested_ctor_kwargs`). The normalization should not depend on the callee's spelling.
- **[LOW small] (spurious warnings, both paths) Two false positives around aliasing.** [`spurious-alias-warnings-select-and-own-literal`] (a) "ternary copies a reference type where CPython would alias" fires on a pointer-Optional select whose arms are container ELEMENT lvalues -- no copy occurs and the mutation is observed (`tests/cases/control_flow/ternary_lvalue_arms`); (b) "Own[T] param 'a' is never consumed" fires when the param is moved into a returned container literal (`tests/cases/generics/generic_list_literal_elem`). Both cases carry the warning annotated.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; the oracle SEGFAULTED) A module-scope union global initialized to `None` first -- `g: A | B | None = None` -- rejects at `top_level.global_slot_shape`.** [`global-union-none-first`] The pre-deletion emitter wrote the monostate through the still-null slot pointer (`(*g) = std::monostate{};`), built, and died with exit 139, so there is no render to mirror. The sibling shapes (a record or container rvalue, a field source, a subclass upcast) route since 2026-09-04 (`tests/cases/globals/global_slot_source_shapes`); this one needs the slot allocated before the None store. Related: a union global written from a SCALAR global name (`u: Int32 | Point = n`) also rejects, where the oracle emitted `int32_t*` into a `std::variant<int32_t, Point>*` and failed the build. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; the oracle was SILENTLY WRONG) A local that shadows a `native_global` name and is written inside a branch or a `try` body rejects (`if.hoist_native_global`; the `try` twin at `stmt.try:try.hoist`).** [`native-global-shadow-branch-write`] `if c: frame_count = 1` ... `return frame_count` with `frame_count` also a `native_global` at module scope: the pre-deletion emitter read the EXTERN (`::DG_FrameCount`) after the branch, returning the wrong value with no diagnostic, so the reject is the honest state until the hoist declares the shadowing local before the branch. Two bin rows (`stmt1/if_3056_native_global_shadow.py` and the `try` twin). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; oracle ill-formed) A nested def capturing a NARROWED union name does not lower.** [`nested-def-narrowed-union-capture`] `nesteddef.narrowed_capture` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`): the pre-deletion emitter referenced the narrowing alias inside the lambda without capturing it (`'__u' is not captured`). The lambda needs the alias in its capture list, or the narrowing re-derived inside. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; the oracle read the walrus target UNINITIALIZED) A condition mixing a walrus and a hoisted temporary -- `if (m := g(n)) > take(m):` -- rejects at `if.mixed_walrus_temps` / `while.mixed_walrus_temps`.** [`cond-walrus-before-hoisted-temp`] The pre-deletion emitter hoisted `__tmp_1 = take(m)` ABOVE the walrus assignment, so the call saw `m` before it was written; the reject replaces silent garbage. The condition-temp flush must order the walrus store before any temp that reads its target (the walrus rows in `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` are the place). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong code, THIR branch path only) A branch-body `isinstance` narrowing alias inside a RESUMABLE frame is not renamed away from a same-spelled frame field, so it shadows the user's variable.** [`resumable-narrow-alias-shadows-frame-field`] `async def f(a: Dog | Cat)` with a local named `__a = 7`, an `await`, then `if isinstance(a, Cat): print(a.sound(), __a)` emits `auto& __a = *std::get<Cat*>(a);` for the narrowing and then `std::cout << __a.sound() << " " << __a` -- the second `__a` reads the `Cat&`, not the user's 7. The resume-narrowing path still renames the alias unconditionally (`fresh_alias_local`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/emit_prims.py`, called from `_emit_resume_narrowings` in `gen_async.py`); THIR's branch alias naming (`_persistent_alias_name` / `_lower_narrowed_branch`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) applies the frame-field rename only on the post-`if` path. The resumable face of the LOW alias-collision entry below; found 2026-09-04 while closing the post-`if` narrowing rows in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py`, which is why the alias-vs-frame-field collision rows (`res.narrowed_resume` at `statements.py:4942/5088`) were left rejecting rather than half-closed. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++ on valid code, both paths) A `match` `as` capture of a `str` from an `Optional[str]` subject returned at a `-> str` slot has no view-to-owned conversion.** [`match-str-capture-owned-return`] `match s: case str() as got: return got` emits `return got;` with `got` a `std::string_view` into a `std::string` return slot. Same family as `select-narrowed-optional-view-params-owned-sink`; `tests/cases/match/optional_inner_chain_guard` returns `"got:" + got` to sidestep it.

- **[HIGH small] (SILENT CPython divergence, no warning) `reversed()` over a list of a reference type yields COPIES of the elements, so a mutation through the loop variable is lost.** [`reversed-yields-element-copies`] `for n in reversed(nodes): n.v += 1` over `list[Node]` leaves `nodes` unchanged (TPy prints `[1, 2]`, CPython `[2, 3]`). Reproduces in a plain `for` loop, so it is the runtime combinator, not the comprehension: `reversed_iter::__next__` (`runtime/cpp/include/tpy/`) returns `__getitem__` BY VALUE into its `expected`, where the forward iterator yields a reference. The other combinators (`zip`, `enumerate`) should be checked for the same value-return. Found 2026-09-04 while admitting combinator sources in comprehensions; the comprehension route FENCES it (`_combinator_copies` / `_source_arg_copies` / `_begin_end_container` in `tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`, keyed on the callee's `qualified_name`, one node at a time with NO recursion, reference elements only): `reversed` (or any callee off the list) rejects; `zip` rejects unless EVERY source argument is a plain NAME of a begin/end container (a field argument is a safe over-reject, `BUGS.md#comp-zip-field-arg-over-reject`); `enumerate`/`map`/`filter`/`iter` reject unless every source argument is a begin/end container of either value category (list/dict/set/Array/dict-view/`Span`/records with synthesized begin-end); any combinator call as an argument rejects at either tier (`tests/cases/list/error_comp_reversed_ref_elem`, `error_comp_reversed_nested_ref_elem`, `error_comp_nested_combinator_ref_elem`, `error_comp_rvalue_container_arg`, `error_comp_owned_container_arg`, `error_comp_generator_arg`, `error_comp_filter_generator_arg`, `error_comp_nested_filter_arg`, `error_comp_nested_lending_combinator`; the lending shapes route in `list/comp_combinator_source`, including `enumerate(mk())` over an owned rvalue and a named `Span[Node]` zip argument) precisely because of this entry -- remove that fence together with the runtime fix. The open question is answered: `zip`, `enumerate`, `filter`, `map` and `iter` lend references only on the direct-container flavor (after the 2026-09-04 `NextIterator::operator++` fix, which refills its cached tuple by destroy-then-construct instead of assignment); `reversed` copies always, and every combinator copies on its non-container flavor (`BUGS.md#nested-combinator-yields-element-copies`). A plain `for` over any of those copying spellings is untouched and still loses the mutation. Distinct from the move-only `reversed()` entry below (that one is rejects-valid). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, sema misses a readonly violation) A COMPREHENSION loop variable over a `readonly[list[T]]` passed to a mutating consumer is not checked.** [`comprehension-loop-var-readonly-unchecked`] `def f(items: readonly[list[P]]): [bump(v) for v in items]` with a mutating `bump` passes sema (the for-statement form is rejected) and emits `bump(const P*)`, which g++ rejects. Same for `readonly[list[P | None]]` with an Optional-narrowed loop var. Pre-existing on master through the non-Optional form; the THIR fence that hid the Optional form went with the 2026-09-04 comprehension rows. Same root as the untagged entry on comprehension-body mutation not propagating to the source container. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

Taking a container read-only and then reading it is ordinary code, and there is no spelling of the access that gets through. **PRE-EXISTING** -- reproduces byte-for-byte on the pre-cutover checkout, so it is not fallout from deleting the AST body emitters. - **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A NUL `Char` is falsy in a boolean context, where CPython -- and this project's own documented rule -- make every `Char` truthy.** [`char-nul-truthiness-diverges`] `nul = Char("\0")` followed by `if nul:` takes the ELSE branch under TPy and the THEN branch under CPython. `Char` lowers to C++ `char`, and the condition renders as the bare `if (nul)`, which is C++'s `!= 0` test -- so the one code point whose integer value is zero flips. `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` puts `Char` in the str-like family (`len(c)` returns 1) and states the truthiness rule for that family as `__len__() != 0`, which is constant-true for a `Char`; CPython agrees, since a length-1 `str` is always truthy. So the C++ side is the wrong one, not the stub. Silent: no diagnostic fires, and the divergence is invisible to a test that never uses NUL. Reachable wherever a `Char` comes from parsed or binary input -- a NUL terminator, a padding byte, a `chr(0)` sentinel -- which is exactly where a scanner would test it for emptiness. Both paths render identically, so this is not a lowering artifact. Fix shape: render a `Char` condition as the constant-true form the str-like family already uses (evaluating the operand for its side effects), rather than falling through to the scalar `!= 0` test. Repro `/tmp/agents/grind2/probes2/char_truthy.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

In-place accumulation is a normal use of `reduce`, so the divergence is reachable without doing anything unusual. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

The narrowed sibling was fixed; this arm fires only when the analysed type is NOT Optional, so the runtime-check branch was never covered. The aug-assign flavour of the same shape is instead a LOUD build failure, and the dict flavour is unreachable (sema rejects a str index on an un-narrowed `Optional[dict]`). **PRE-EXISTING.** Fix shape: the same shared receiver-unwrap helper as the union entry above -- these two are one defect seen at two receivers. - **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output) A GUARDED catch-all in a non-final `match` arm is hoisted to the C++ `switch` default, so a later arm wins over it.** [`guarded-wildcard-switch-default`] `match c:` with `case _ if cond: return 1` followed by `case C.G: return 2` emits `switch (c) { case C::G: return 2; default: if (cond) return 1; else return 3; }` -- a C++ switch has no source order. Re-verified 2026-09-03 on an enum subject, built and run: TPy prints `1 2 3 3` where CPython prints `1 1 3 3`. The site is `_lower_scalar_arms` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py:1389`): every label-less arm goes into `default_entries` and that group is appended after `group_order` regardless of source position. Reproduces on enum and on fixed-int subjects, and on an `Optional`-of-enum subject through the optional inner dispatch, which shares the same helper. **Scope this by CALL SITE, not by subject type.** An earlier version of this entry enumerated safe SUBJECTS, which is the wrong axis and is how both the `str` tier and the optional wrapper were missed: the defect is in the shared arm walk, so every tier that calls it inherits it and the reachable spelling differs per caller. `int`/BigInt and bare union subjects ARE safe (a guard forces the ordered if/elif tier, and the guarded union tier appends the wildcard per index in source order), and under the optional wrapper a plain `case _ if k:` is also safe because `partition_optional_cases` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py:184`) bails on guard-plus-catch-all -- only the or-with-wildcard spelling reaches it there. **`str` is NOT safe.** The string tier has its own order-destroying partition, filed separately at BUGS.md#guarded-arm-string-switch-hoist: past `STRING_SWITCH_THRESHOLD = 5` literal arms it emits the non-literal arms in a block AFTER the switch, so a guarded arm loses to every literal following it. **The two are one defect class at two tiers** -- a dispatch tier that partitions guarded/non-literal arms into a trailing or default group discards source order, which is the whole of Python's dispatch semantics -- so fix them together or the fix will be re-derived per tier. The or-group spelling `case C.R | _ if cond:` is the same bug -- the irrefutable-arm check added for the unguarded form deliberately skips guarded arms. `case _ if cond:` before a specific arm is ordinary Python, and this is silent. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
