- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container LITERAL at a union param builds the ptr-variant from the literal's own expr type, not the union member's.** `def take(o: list[Int64] | Int64)` called as `take([1, 2, 3])` hoists `std::array<int32_t, 3> __tmp_1` and then emits `std::variant<int64_t*, std::vector<int64_t>*>{&(*__tmp_1)}`, which has no viable constructor. Reproduces with NO short circuit present, so it predates `143d7f1dc`; the same shape with `list[Int64] | StrView` fails identically. The temp is typed from the literal rather than from the union member the literal is being coerced into. Distinct from the `emplace` brace-init regression fixed in `0e1103a91` -- that fix makes the emplace itself well-formed and this variant construction is the remaining error. No corpus witness. Repros `/tmp/agents/fix-emplace/p21b_control.py` and `u1.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[LOW small] (latent, `-Werror` only) An `IntN(0)` constructor call loses its cast when it is a ternary arm.** `Int8(0)` as the else-arm of a ternary renders as bare `0`, so an `int` flows into an `int8_t` slot and the build fails under the test harness's `-Werror=conversion` while compiling clean without it. Found when a `narrow_int` row of `tests/cases/operators/short_circuit_brace_arg` tripped the harness; the row was reworded rather than pinned. Only the harness's warning flags make it observable today, which is why no case caught it.

- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A polymorphic `match` inside a method whose readonly-ness is INFERRED casts away const: the emitted signature takes `const`, the `dynamic_cast` target does not.** The `auto& __match_subject_1 = this;` bind and the `dynamic_cast` of a `Pet**` this entry recorded are FIXED -- the subject now binds `(*this)`. What survives is BROADER than the `match self:` headline it was filed under: for any method sema infers `@readonly` for (no decorator), the emitted `std::string Animal::describe() const` pairs with `if (Dog* __mpoly_0 = dynamic_cast<Dog*>(&__match_subject_1))` off a `const Animal*`, and g++ reports `conversion casts away constness`. The SAME method with an EXPLICIT `@readonly` emits `dynamic_cast<const Dog*>` and compiles, which is what isolates the gap: `_poly_subject_const` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:7757`) decides from the subject expression's ReadonlyType / const-borrow-name facts and never consults the enclosing method's inferred `is_readonly`. It bites `match self:` and `match self.<field>:` alike (both verified as build failures), and the corpus witnesses (`tests/cases/match/poly_expr_*`) all spell `@readonly` explicitly, which is why nothing fails today. Loud and toolchain-caught. Repro: a `@dynamic` `Tag` protocol, `class Animal(Tag)` / `class Dog(Animal)`, then an UNDECORATED `def describe(self) -> str:` holding `match self: / case Dog(): return "dog" / case _: return "?"`. The record-ternary composition (`c = self if flag else other` then `match c:`) now compiles and prints correctly, so that half of the entry is closed. Fix shape: seed the poly-cast const from the receiver's EMITTED const-ness, not from the subject expression alone. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, two positions) Work that a short circuit should skip is still evaluated in a comprehension with TWO OR MORE `if` filters and in a `match` OR-pattern guard.** Each hoists a temp for a conditionally-evaluated operand at the enclosing statement, so a ctor or call that CPython never reaches runs anyway. Exec-verified: `[x for x in xs if x > 100 if guard(Ctor(2))]` runs the ctor once per element with no element passing the first filter; `case Dog() | Cat() if guard(Ctor(9))` runs it against a non-matching subject (repros `/tmp/agents/shortcircuit/repro2.py`, `repro3.py`). **Neither is the conditional-region fix** that closed the `and`/`or`/ternary/chained-compare positions (`TempState.conditional_region`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`): the comprehension one is a render restructure (the filter clauses are joined and their temps flushed together) and the match one looks like a misplaced temp flush in the guard path. The comprehension one was re-verified as still-divergent AFTER that fix landed (`repro2.py`, ctor still runs per element). The match one could NOT be re-verified: `repro3.py` as written is rejected by sema (`class pattern 'Dog' does not match subject type 'Animal'`) both before and after the fix, so the original "exec-verified" claim for that position rests on a repro that does not compile today -- re-establish a compiling repro before treating the match guard as confirmed. An adjacent agent also proposed `elif` / `while` / `assert` / single-filter comprehensions / non-OR match guards as already-correct -- NOT independently verified, so do not treat that as a closed list either. Surfaced while scoping the short-circuit arg-temp fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence; residue of the conditional-region fix) An `auto`-typed arg temp in a conditionally-evaluated operand is still evaluated UNCONDITIONALLY.** `TempState.conditional_region` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) defers a conditional-operand temp by declaring it as an uninitialized `std::optional<T>` slot and banking `__tmp_N.emplace(init)` into the operand -- but `std::optional<auto>` is not a spelling, so `_slot_spellable` leaves any `auto`-typed temp eager. One site is a real divergence: `expressions.py:276`, the nullable-protocol-union arg path, which falls back to `create_typed("auto", gen)` when the analyzer has no type for the argument (`arg_expr_type is None`) and the argument is a genuine temporary -- so a ctor there still runs in a skipped branch. The two sibling `auto` sites (`expressions.py:1312`, `1325`) copy an LVALUE into an `Own[T]` slot; that copy runs no user code, so it is a wasted copy in a skipped branch (potentially of a large container) rather than a parity divergence. **Not witnessed live:** the `arg_expr_type is None` fallback is hard to reach and no repro was constructed -- confirm the shape is reachable before spending on it. Fix shape: give the site an explicit type so the slot can be spelled (the `Own[T]` str arm just above it already does exactly this, using `type_to_cpp(own.wrapped)` instead of `auto`), rather than teaching the region to handle `auto`. Surfaced while landing the conditional-region fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence; residue of the conditional-region fix) A NON-MOVABLE arg temp in a conditionally-evaluated operand is still evaluated UNCONDITIONALLY.** Sibling of the `auto`-typed residue above, different cause: `TempState._register` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) defers by emplacing into a `std::optional<T>` slot, and `emplace(T(...))` requires `T` move-constructible where the eager `T t = T(...);` form compiles via guaranteed C++17 elision even with the move deleted. So a temp whose type is non-movable (`@nomove`, or a record transitively owning a `UninitArrayStorage` of a non-trivially-relocatable element without `__move__`) MUST stay eager or the program stops compiling -- the `movable` gate on `_register` does exactly that, and `tests/cases/operators/short_circuit_nomove_arg` pins it. The cost is that `flag and take(Pinned(7))` builds the `Pinned` even when `flag` is false, so a ctor with side effects diverges from CPython for this one type class. Verified live: without the gate, `emplace(Pinned(7))` is a hard g++ error (`no type named 'type' in 'struct std::enable_if<false, Pinned&>'`), so the fix without the gate would have been rejects-valid; with the gate the shape compiles and runs eagerly. **Also over-conservative in the safe direction:** `is_movable()` is False for any `@nomove` record, but codegen only emits the deleted C++ move when the record also has a `__del__` (`records.py` `nonmovable` branch, which early-returns on `del_method is None`) -- a `@nomove` record without `__del__` keeps an implicit move and could have deferred. Fix shape: emplace via an in-place factory whose `operator T()` returns a prvalue (direct-init through a conversion function is elided, so no move ctor is needed), which would close both this entry and let the gate be dropped -- a runtime-helper addition, so it needs a design pass, not a patch. `create_typed` also defaults `movable=False` (a C++ spelling alone cannot answer movability); measured as costing zero snapshot churn across the corpus, so no `create_typed` deferral is witnessed today, but a caller that knows its type moves can opt back in. Surfaced by /tpy-review (runtime-cpp-correctness) of the conditional-region fix. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` for the factory, or leave as-is.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A walrus target typed pointer-repr `Optional` has no lowering arm for a CALL source.** `if (x := maybe_get(i)) is not None:` for `def maybe_get(i: Int32) -> Own[Item | None]` dies with `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.walrus)` (verified with `uv run tpyc` on 2026-09-03; the earlier symptom, `x = maybe_get(i)` against an `Item* x` and a g++ `cannot convert 'std::optional<Item>' to 'Item*'`, is gone with the AST emitter). The `opt_ptr` arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:6967`) delegates to `_walrus_opt_ptr_source`, which admits only a storage-Optional FIELD source, `None`, or an already-pointer NAME; a bare call rejects with detail `walrus.opt_ptr_src`. Closing it is not just adding the arm: the owning `std::optional<T>` rvalue must first materialize into stable storage before its address is taken, which is exactly the rebind-slot / resumable-ptr-slot machinery the sibling `TpyVarDecl` / `TpyAssign` pointer-rebind path already runs -- so a naive form fix would trade the compile error for a frame pointer into a destroyed temporary. Loud and reproducible in sync and resumable-frame bodies alike. Workaround: bind in a separate statement (the VarDecl path handles it). Everyday shape -- worth queueing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A borrow-tuple walrus bound from a tuple LITERAL over a `readonly` container spells a non-const element pointer -- ill-formed C++.** `(t := (i, nodes[i]))` for `nodes: readonly[list[Node]]` emits `t = std::tuple<int32_t, Node*>{i, &(nodes[...])}` where the address-of yields `const Node*`, and g++ reports `no matching function for call to 'std::tuple<int, Node*>::tuple(...)'` (verified directly, sync and resumable-frame bodies alike). The explicit tuple-type prefix comes from the walrus decl's borrow spelling, whose const-ness is read off `const_borrow_form_tuple_locals`, while the element render derives its own const from the SOURCE -- so a const-rooted literal element and the non-const tuple type disagree. A CALL source is unaffected (it renders its own borrow tuple). Loud and toolchain-caught, no corpus witness. Workaround: bind in a separate statement, or drop `readonly`. Pre-existing and independent of the resumable-frame walrus fix, which reproduced it unchanged on both paths. Repros `/tmp/agents/walrus-fix/r3_consttuple.py` (frame) and `r3b_sync.py` (sync). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of that fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A walrus in a SIMPLE-GENERATOR peephole body emits its pre-declaration AFTER its use -- ill-formed C++.** `yield (n := i * 10)` in a peephole generator emits `auto __val = (n = ...);` followed by `int32_t n;` inside the lambda, so g++ reports `'n' was not declared in this scope` (verified directly); the borrow form fails the same way with its pointer predecl landing after its use. The while-CONDITION walrus IS handled (its predecl goes to lambda scope, covered by `tests/cases/generators/gen_while_temp_condition`); a walrus in the YIELDED EXPRESSION is not. Same flush-ordering family as the walrus-bound `with` manager and the genexpr-filter walrus entries elsewhere in this file. Loud and toolchain-caught, so it cannot ship silently. Workaround: bind in a separate statement. Distinct from the RESUMABLE-frame walrus family (fixed 2026-08-19 on `fix-walrus-frame-shadow`: a frame-field target declares nothing and writes the field, `tests/cases/generators/gen_walrus_frame_shapes`); this is the peephole lambda path, where locals live on the lambda stack and a predecl is genuinely needed -- only its ORDER is wrong. Probes `/tmp/agents/walrus-frame/`, `/tmp/agents/walrus-fix/peep1.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[HIGH small] (silent value/reference divergence; what the unpacked binding aliases changes) An `Own[tuple]`-returning CALL relayed through another function loses its `tuple_to_pointer` lift at the unpack site.** For `def pass_through() -> Own[tuple[Int32, Box]]: return mk()` then `n, b = pass_through()`, the AST emits `auto __tup_1 = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<int32_t, Box*>>(pass_through());` while what ships is the bare `auto __tup_1 = pass_through();`. `tuple_elem_ref` then sees a `Box` VALUE where the lift would have handed it a `Box*`, so the reference-type element `b` binds to a different object -- a value/reference divergence, not a spelling nit. Confirmed live with `dualgen.py`: the diverging body (`main`) ROUTES; only the callee falls back, so no fallback masks it. No corpus case has the shape, so the byte-diff and the ratchet are both blind, and `move_audit`'s join is empty here. Distinct from the borrow-tuple RETURN rows landed in `dfa5b5150` (those cover the return position; this is the unpack SOURCE position consuming a relayed call). Repro `/tmp/agents/f1/main.py`. Surfaced by adversarial probing while scouting the sole-site tail. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[MED small] (unverified move at a copy/alias position; no corpus witness) An `Own[T]` NAME element of a tuple literal at a native protocol slot is MOVED where the deleted AST emitter passed it bare.** `def h(b: Own[Box]) -> UInt64: return hash((1, b))` -- both paths pick the same VALUE slot (`std::tuple<int32_t, Box>`), but the AST renders `{1, b}` and THIR rendered `{1, std::move(b)}`. Independent of the per-element capture fork that fixed the six sibling shapes (the slot is identical on both sides here; only the move differs), and structurally invisible to `move_audit`, whose join is empty at a copy/alias-position arm. Which render is right is now an open question with no second author to defer to: the element IS an owned last-use param, so the move is arguably correct and the deleted emitter's bare pass a missed move. The THIR fork now DEFERS the shape (`_proto_tuple_elem_borrow` returns None for any `Own` element; the unit that pinned the defer went with the THIR unit suite), so nothing miscompiles today -- what remains is deciding the oracle render and then admitting the shape on both paths. Note `get_expr_type` on an `Own[T]` NAME has already dropped the `Own`, so any fix must key on the declared type. Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/orch/implL/bug.py` (row `hash((1, b))`, `b: Own[Box]`). Surfaced by ablation scouting of the native-protocol tuple-literal arg row. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud; contradicts a warning on the same line) An UNPROVEN `Optional[dict]` receiver under a dict-view call has no lowering arm, so the loop head is a hard compile error.** `def scan(d: dict[str, Int32] | None) -> Int32: for v in d.values(): ...` warns "Potential None access on optional value; generated code adds runtime null check" and then dies with `error: in function 'scan': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:iter.method_call_shape)` (verified with `uv run tpyc` on 2026-09-03). The earlier symptom -- an unconditional `::tpy::dict_values((*d))` with no `deref_check`, silent UB on `scan(nullptr)` -- went with the AST receiver render. `_dict_view_iterable_ok` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:10847`) rejects any receiver carrying `needs_optional_runtime_check`, which is a correct fence -- the PROVEN-narrowed row beside it renders the bare deref -- but nothing renders the CHECKED-deref flavour, so the warning still promises code that is never emitted. Fix shape: render the checked deref in a receiver arm the way the value positions do, or reject the shape in sema with a message that matches the warning instead of leaving the two in contradiction. Everyday shape -- worth queueing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) Rebinding a BORROW-form tuple-unpack target writes THROUGH the alias instead of rebinding the name.** `x, y = both(p, q)` (for `def both(p: Point, q: Point) -> tuple[Point, Point]`, and the mixed `ref, owned = split(p)` flavour off `-> tuple[Point, Own[Point]]`) binds the borrowed element as `auto&& x = ::tpy::unwrap_ref(::tpy::tuple_elem_ref(std::get<0>(__tup_1)));`, and a later `x = q` emits a bare `x = q;` -- a copy-assign into the referent, so `p` silently becomes `q`. TPy prints `80` where CPython prints `8` (re-verified 2026-09-03, built and run both ways). The `is_ref` leg of `_standalone_unpack_target_binds` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:2181`) picks bind mode `"ref"` at `:2239` off `_f1_record` alone and never consults `lc.prescan.reassigned`; `tpyc/thir/emit.py:4454` then spells the `auto&&` alias. So it misses the pointer-local promotion the sibling target classes at the same site already do for a reassigned name. Silent: no diagnostic, wrong output. Fix shape: give a reassigned borrow-ref unpack target the `T*` pointer-local binding rather than the reference alias. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) `self: auto_own[Self]` combined with `@overload` emits every specialization TWICE with identical signatures.** `class W: @overload def m(self: auto_own[Self], x: Int32) -> auto_own[Int32]: ...` plus a `str` stub and an impl emits four member functions -- `int32_t m(int32_t)` and `int32_t m(std::string_view)` each declared twice -- and g++ rejects ("cannot be overloaded with"). Method expansion clones both the stubs and the impl into borrowing + consuming halves, so each stub appears twice; `_gen_overload_specialized_method` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py`) then takes `is_readonly=stub.is_readonly` but `is_consuming=impl.is_consuming` -- so the consuming axis comes from whichever clone `_collect_method_overload_groups` registered first and never varies per stub, leaving the two clones of each stub spelling one signature. Note the ownership consequence even if the duplication were suppressed: one polarity of the pair would be unreachable for the whole overload set, selected by clone-registration order rather than per-stub intent. The non-composed `auto_own` pair (no `@overload`) is unaffected -- it emits a borrowing and a consuming body correctly. Pre-existing and unrelated to THIR: the emission is the AST path, and `codegen_cpp/functions.py` is untouched by the branch that found it. Loud, no corpus witness. Fix shape: derive the consuming polarity per STUB the way const-ness already is, and suppress the duplicate where both clones of a stub would spell one signature. Repro `/tmp/agents/ovl/aown.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR overload-clone skip; the reviewer reported it as a silent polarity collapse, and building the repro showed it is actually a hard compile error. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A record inheriting a builtin container with NO explicit `__init__` emits `using std::vector<int32_t>::list;` -- the inherited-constructor `using` spells the TPy type name instead of the C++ base's constructor.** `class Plain(list[Int32]): pass` then `Plain([1, 2, 3])` fails with `'list' has not been declared in 'class std::vector<int>'`; a second error rides along (the ctor arg renders `std::array<int32_t, 3>` where the base wants `std::vector<int>`). The inherited-ctor `using` is emitted from the record's TPy base NAME, but the base's C++ spelling comes from the container formatter, so the two never agree for a formatter-carrying builtin -- the injected-class-name is `vector`, not `list`. Declaring any `__init__` avoids it (the record then has its own constructor). Loud, no corpus witness. Pre-existing -- reproduces unchanged at `5af9b227b`. Fix shape: emit the inherited-ctor `using` against the base's rendered C++ type (its injected-class-name), or suppress it for formatter-carrying builtin bases and synthesize a forwarding ctor. Repro `/tmp/agents/inh3/noinit.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the THIR inherited-container row and confirmed independently. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (rejects valid) `x in t` is rejected when `t` is a record inheriting `set` -- "Cannot use 'in' with non-iterable type Tags".** `class Tags(set[StrView]): ...` then `"x" in t` errors, though the record inherits `__contains__` from the set stub and CPython accepts it. The membership dispatch resolves `__contains__` / iterability against the receiver's own record, not its inherited builtin base, so every container-inherited operator-protocol dunder is suspect here (`in`, and by the same shape iteration and comparison dunders) -- ordinary inherited METHOD calls (`t.add(...)`, `t.discard(...)`) resolve correctly, so the gap is specific to the operator paths. Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: call the method form. Pre-existing and unrelated to THIR (the reject is in sema). Witness: the shape was cut from `tests/cases/inheritance/inheritance_builtin_dict_set` for exactly this reason. Fix shape: let the membership / iterability resolution walk the record's parents to a builtin container base, as the method-call path already does. Surfaced writing that case. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) `super().<method>()` on a builtin-container base spells the TPy method name against the C++ base type, ignoring the stub's `@native` rename.** In `class Overrider(list[Int32])`, an overriding `append` calling `super().append(value)` emits `this->std::vector<int32_t>::append(value)` -- `std::vector` has no `append`, g++ rejects. The qualified-super render composes `NominalType(parent).to_cpp()` with `escape_cpp_name(method)`, so it never consults `fi.native_name` (`push_back`) the way the ordinary inherited call does (`ml.append(10)` -> `ml->push_back(10)`, correct); a `@native(function=True)` stub like `pop` would need the free-function form instead, which that render cannot spell at all. Loud, no corpus witness -- overriding an inherited builtin method is already warned about ("Method 'Overrider.append' hides 'list.append'"), and no case does it. THIR keeps this on the AST path (the super-marked call is outside the plain-member slice), so no mirror to unwind. Fix shape: route the super/unbound-self dispatch through the same fi-driven native-name / free-function selection the plain member call uses, keeping only the base qualification. Repro `/tmp/agents/inh/ovr.py`. Surfaced probing the THIR inherited-container receiver row's override boundary. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent behavior divergence) `return <side-effecting-call>` in a Void-returning `async def` silently drops the call.** `async def outer() -> None: await asyncio.sleep(0); return noisy()` (noisy() -> None, prints) emits NO call to `noisy` at all -- `_make_async_return` keys the whole value render on `isinstance(ret_type, VoidType)` and never evaluates `stmt.value`, where CPython evaluates the expression and prints. The sync path is unaffected (a sync `return f()` evaluates f). Only literal `return None` / bare `return` are corpus-witnessed, so the drop is invisible there. THIR mirrors the skip byte-identically (the VoidType gate in the resumable ReturnT arm) -- per the broken-oracle rule the AST fix comes first, then both paths inherit it; the unit that pinned the mirror went with the THIR unit suite. Fix shape: when `stmt.value` is a non-literal expression at a Void slot, evaluate it as a discarded statement before the ready-return. Probe `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/void_side_effect2.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, async-sink cells 4-7 round) with a CPython comparison. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A pointer-repr container NAME in a REF vararg pack takes `&name` over the un-deref'd pointer.** A module-global `list[T]` (a `T*` pointer slot) passed by name into a `*args: T`-style REF pack renders `&xs` -- `T**` where the `std::array<const T*, N>` element needs the deref'd `&(*xs)` -- a hard g++ error on BOTH codegen paths (reviewer-probed with the AST alone). No corpus witness (the committed vararg cases pass locals/elements). THIR mirrors the render; the BORROW_BIND threading in `_lower_vararg_pack` documents that its "renders identically" claim holds only for the currently-reachable record slice. Fix shape: the pack element render should read pointer names through the same deref the value positions apply. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, cells 15 round). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++, toolchain-caught) A `match` capture passed as a VARARG takes the address of an already-pointer local.** [`vararg-of-pointer-capture-takes-address`] `def bump_all(*counters: Counter)` called as `case Bag(c=q): bump_all(q)` emits `std::array<Counter*, 1> __tmp{&q}` where `q` is already a `Counter*`, so g++ reports `cannot convert 'Counter**' to 'Counter*' in initialization`. The capture binds to the pointer form (it aliases the subject's field), and the pack element render does not deref a pointer-repr NAME before taking its address. Same mechanism as the module-global `list[T]` REF pack entry above -- the pack element render is pointer-blind for every pointer-repr source, not just globals -- so fix them together. Pre-existing: identical on master, where the const-inference miss adds a second error ahead of it. This is why `tests/cases/match/match_capture_mutation_credited` has no vararg section, although the vararg arm of the call-edge attribution it covers does handle captures. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/probe_vararg_simple.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the capture-attribution branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.


- **[MED small] (uncompilable C++) A raw-lowered `@error_return` call with a nested `@error_return` call in its argument subtree renders ill-formed C++.** `self.p = make(inner(n))` (both callees `@error_return`, inside a try or auto-propagate body) emits the outer `__try_tmp_N` block with the inner call's expression-level unwrap misplaced -- g++/clang reject (`cannot convert std::expected<int,E> to int32_t`; `deduced type 'void' for '__try_tmp' is incomplete`). Any raw statement-level er sink reaches it (name bind, field target, discard); no corpus witness exists because sema/codegen never gated it -- the THIR side rejects the shape via `_reject_nested_error_return_arg` at all four statement sinks, keeping both paths in fallback lockstep without blessing the broken render. Fix shape: the AST's raw-call statement handlers must pre-hoist nested er unwraps (or reject with a diagnostic). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, long-tail cells 11 round) with a direct g++ compile of the AST-only output. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small, latent UB] A top-level global-slot write inside a FOR-loop body leaves the global pointing at a BLOCK-scoped slot; the WHILE-body twin freezes the first iteration.** At module init, a first rvalue write to a non-value global inside a for-each body emits the backing slot WITHOUT `static` (`Point __global_slot_1 = Point(i);`) and then `p = &__global_slot_1;`, so any read after the loop exits derefs a dead stack slot -- latent UAF that happens to pass exec (the frame memory is typically intact within `__tpy_init`; the repro below builds, runs and prints `2`). The `static` is dropped by `branch_scope=in_branch` on the `GLOBAL_RVALUE` `THIRPtrLocalDecl` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:4503`, gated to for-bodies at statements.py:7609) and consumed at `tpyc/thir/emit.py:3843` (`_gs_static = "" if stmt.branch_scope else state.slot_static`). The sibling scopes do NOT share the defect and must not be conflated with it: the same write inside an `if`/`while`/`with`/`try` body is a hard reject (`stmt.var_decl:top_level.global_slot_branch`, statements.py:7606), so until 2026-09-04 the for-body arm was the only one that emitted; the `if` / `with` / `try` bodies now emit too, correctly with `static` (`tests/cases/globals/global_slot_branch_and_hoist` for `if`, `tests/cases/control_flow/with_target_reuse_read_after_global` for `with`; `try` probe-verified); the `while` body still rejects (`tests/cases/globals/error_global_slot_while_write`), so the for-body arm is the one outlier still emitting the unsafe form. The `while`-body twin (2026-09-04, oracle-verified) is worse than latent: a module-level `while` whose body writes a non-value global prints `0 0 0` where CPython prints `0 1 2`, because the slot's first-iteration value is re-read on every pass; it still rejects on THIR. Witness: `inference/reassign_none_loop_narrowing` (post-loop `if x is not None: print(x.x)`). Repro: `class Point` with an `Int32` field, `p: Point | None = None`, `for i in range(3): p = Point(i)`, then `if p is not None: print(p.x)`. Fix shape: NOT a bare static-ize -- `static T slot = init;` initializes once, which would freeze the first iteration's value. Route the for-body write through the existing hoisted flavor instead (`GLOBAL_HOIST_RVALUE`: a `static std::optional<T>` slot declared outside the loop, re-emplaced per iteration), which gives both a stable address and per-iteration assignment. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[LOW small] Sema stamps concrete narrow facts on statically-dead branches of exhaustively-folded isinstance or-chains, emitting dead extractions.** `if isinstance(v, A) or isinstance(v, B):` on `v: A | B` folds the second leaf to `true` (the chain is tautological), yet the implicit-else path carries a concrete `{v: A}` fact -- the AST emits an unreachable `auto& __v = *std::get<A*>(v);` past the early-return if (and, for the negated flavor, inside the dead branch). Semantically harmless (unreachable code) but wrong facts on dead paths; both paths emit it identically (THIR mirrors the oracle per the byte-diff discipline -- see the or-chain wave ledger entry, 2026-08-12; witness `tests/cases/union/union_isinstance_or_chain`'s `two_member`/`negated_or`). Fix belongs in sema's fold-aware fact stamping, not in either emit path.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NARROWED-Optional field as a borrow-tuple element has no lowering arm.** In a method returning `tuple[Inner, Int32]` (a `std::tuple<const Inner*, ...>` borrow tuple), `return (self.maybe, 1)` under `if self.maybe is not None:` dies with `error: in function 'get': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.tuple_literal)`, while the plain-field flavour `return (self.inner, 0)` compiles (both verified with `uv run tpyc` on 2026-09-03). The earlier symptom was the un-deref'd `&(this->maybe)` -- an `std::optional<Inner>*` into the `const Inner*` slot, rejected by g++ -- and it is gone with the AST emitter. The field-element leg (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:11596`, rejecting at `:11612` with detail `btuple.elem_source`) excludes an Optional-DECLARED field deliberately, but its comment's rationale -- that the AST emitted the broken render there so the shape must defer until the AST is fixed -- is stale: that emitter is gone and this leg is the only author, so it simply owes the narrowed deref. Fix shape: render `&((*this->maybe))` for a proven-narrowed Optional field element instead of rejecting. No corpus witness (the committed borrow-tuple cases use plain fields/names). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] Bytes ternary mixing a plain view-param arm and a bytes literal emits uncompilable C++.** `def f(c: bool, b: bytes) -> bytes: return b if c else b"x"` renders `return ((c) ? (b) : (::tpy::bytes_literal_owned("x", 1)));` -- the span param and the owned-vector literal have no common type, so the emit fails at the C++ step (clang: no conversion from `std::span<const unsigned char>`). Hidden because no exec witness exercises the shape (the narrowed `Optional[bytes]`-param flavor takes the whole-ternary `bytes_copy` wrap and compiles). Surfaced 2026-08-07 by the THIR wave-39 widening: THIR's arm is narrowed to the value-opt-param flavor and the plain-param flavor keeps deferring (the fence pin that documented it went with the THIR unit suite) until this emit is fixed -- the likely fix is applying the same owned materialization the str-mixed arms get.
- **[HIGH small] (silent UAF, certain) A `StrView` FIELD member-initialized from an owned-str-returning CALL dangles immediately.** `self.view_field: StrView = make_greeting(name)` in a ctor emits `Holder(...) : view_field(make_greeting(name)) {}` -- the `std::string` temporary dies at the end of the mem-initializer, so the `std::string_view` field points at freed storage from construction onward. The same class as the tracked StrView/Span field-gap entries but this manifestation is a CERTAIN use-after-free (no caller-lifetime dependence). Both codegen paths emit it identically (worktree-verified pre-existing at `7e9104262`; the THIR ctor-MIL call-rvalue leg mirrors it byte-identically per the owned-bytes-assign precedent rather than silently fixing one path). Fix shape: a sema diagnostic at the view-field-from-owned-rvalue MIL sink (steer to an owned `str` field or a named local), or materialize an owned backing member. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, waves 9-10 round). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (diagnostic false positive) `copy()` at a field store is not credited as Own-param consumption.** [`copy-not-credited-own-consumption`] `def __init__(self, v: Own[A | B]): self.u = copy(v)` warns `Own[A | B] param 'v' is never consumed` although codegen genuinely moves `v` into the field (the MIL's copy-unwrap + last-use move). The field/container consumption check (`tpyc/sema/statements.py:5307`) matches a bare-`TpyName` RHS only, unlike the shared `check_own_consumption` (`tpyc/sema/compatibility.py:2041`) which unwraps `copy()` at its other call sites. Fix shape: route the field-store check through the shared helper. Witness committed with an explicit `warning(/never consumed/)` annotation in `tests/cases/records/ctor_param_name_collision` (its diag documents the false positive; fixing this removes that warning line). Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the scope-leak fix.

- **[LOW audit] Residual stale name-keyed fields in the ctor member-init window.** The scope-leak fix (seed_param_locals_scoped clearing PARAM_LOCAL_SET_FIELDS + var_types) closes the demonstrated leak, but other per-body name-keyed fields stay stale through the pre-`setup_body_scope` MIL window: `const_ref_params` / the codegen context's `deep_const_borrow_params` name set (consulted by `is_const_union_source` and const-ref checks), `declared_vars` (the imported-function shadow check), `local_scope_names` (native-global shadowing), `narrowed_vars`, `overload_param_types`. No repro constructed -- a targeted probe (leftover `readonly[A | B]` const-ref param colliding with a ctor's Own-union param) rendered correctly because the MIL move arm consults none of them, and ctor params are never const-ref by design (a ctor's params carry no const verdict). The failure class is the fixed bug's: a same-named collision flipping a silently-different-but-compiling render. If a repro appears, extend the scoped seeder's clear with a purpose-named field tuple ("names read during the pre-setup window") rather than overloading PARAM_LOCAL_SET_FIELDS further. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + codegen-correctness).
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, loud) A WALRUS inside a genexpr FILTER over a `range()` source fails to compile: the counter lambda never CAPTURES the walrus target.** `sum(x for x in range(n) if (y := x * 2) > 3)` hoists `int32_t y;` at function scope but emits the counter lambda with an init-capture-only list and no capture-default (`[__i = int32_t(0), __stop = static_cast<int32_t>(n)]() mutable`), so the filter's `(y = ...)` draws `error: 'y' is not captured` / `note: the lambda has no capture-default`. (An earlier version of this entry said no declaration was emitted at all -- the declaration IS emitted, at function scope; it is the capture that is missing, so the fix is in the capture list, not in a predecl.) The capture list is built by `_genexpr_captures` (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py:1145`) from `collect_name_refs` over the element and the filter conditions, and a walrus TARGET is a write-only name -- it never lands in `refs`, so no `&y` is emitted; the render is the `range_args` counter-lambda arm of `tpyc/thir/emit.py` (line 1166 onward). Loud, toolchain-caught. Fix shape: add the genexpr's walrus targets to the capture set alongside the read refs. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) An `assert isinstance(...)` narrowing inside one branch of a RESUMABLE body (generator/async) leaks its C++ extraction alias into sibling branches of the flat CFG -- g++ rejects.** `def gen(a: int | str, flag): if flag: assert isinstance(a, int); yield str(a + 1) / else: print(a)` emits `const auto& __a = std::get<...>(a);` scoped inside the if-block and then references `__a` again in the else-block, where it is out of C++ scope -- `'__a' was not declared in this scope`. The non-resumable equivalent compiles fine (the persistent alias and its readers share a scope there); only the flat-CFG resumable driver splits them. Same flat-CFG-scoping family as the `await`-in-`except ... as e:` entry below, different root: the U4 persistent assert-narrow alias is emitted block-scoped while its narrowing fact stays live for the rest of the function. Fix shape: hoist the persistent extraction alias to frame/function scope in resumable bodies (or re-extract per BB). THIR fences the shape rather than mirror it (the union STR print row rejects in resumable bodies; the unit that pinned both the fence and the leak's mutation-detection went with the THIR unit suite); fixing the AST unfences it. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + docs-sync, the dynret/union-returns round; both compiled independent repros). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (uncompilable emit, exotic shape) An unproven field access directly on an `Own[record | None]`-returning CALL emits `::tpy::deref_check(<call>)` over the by-value `std::optional<T>` result -- no such overload exists, g++ rejects.** `print(make_maybe(True).x)` on `def make_maybe(..) -> Own[Point | None]`: the runtime-check emit assumes a raw-`T*` receiver, but the Own-declared return materializes the storage optional; the render should be the `deref_optional_check` storage sibling (or a sema error steering to a narrowed local). Loud, toolchain-caught, no corpus case. THIR fences the shape (`_optional_checked_recv_call` excludes Own-declared returns) and falls back byte-identically, so the fix belongs on the AST emit and THIR inherits it. The boundary unit that pinned the repro went with the THIR unit suite. Surfaced by the batch-10 review's exclusion probe. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A reassigned borrow-tuple local with ONE const binding source and a later ELEMENT WRITE emits ill-formed C++.** `_compute_borrow_tuple_const` ORs const over ALL binding sources, so `t = h.pair; t = h2.pair; t[1].val = 9` (h const-inferred, h2 not) declares `std::tuple<Int32, const Box*> t` and then writes through the const pointer -- g++ rejects (`assignment of member ... in read-only object`) though the write targets h2's mutable storage and CPython accepts. The const-OR is right for declarations (mutable->const lift compiles) but the ELEMENT-WRITE fact must feed back: a written name needs its const sources rejected in sema (a located diagnostic) or the write must re-anchor. Loud, toolchain-caught, no corpus case (the existing cases never write through a const-flipped name). THIR mirrors the AST byte-identically here (the btuple const-fixpoint rows), so the fix belongs at the AST/sema side and THIR inherits it. Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/adv_btconst.py` (`mutable_stays`). Surfaced dualgen-probing the THIR borrow-tuple const fixpoint. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (compiler crash on valid code, contract violation) A `THIRValidationError` escapes as an internal error instead of a located reject and kills the compile: a temp-needing call ARGUMENT at a tuple-unpack source.** [`thir-validator-escapes-unpack-temp`] `a, b = f(M())` -- the unpack-source call's ctor arg needs an arg temp, the unpack position does not thread `allow_temps`, and the gate admits the shape anyway; lowering builds a `THIRArgTemp` under the non-flushable statement and the post-lowering validator raises, so plain `tpyc --dump-code` exits 1 with `Internal error: main: THIRArgTemp at SourceLocation(...): THIRArgTemp under a non-flushable statement position` (re-reproduced 2026-09-02; originally probe-found while widening the tuple-return source gate, 2026-08-03, and verified pre-existing on `4b4983395`). This violates the stated lowering contract -- a shape lowering cannot handle must raise `ThirUnsupported`, which the fold point turns into a located `ThirRejectError`, never escape as an internal error. The general claim rides here: a too-strict validator RULE is a compiler crash on valid code, not a diagnostic. This entry is the only live holder of that claim -- its former sibling was withdrawn. **A SECOND node type reaches the same escape at the same position:** `a, b = send(b"hi")` where `send` takes a `bytes | dict[str, str] | None` -- the bytes literal needs a union-lift temp, and lowering builds a `THIRUnionArgLift` under the non-flushable unpack, dying with `Internal error: main: THIRUnionArgLift at SourceLocation(...): temp-bearing THIRUnionArgLift under a non-flushable statement position`. So the over-admission is not specific to `THIRArgTemp`: the unpack source's flushability is not threaded into ANY temp-bearing arg gate. Fix shape: thread the unpack source's flushability into the call-arg gate, so the gate refuses the temp-needing arg and the reject is reported at the blocking line. Routing the raise somewhere gentler is not an option -- with a single author a validator raise has nowhere to go, so per-RULE correctness is the only fix and every structural rule must be exactly as strict as the render actually requires. No corpus case holds either shape, and the unit that asserted the CURRENT raise went with the THIR unit suite; the two spellings above are the reproduction. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) An `@overload` impl whose isinstance dispatch sits BEHIND a live dynamic branch is a hard compile error for the statically-True stub.** `@overload def judge(a: Dog, n: int)` + `(a: Cat, n: int)` over `def judge(a: Dog | Cat, n: int): if n > 3: return 'big'; elif isinstance(a, Dog): return a.name; else: return str(a.lives)` -- the Dog stub resolves the isinstance True BEHIND the live `n > 3` branch, and lowering declines the fold rather than emit a body that silently drops the dynamic branch: `error: in function 'judge': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.if:if.overload_true_after_dynamic)`. `_lower_overload_folded_if` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:7166`, the `if.overload_true_after_dynamic` detail at `:7200`) admits a chain only when the True-resolved node has no live predecessor; the fix is to emit the live prefix and fold the True node into its else tail. Not exotic -- an early-out guard ahead of the isinstance dispatch is an ordinary way to write an overload impl -- so worth queueing. The unit fixture that pinned the reject went with the THIR unit suite. Surfaced designing the THIR live-chain mirror. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) BODIED `@overload` variants (mode b) with `Literal` params emit unmangled duplicate definitions while the CALL site references the mangled name -- the C++ never compiles.** Two bodied stubs `def k(a: Int32, m: Literal["fast"]) -> Int32: <body>` / `Literal["slow"]` emit as two identical `int32_t k(int32_t, std::string_view)` definitions (duplicate symbol), while the call `k(1, "fast")` emits `k__lit_fast(1, "fast")` -- a symbol nothing defines. The bodied-stub fall-through in `gen_function_def` never applies `literal_mangled_name`, but the call-site `is_literal_mangled` predicate keys only on "multi-overload + resolved fi has a Literal param" and fires regardless. Loud (duplicate definition + undefined reference), no corpus case (the shape cannot pass exec). Both paths emit identically -- THIR routes the call with the same mangled spelling via the shared helper, so this is AST-side, not a divergence. Fix shape: mangle bodied literal-stub DEFINITIONS with the same `literal_mangled_name` (definition + forward decl + cross-module attr spelling), or reject the bodied-Literal combination in sema. Repro: the two bodied `Literal` stubs above plus the `k(1, "fast")` call, through `--dump-code` (the unit that carried the source went with the THIR unit suite). Surfaced re-pinning the callee-reject units for the THIR literal-overload round. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) An augmented assignment through a CALL receiver (`o.get().v += 1`) double-evaluates the receiver call in generated C++ where CPython evaluates it once.** The aug-assign arm of `_lower_stmt` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` lowers `stmt.target` TWICE -- once as the assign lvalue, once as the binop's left operand (the `else` leg beside the class-constant `_lower_class_const_write_target` split) -- so `target OP= value` becomes `target = (target OP value)` with the receiver call spelled on both sides. Verified 2026-09-03: `uv run tpyc --dump-code` emits `o.get().v = (o.get().v) + (::tpy::BigInt(1));`, and `uv run tpy` reports 2 receiver calls where CPython reports 1. Unobserved in the corpus -- the only exercised receivers are pure accessors (Box.get), so the cpy phase stays green. Fix: evaluate the receiver once into a local and aug through the alias; the class-constant leg already splits its receiver eval off exactly once via `recv_eval`/`recv_wrap`, so extend that split to a general call receiver. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) Copying a non-copyable recursive-union member out of an accessor (`w = box.get()`) passes sema and fails only at g++.** A recursive-union wrapper (`type Value = int | str | Neg` where `Neg` owns a `@nocopy` `Box[Value]`) holds `Neg` by value in its `std::variant`, so `Neg`'s deleted copy ctor deletes `Value::Value(const Value&)` -- and a plain decl `w = n.inner.get()` (a borrow-returning accessor result copied into an owned local) emits `Value w = n.inner.get();`, which g++ rejects with `use of deleted function`. CPython runs the same line fine (it aliases). No front-end diagnostic points at the copy; contrast `error_union_box_field_copy`, which catches the structurally identical copy at a FIELD-assignment site -- the local-decl sink is missing the same check. Both codegen paths emit the identical (uncompilable) C++, so this is an AST-side sema gap, not a THIR divergence. Repro: the wrapper-accessor decl above run through the toolchain (probe left at `/tmp/agents/probe_wrapper_copy3.py`); the unit fixture that carried it went with the THIR unit suite. Fix shape: extend the union-member copy check that guards field assigns to owned-local decl (and likely return/arg storage) sinks. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the THIR receiver-row wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (ill-formed C++, no diagnostic) `is_type_non_copyable` has no `UnionType` arm, so a store into a field/container typed as a union of `@nocopy` members is never rejected.** [`union-nocopy-field-store`] With `A` and `B` both `@nocopy` and a field `u: A | B`, `self.u = tmp` emits `::tpy::to_value_variant<std::variant<A, B>>(tmp)` and dies in raw libstdc++ spew (`no matching function for call to 'std::variant<A, B>::variant(...)'` -- the variant's copy ctor is deleted because an alternative's is) with no TPy diagnostic. The structurally identical store into a `@nocopy` RECORD field IS rejected (`cannot copy non-copyable type 'Box[Expr]' into field`, pinned by `tests/cases/union/error_union_box_field_copy`), so this is one missing arm, not a policy. Both `tpyc/sema/context.py:1337` (`is_type_non_copyable`, which upgrades the copy WARNING to an error) and its narrower sibling `is_type_nocopy` (`:1296`) walk `Readonly` / `Own` / `Optional` / `Tuple` / `RecursiveAliasInstanceType` / dyn-protocol / record and then fall through to `get_record_for_type(<union>)` -> `None` -> `False`. The recursive-alias arm exists for exactly this reason (its comment: a non-copyable alternative propagates through the wrapper's `std::variant`), and a plain union lowers to a `std::variant` just the same. Sema-layer, so both codegen paths inherit it. Independent of the last-use copy-warning suppression: verified at the local's last use (no warning at all) and at a non-last use (warns `copies B into field` but never upgrades), both spewing. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Fix shape: give both helpers a `UnionType` arm returning True when any member is non-copyable. Repros `/tmp/agents/nocopyunion/main.py` (last use) and `/tmp/agents/nocopyunion2/main.py` (non-last use). Surfaced probing the field-store copy-warning suppression. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) `await` inside an `except ... as e:` handler body reads `e` out of scope in the generated coroutine.** The handler binding is a C++ `catch (const MyErr& e)` parameter, but the resumable frame splits the handler body at the suspension, so the post-resume code reads `e` from a later, disjoint `case` block after the catch scope has already exited -- g++ reports `'e' was not declared in this scope`. Idiomatic async retry/logging code (`try: await op() / except TimeoutError as e: await report(e)`) is valid Python and gets raw compiler spew. Root cause is that an except capture is never given frame storage: it lives only in the catch parameter, so it has nowhere to survive a suspension. The `with` member of this family is fixed -- a target is frame-resident unconditionally and the emit binds through that field -- and the remaining siblings are this one, which has no gate at all, and the match capture, whose `needs_frame_field` gate is still narrower than the construct (see the match entry below). Fix shape: give a handler binding read after a suspension a frame slot and copy the caught value into it at catch time, so the resume block reads the slot rather than the dead parameter. Note the capture must take an OWNING frame copy, not the aliasing form the `with` target uses: `_classify_pointer_alias_locals` deliberately excludes handler bindings because the caught object dies at handler end, so a pointer would dangle. Verified on master, independent of the capture-registration work. Three separate review passes converged on this same missing-frame-storage gap, of which this is the sharpest form. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (cpy stub divergence, blocks test coverage) The `lib/cpy` `Span` stub mis-bounds a span minted by `take_ptr(x).span(n)`, so the last element raises where TPy reads it fine.** `a = Array[Int32, 3]([10, 11, 12]); s = take_ptr(a[0]).span(3)` then `s[2]` prints `12` under TPy and raises `RuntimeError: span index out of bounds` under `PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3`, while `len(s)` reports `3` on both -- so the stub's length and its index bound disagree. Stub-only (`lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py` ~406, seen only by CPython), so it is a test-infrastructure defect rather than a compiler one, but it blocks cpy-comparing any case whose shape needs a pointer-minted Span: `control_flow/with_target_pointer_bearing_value` had to drop its `Span` half for exactly this reason (the shape is still covered by the compiler fix and a scratch probe, just not by an exec+cpy case). Repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/spanchk/main.py`. Surfaced authoring the pointer-bearing-value with-target case.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A simple-generator lambda does not capture a pre-loop `with ... as` target, so reading it inside the loop fails the C++ build.** `_build_capture_list` (`codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`) collects only `TpyVarDecl` names from the init statements preceding a simple generator's loop, so a `with Mgr() as m:` before the loop leaves `m` out of the capture list and the emitted lambda references it anyway -- g++ reports `'m' is not captured`. Toolchain-caught, not silent. Pre-existing and independent of the with-target storage work: the simple-generator peephole keeps its locals on the lambda stack rather than in a frame, so none of the frame-residency changes reach it (verified -- the peephole still emits `auto& m = __ctx_1.__enter__();`). Fix shape: collect every name BOUND by an init statement, not just var-decls -- a with target, a tuple-unpack target and a match capture have the same problem. Repro `/tmp/agents/mergecheck/simplegen_with.py`. Surfaced by the semantic-conflict pass of `/tpy-merge-master`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (inconsistent fact, no observable effect today) A `with ... as t` target records `Own[T]` as its frame-local type where an ordinary binding of the same value records `T`.** `def __enter__(self) -> Own[Item]` makes the target's `generator_locals` entry `Own[Item]`, while `t = make()` over the same `-> Own[Item]` function records `Item`. The storage consequence is closed -- the frame-layout plan now looks THROUGH `Own` at the object it names, so both spellings land on the same `frame_slot<Item>` field (before that, the target's `Own` read as a value type and took a bare field, which default-constructed at frame creation and so failed to build outright whenever `Item` held a non-default-constructible member such as a `Box`; pinned now by `control_flow/with_target_own_enter_no_default_ctor`). What remains is the recorded type itself: two different answers for the same value depending on how it was bound, which any future consumer keying on it would read differently. Fix shape: record `T` at the with target, matching the ordinary-binding spelling, and drop the plan's `Own` unwrap if nothing else needs it. Surfaced by the inverse test of the with-target storage fix.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A return-tier `try`/`except` in which EVERY path returns emits an unreachable fallthrough with no return, so `-Werror=return-type` rejects it.** `def outer(k: str) -> Int32: try: return inner(k) / except NotFound as e: return e.code` (with `inner` `@error_return`) emits the `goto`-based return tier ending `__after_try_1:; }` -- both real paths return, but the label is still a syntactic fallthrough point, so g++ reports "control reaches end of non-void function". A plain `uv run tpy` builds it (the harness compiles with warnings-as-errors, which is what surfaces it), so it bites the test suite and any `-Werror` build. Pre-existing and independent of name shadowing -- reproduced with a non-colliding binding, `/tmp/agents/scopens/p_rt_plain.py`. Existing return-tier corpus cases miss it because they re-raise or continue after the try rather than returning on every path. Workaround: assign in the handler and return after the try (what `tests/cases/name_shadowing/except_return_tier_shadow` does). Fix shape: emit an unreachable-return (or `__builtin_unreachable`) after the join label when every tier path terminates. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A `match` capture that persists past the match and is read by a LATER suspension gets no frame slot.** `needs_frame_field` (`sema/match.py:171-175`) only scans for suspensions inside the match statement's own arms, but a capture is an ordinary function local in Python and stays live afterwards -- so `case 5 as hit: ...` followed later in the body by `yield hit` leaves `hit` as a C++ local scoped to one switch-`case`, read out of scope from a later one. Undiagnosed C++ build failure. The predicate needs to ask whether the capture is read after any suspension anywhere in the body, not just within the match. Reproduced: `case 5 as hit: pass / case _ as hit: pass` then `yield 1` / `yield hit` gives `error: 'hit' was not declared in this scope` where CPython prints `1` then `5` -- repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/v_match_after.py`. Pre-existing (byte-identical on master). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `with ... as NAME` capture that reuses an already-bound name, and any `with` whose `__enter__` returns a tuple, are hard compile errors.** `x = 1` then `with Counter(5) as x:` (a `-> Counter` `__enter__`) prints `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.with)` -- valid Python, since CPython simply rebinds the name. A borrow-form TUPLE target is the second face and needs no reuse at all: `__enter__ -> tuple[Item, Int32]` bound by a single `with CM(base) as p:` rejects with the same bare `stmt.with`. `_lower_with` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:15100`) admits a fixed ladder of target rows -- plain non-value hoist, pointer predecl, the frame-resident flavors -- and raises `stmt_reject_reason(stmt)` with no detail for everything else, so the message names no shape. Two things are owed: a located TYPE diagnostic for the incompatible-type reuse (`_analyze_with` in `tpyc/sema/statements.py` still calls `current_scope.define` unconditionally, bypassing the reassignment-type-mismatch check that guards a plain `x = ...`), and a tuple-target row. The SAME-type value reuse this entry also covered is FIXED: `case 1 as v:` then `with CM(7) as v:` (a `-> Int32` `__enter__`) now emits `auto v = __ctx_1.__enter__();` in its own scope, builds and runs. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the with-target storage branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic) A read of a name shadowed by a later-arm `match` capture reports callability, not the shadowing.** `case Cat(lives=helper): ... / case Dog(): return helper()` where `helper` is also a module function reports `'helper' is not callable` -- correct to reject (CPython raises `UnboundLocalError`, since the capture makes the name a function-local), but the message names neither the `match` capture nor the scoping rule, so a user whose code compiled before this became reachable has no path from the message to the cause. Pinned by `tests/cases/name_shadowing/error_match_capture_shadows_function`. Fix shape: when the shadowing binding is a pattern capture, say so and point at the capture. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) A `match` capture does not make its name a function-local for the arms BEFORE it, so an earlier arm can still reach an outer binding of that name.** Python makes a capture pattern's name a function-local everywhere in the enclosing function, so any arm referencing it raises `UnboundLocalError` unless that arm bound it -- verified: `case Cat(lives=helper): ... / case Dog(): return helper()` raises in CPython. Arms AFTER the capture behave correctly (the binding is visible and the read is rejected); arms BEFORE it still resolve the name to the module-level function and silently succeed. Same family as the post-handler `except` read entry below: TPy models captures as block-scoped where Python scopes them to the function. Closing both means function-scoped capture locals (bind-then-mark-dead), a variable-model change tracked in TODO.md -- not a local patch, and NOT fixable by resetting the namespace per arm, which would re-break the after-arms case that now works. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (missing safety diagnostic) The unconsumed-`Own` warning is WHOLE-TUPLE granular, so a dropped owned ELEMENT is never reported.** A scalar `Own[T]` param that is never consumed warns (`Own[Box] param 'x' is never consumed`), and a fully-owned tuple param that is never touched warns (`owned tuple param 'p' is never consumed`) -- but the tuple form is an all-or-nothing check on the aggregate. Two shapes slip through, both verified: (1) a fully-owned tuple that IS unpacked but then drops an element (`a, b = p; sink(a)` -- `b` is never consumed, no warning), since unpacking alone counts as consuming the tuple; and (2) a MIXED `tuple[Own[A], B]` param whose owned element is never consumed, which warns nothing at all because it is not an "owned tuple param" to begin with. Under the elementwise rule (`TODO.md`) element `i` should behave as `Ti` would as a singleton at that position, and a singleton `Own[T]` param warns -- so both should. The remediation is the same one the scalar warning implies: drop the `Own` from that element and take a borrow. Note shape (2) additionally cannot be consumed even if you try (see the mixed-param consume entry above), but the warning is a separate defect: it is missing for shape (1) too, where consumption works fine. The `local` position already gets this right for tuples (`std::tuple<Box*, Box*>`, aliases, verified 42), so the global slot simply fails to follow the local's borrow form. Element form matters: value / `int` / `str` / `bytes` / `Own` globals are all correct at both arities -- only a reference-type element diverges. **A SECOND, sharper symptom on the same root cause: an alias into the tuple FOLLOWS A REBIND of the global.** `g: tuple[Int32, Cell] = (1, Cell(5))` then, under `global g`, `c = g[1]` / `g = (123, Cell(9))` / `print(c.v)` prints TPy **9** and CPython **5** -- `c` binds a `Cell&` into the tuple's storage, so rebinding the global overwrites that storage in place and every live alias silently observes the new object, where CPython keeps the old one alive. Root cause is the global classification asking whether the WHOLE type is a value type (`pointer_globals` in `codegen_cpp/generator.py`) -- a tuple answers yes even when every element is a reference, so it can never become a borrow slot. Fixing it is not that predicate: a borrow-form global needs the local's machinery mirrored at global scope (`_global_cpp_type` emitting `tuple_borrow_cpp`, the matching `extern`, `->` element reads, the assign lifting a storage source to pointer form, const-element handling, cross-module externs). Note the wave did not simply inherit the MIXED shape here -- `G: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(B)` failed the C++ build before it and copies silently after, so the wave converted a loud error into a silently wrong program and made this sink reachable. (The all-borrow `(V, V)` shape was already silent.) A wave turning a loud error into a silent one is what raises a cell to HIGH, and the argument applies with more force here. Pinned by `tests/cases/tuple/element_vs_singleton_global`, which records the wrong-but-shipping output (TPy `42 2 2`; CPython prints `42 43 44`, which is what FULL parity requires. If the mixed-stays-storage carve-out survives its re-justification the fix lands on `42 43 2` instead, leaving the mixed element diverging -- so the endpoint is conditional on that decision, not settled) so the fix has a regression target; that case's expectations flip when the global slot learns the local's borrow form. Fixing this bug would make the marker HARDER, not easier: it invalidates the working arm and churns two currently-green routed cases. Repros `/tmp/agents/mixstep1/lostwrite.py` (silent lost write), `consume.py` (the copy), `nocopy_unpack.py` (build failure). Raised LOW -> HIGH once the lost write was measured -- a measured silent wrong answer is the criterion, the same one that raised the module-global entry above. Surfaced by the tuple-element-vs-singleton census; the consume mechanism found reading the pinned diag of `mixed_own_tuple_param_from_call`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic) A missing MEMBER on `cls` inside a @classmethod reports the `cls`-as-a-value message instead of naming the member.** `cls.NOPE` where `NOPE` is not a class constant / ClassVar falls out of the class-member resolution path and reaches the bare-name value read, so the user gets "'cls' can only be used to construct ('cls(...)') or to access class members ('cls.NAME') -- passing or returning a class as a value needs 'type[T]'" when their actual mistake is a typo'd member name. Correct and located, just pointed at the wrong thing; the equivalent through the class NAME (`P.NOPE`) names the member. Fix shape: resolve the field against the record before falling through to the value read, so the miss reports the member. Surfaced probing `cls` in non-construct contexts on the classmethod branch.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid) Binding an `except ... as` capture to a local alias fails the C++ build -- the catch parameter is `const` but the alias decl is a non-const reference.** `except MyError as exc: e = exc` emits `MyError& e = exc;` while the handler catches `const MyError&`, so g++ rejects with "binding reference of type 'MyError&' to 'const MyError' discards qualifiers". Toolchain-caught, not silent. Reading a FIELD off the capture (`exc.code`) is fine -- only binding the whole object to a local trips it. Verified byte-identical with and without the capture-registration fix, so it is independent of name shadowing: reproducer `/tmp/agents/scopens/p_alias.py` (a 3-line handler, no name collision). Fix shape: either the alias decl follows the catch parameter's const-ness, or the handler catches by mutable reference where the binding is later aliased -- the decl and the catch signature must agree. Surfaced while probing the capture-registration fix (the fix moved resolution far enough to reach codegen, exposing this). Note for whoever fixes it: `tests/cases/name_shadowing/except_capture_shadows_class` is read-only because mutating through the capture trips exactly this bug -- once it is fixed, that case wants a mutate-and-observe assertion so the boundary stops being parity-blind if catch ever becomes by-value.
- **[LOW small] (accepts invalid) Reading an `except ... as NAME` capture AFTER its handler resolves to whatever NAME meant outside instead of raising.** CPython makes the capture a function-scoped local and deletes it at handler end, so a later read is `UnboundLocalError`; TPy unbinds the capture from the local namespace, which re-exposes the outer binding (a module-level class of that name, say) and the read silently succeeds. Probe: a class `Reg` with `code = 999` plus `except MyError as Reg: inside = Reg.code` then `return inside + Reg.code` prints 1006 under TPy where CPython raises. Accepts-invalid on pathological input, and the value read inside the handler is correct (that was the shadowing bug, fixed) -- only the post-handler region diverges. Closing it means modelling Python's function-scoped locals for captures (bind-then-mark-dead rather than unbind), which is a variable-model change, not a local patch: TPy's whole local model is block-scoped. Surfaced by the capture-registration fix.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) Binding `it = iter(c)` / `it = c.__iter__()` for a class whose `__iter__` returns `self` COPIES the object instead of aliasing it.** The standard "class is its own iterator" idiom: CPython gives `it is c`, so advancing `it` mutates `c`; TPy decls `auto it = ::tpy::__iter__(c);` where the helper returns `decltype(auto)` (a `Counter&`) but plain `auto` strips the reference -- a value copy, so mutations through `it` are invisible on `c`. Verified by probe: `PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3` prints `2`, `uv run tpy` prints `0` (advance via `it`, then read `c`'s counter). The `for x in c:` loop idiom is unaffected (verified separately). Shared by BOTH emit paths -- THIR's `_protocol_auto_slot` decl arm mirrors the AST's `_cpp_decl_type` `auto` spelling byte-identically -- and concealed in the corpus because `iterators/iter_next_builtin` never re-reads `c` after binding `it` (a parity-blind read-only shape). Fix shape: the protocol-typed iterator decl needs the reference-preserving spelling (`auto&&`, or `decltype(auto)`) when the init is a borrow-returning `__iter__`; both paths must change together (byte-identity), and the concealing test wants a mutate-after-bind observation. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) on `thir-decl-slot-track`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A callable PARAM or local invoked under a name that also names a module function is a hard compile error.** `def f() -> None: ...` + `def apply(f: Fn[[Int32], Int32], v: Int32) -> Int32: return f(v)` prints `error: in function 'apply': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (expr.call:call.callable_shadow)`. Sema resolves the callable BINDING correctly (CPython scoping: the param shadows); lowering declines rather than emit the module function's call -- `note_detail("call.callable_shadow")`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:7473`. Everyday shape -- a callback param named `f` / `key` / `filter` alongside a module function of the same name -- so worth queueing. Same family as the nested-def builtin-shadow reject (`call.closure_import_shadow`, a closure shadowing an imported or builtin name). Fix shape: consult the local binding before the module/builtin registry lookup, and take the BINDING's params for the arg zip. Surfaced pinning the callable-field arg row. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent, unverified] `get_resolved_type`'s `var_types` short-circuit now resolves pending CONTAINER types too, and no test exercises that half.** The short-circuit was fixed to route through `resolve_type()` so a tuple-unpack target's `PendingStrType` no longer leaks out unresolved; `resolve_type()` also resolves `PendingListType`/`PendingDictType`/`PendingSetType`. That is the architecturally right chokepoint (the non-`var_types` path has always resolved both), but the container half is a behavior widening nobody has a witness for. The specific worry is one level down, in `_resolve_pending_container`'s BEST-EFFORT fallback (`make_list(elem)` / `make_dict` / `make_set`, taken when sema's resolution never ran). Before this change that path could not be reached from the short-circuit, so an unresolved pending list surfaced as a LOUD `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen` crash; now it can silently become `list[T]` where the truth is `Array[T, N]` -- a reference-vs-value guess, and a copy-vs-alias decision keyed on it would be a SILENT divergence, the project's most serious class. (The resolved answer itself is the truthful one -- returning it is strictly better than returning the raw pending node, which is why the fix is not to narrow the resolution back to views.) A whole-corpus comp run over both variants (view-only vs container-inclusive) produced byte-IDENTICAL output, and a review pass could not construct a reachable case across ~89 `get_resolved_type` call sites, so there is no evidence of a live defect -- this is filed because "unverified across 89 call sites" is exactly what resurfaces later as an aliasing bug, not because a symptom exists. Fix shape if a witness appears: audit the call sites that ask `is_value_type()` / a value-vs-reference question about a `var_types` entry, rather than narrowing the resolution back to views. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity, self-tagged low confidence) on `fix-pending-view-unpack`.
- **[MED small] (wrong answer from a type predicate, latent) `Own[T]` reports `is_trivially_destructible() == True` for every `T`, so `Own[bytes]` / `Own[list[int]]` claim to be cheap heap-free value types.** `OwnType.is_value_type()` returns `True` unconditionally (deliberate -- documented as "Own[T] uses T&& at param boundaries; treat as value type for other purposes", `tpyc/typesys.py:1673`), and `is_expensive_copy()` is NOT overridden, so it falls through to the base implementation whose `_nominal_td()` is None for a wrapper type and returns `False`. `is_trivially_destructible()` is `is_value_type() and not is_expensive_copy()` (`tpyc/typesys.py:523`), so it is `True and not False` regardless of the wrapped type -- confirmed directly: `OwnType(NominalType('builtins.bytes')).is_trivially_destructible()` is True where the bare `bytes` answers False. Any consumer asking an `Own[T]` whether a move is cheap gets the wrong answer; the live consumer is `_del_var_trivial` (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:584`, the `del x` emit-nothing skip), not confirmed reachable with an OwnType, hence latent rather than a live miscompile. Found the hard way: a candidate fix for the `_maybe_move` frame-local regression used `is_trivially_destructible()` directly and silently kept dropping the move on `Own[bytes]`; the shipped fix unwraps `Own` explicitly to sidestep this, which is a workaround at the consumer, not a fix. Fix shape: forward `is_expensive_copy()` (and probably `is_trivially_destructible()`) to `self.wrapped` on `OwnType` -- but check each existing consumer first, since `is_value_type()`'s unconditional `True` is load-bearing at param boundaries and the three predicates are entangled. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH medium] (silent CPython divergence) A local's type is inferred from its PRE-LOOP binding only; a back-edge widening (`z = z + 1.5`) leaves dependent locals typed at the stale width and silently truncates.** `z = 0` then in a loop `sq = z * z; z = z + 1.5`: `z` itself widens to `double`, but `sq` keeps the pre-loop `Int32` inference, so codegen emits `mul_check<int32_t>(z, z)` narrowing BOTH operands -- CPython prints `0, 2.25, 9.0`, TPy prints `0, 1, 9` (repro `/tmp/agents/loopwiden.py`, verified). Compiles clean, NO warning -- exactly the CPython-divergence case goal #5 promises to flag; in a mandelbrot port this made all 6084 points test in-set (solid `#` block). Fix shape, two independent parts: (1) body type inference needs a fixed point over the loop back-edge before dependent locals are typed (the real fix); (2) regardless, a float->int operand narrowing at a checked-arith emit site should WARN -- the silent `mul_check<int32_t>(double, double)` coercion is never intended. Sibling entry: the LOUD flavor of stale-width re-assignment ("A PLAIN re-assignment that widens an inferred-`Int32` variable to `BigInt` emits invalid C++") -- same missing-widening root, there caught by g++, here silently miscompiled, so a shared fix should close both. Workaround: initialize `z = 0.0`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (inference architecture). Surfaced porting mandelbrot.
- **[HIGH small] (rejects-valid) `input(prompt)` is rejected -- "No matching overload for input(str)"; only the bare `input()` overload exists.** Textbook first-program Python (`name = input("your name: ")`) fails with an opaque overload error that never says the prompt form is unsupported. Bare `input()` works (verified; probe `/tmp/agents/inp.py`). Fix shape: add the one-arg overload to the `input` stub (write the prompt to stdout without a trailing newline, flush, then read the line -- CPython semantics), which also retires the diagnostic problem; if the overload is deferred for any reason, the minimum is a located "input(prompt) is not supported yet" message. Was previously tracked only as a RELEASE_PLAN bullet; filed here per the bugs-block-releases rule. Surfaced planning 0.6.0.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) An unbound-self read of a `@native`-RENAMED base field is a hard compile error.** `BaseA.x` inside a descendant method, where `BaseA` is `@native` with `x: Int32 = native_field("m_x")`, dies with `error: in function 'read': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return:field.receiver_shape)` (verified 2026-09-03 with `uv run tpyc --dump-code`). `_unbound_self_field_ok` in `tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py` refuses the shape outright when `e.native_field_name is not None`, deferring to a renderer that no longer exists; the plain non-native sibling compiles fine to `this->BaseA::x`. Fix: spell the rename in the unbound-self render (`this->{parent}::{native_field_name}`) and drop the predicate's `native_field_name` exclusion. Exotic shape -- an `@native` base carrying a per-field rename, read unbound from a subclass method; no corpus witness. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Printing a NARROWED value-repr `Optional[scalar]` module GLOBAL emits the bare optional.** `g: Int32 | None = 5` then `if g is not None: print(g)` emits `std::cout << g` where `g` is `std::optional<int32_t>`, which has no `operator<<` -- the C++ build fails. The same construct on a LOCAL or a param renders `print_optional_val(g)` correctly, so it is the module-global binding that misses the narrowed-read wrap. Loud, pre-existing (reproduces on master), no corpus witness. Note the THIR overlay already emits the CORRECT `print_optional_val(g)` here, so this is one of the few places the two paths disagree with THIR being right; the field-write/containers wave widened admission enough that more bodies containing this construct now route, which is how it was found (no in-corpus case newly routes -- the whole-corpus byte-diff stayed green). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A `nonlocal` rebind inside a NESTED DEF escapes a loop-body local past the loop without tripping the scope-escape reject.** `saved = Point(-1); for i in range(3): p = Point(i); def capture(): nonlocal saved; saved = p` + `if i == 0: capture(); p.x = 99` prints TPy `0`, CPython `99`, with no diagnostic. `check_escape` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) runs only at the two `TpyName`-target assignment sites in `tpyc/sema/statements.py`, and `nested_def_scope` resets `var_scope_depth` for the nested body, so the depth comparison never sees the outer name; codegen emits a plain value copy of a stale `p` where CPython aliases. Same family as the rejected direct spelling (`pointers/error_escape_loop_body`), just routed through one level of nested-def indirection. Pre-existing (the call sites are unchanged by the reject). Fix shape: treat a nested def's `nonlocal` write of an outer name as an assignment at the OUTER depth, so the escape check sees it -- the same detection gap as the nonlocal match-capture rebind entry below. Probe `/tmp/agents/escapekey/rev/closure.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the scope-escape reject. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent UB + doubled side effects) A WALRUS iterable in a RESUMABLE `for` head is rendered TWICE, so its side effect runs twice and the loop's `begin()` iterator points into destroyed storage.** `for q in (zs := make_list(i)):` inside a generator emits `__for_it_0.emplace((zs.emplace(make_list(i))).begin());` followed by `__for_end_0.emplace((zs.emplace(make_list(i))).end());` -- `make_list` runs twice per loop entry (CPython evaluates the iterable once), and the second `emplace` destroys the payload whose `begin()` was just stored, so a `std::vector` payload leaves the iterator dangling. A plain CALL iterable is unaffected: it materializes once into `__for_src_N` and begin/end read `(*__for_src_N)`, which is exactly the treatment the walrus source is missing -- the for-head classifies a walrus iterable as an lvalue-ish source and re-renders it per iterator bind. Silent (no diagnostic; an `std::array` payload happens to survive because the storage address is stable, which is why the corpus does not show it). Pre-existing on the AST path; THIR mirrors it byte-identically (the frame-walrus row routes the shape).
