Fix shape: treat a walrus iterable like an rvalue source -- materialize into `__for_src_N` once (or render the walrus once and bind begin/end off the target field). Probes `/tmp/agents/cell-walrus/p15_foreach_walrus_call.py` (side effect, vector payload) and `p13_foreach_slot.py` (brace-init payload). Surfaced by the THIR frame-walrus row's witness hunt. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.

- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A WALRUS-bound loop-body local escapes past the loop without tripping the scope-escape reject.** `saved = (p := Point(i))` inside a loop body, with `saved` declared outside it, compiles clean and prints TPy `2`, CPython `99` after a `p.x = 99` in the same iteration. `is_scope_escape` resolves its source through `TpyName` / `TpyFieldAccess` / `TpySubscript` only, so a `TpyNamedExpr` source is never walked and `check_escape` is not reached; the walrus codegen then materializes an independent copy where CPython aliases. Pre-existing and untouched by the reject. Fix shape: resolve a `TpyNamedExpr` source to its bound name in `_get_source_name` / `get_expr_scope_depth` so the walrus form takes the same path as the bare name. Probe `/tmp/agents/escapekey/rev/walrus.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the scope-escape reject. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (warned wrong output) A loop-body local captured CONDITIONALLY mid-loop observes the LAST iteration's value, not the captured one.** `saved = Point(0); for i in range(3): p = Point(i); if i == 0: saved = p` then `return saved.x` gives TPy `2`, CPython `0`. The loop-body local's storage is hoisted to ONE function-scope slot, so every iteration emplaces over the same object and an alias taken earlier follows it. WARNED since the escape diagnostic was reworded to state the consequence ("'saved' will not keep the object it was given") and name `copy()`, so this is an acknowledged divergence rather than a silent one -- but the emitted program is still wrong for anyone who does not act on the warning. Needs no post-loop code, which makes it the most reachable shape of the family. Reproduces identically in a generator/frame context. Fixing it needs per-iteration storage: a slot per BINDING still leaves iterations of one binding sharing a slot. Two mechanisms were prototyped and discarded (see TODO.md) -- a two-slot rotation and a move-at-escape. Repro:
  ```python
  saved = Point(0)
  for i in range(3):
      p = Point(i)
      if i == 0:
          saved = p
  return saved.x   # TPy 2, CPython 0
  ```
  Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the block-local scope-revoke branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Rebinding a loop-body-hoisted record local AFTER the loop is a hard compile error.** `for i in xs: p = Point(i)` then a READ of `p` after the loop (which hoists it to function scope) followed by `p = Point(9)` dies with `error: in function 'main': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.for_each:foreach.hoist_type)` (verified 2026-09-03 with `uv run tpyc --dump-code`); the same loop WITHOUT the post-loop rvalue rebind compiles clean, as does the in-loop alias `saved = p` on its own. The reject is the for-head hoist ladder in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` (`note_detail("foreach.hoist_type")`), whose `_try_hoist_type_ok` / `_opt_storage_hoist_flavor` rungs admit no flavor for a hoisted record local that also needs a rebind slot. Behind the reject sits the ORIGINAL defect, now hidden rather than fixed: the post-loop rebind reused the single hoisted slot, clobbering the object an earlier `saved = p` alias pointed at -- TPy `saved.x == 9`, CPython `2`. **The obvious fix does not work -- do not re-attempt it without reading this.** A slot per rebind SITE fixes the aliasing (probe goes 9 -> 2) but slot REUSE is what destroys the old object eagerly the way CPython's refcount drop does; with a slot per site the old object survives to function exit and `cases/records/destructor_reassign` flips from `drop b | alive: c` to `alive: c | drop b`. The two properties are in tension under a static slot model -- a real fix needs liveness/escape information at the rebind site, or heap storage. Verified by implementing and reverting it (2026-07-27). Everyday shape -- worth queueing. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A local declared ABOVE a loop, aliased by another local and then rebound, still overwrites the alias -- the single-slot clobber reached without a scope escape.** `saved = Point(-1); p = Point(-1); for i in range(3): p = Point(i); saved = p` then `p = Point(9)` gives TPy `9`, CPython `2`. Moving the `p = ...` declaration INSIDE the loop body makes the same program REJECTED (the scope-escape error), so the two spellings disagree on whether the program is even legal -- and the legal one is the wrong one. Hoisting a declaration out of a loop is a routine edit, which is what makes this a trap. `check_escape` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) keys on scope DEPTH, and here source and target are both function-scope, so no escape is recorded and the local keeps one reused rebind slot. The straight-line form without a loop (`p = Point(5); saved = p; p = Point(9)`) is correct -- `p`'s separate rebind slot covers it -- so the loop is what collapses the two bindings onto one slot. Fix shape: the escape check must key on an ALIAS fact (is a live name pointing at this local's storage at the rebind?) rather than scope depth -- the borrow tracker is the natural owner. Being conservative is cheap here: the outcome is a reject, so over-approximating costs false positives, not wrong code. Pre-existing: reproduces identically on master (verified at f74bbacec). Probe `/tmp/agents/escapekey/loopsame.py`. Surfaced writing the escaped-local rotation tests. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (CPython-parity gap in the stubs, not the compiler) A `Deref` type's transparent dereference is TPy-only -- the `lib/cpy` stub forwards no attribute access, so the same source raises `AttributeError` under CPython.** `r = Rc.new(Point(1)); r.x` reads the payload's field in TPy (`__deref__`), but `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`'s `Deref` protocol only declares `__deref__` and nothing forwards `__getattr__`/`__setattr__`, so CPython looks the attribute up on the handle and fails. Affects every `Deref` type the stubs expose (`Rc`, `Arc`, `Box`, the `Mutex`/`RwLock` guards), so any test using the idiomatic spelling needs `no_cpython.txt` -- which costs exactly the parity check such a test exists to provide (`pointers/escape_explicit_rc`). Fix shape: give the stub `Deref` base a `__getattr__`/`__setattr__` that forwards to the payload, mirroring TPy's implicit deref. Surfaced writing the escape-reject's escape-hatch coverage. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A reference-typed for-loop variable READ after the loop and then reassigned fails the C++ build -- `cannot convert 'const Point' to ...`.** `for p in points: print(p.x)` + `print(p.x)` + `p = Point(9)`: the trailing read forces sema's pending-loop-var promotion, and the promoted (pre-declared) binding is emitted const, so the later rebind cannot assign it. Without the read the same rebind compiles and runs correctly (the block-local scope-revoke path gives it a fresh declaration), so the PROMOTION path is the broken one -- which is why block-local reassignment was NOT routed through promotion. CPython accepts the program (prints 1 2 2 9). Loud, pre-existing: reproduces identically on master. Probe `/tmp/agents/twoobj/promote.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) An `int | None`-annotated local initialized from an `Int32`-typed expression is rejected -- `Type mismatch in variable 'v': expected int | None, got Int32 | None`.** `v: int | None = i if flag else None` (with `i: Int32` from `range`) fails, though the un-annotated `int` sibling widens fine and `v: int | None = None` followed by `v = 9` compiles. The BigInt-vs-IntN widening that applies to a bare `int` target is not applied through the `| None` union arm, so the ternary's `Int32 | None` never widens to `int | None`. Loud (sema-rejected). Pre-existing: reproduces identically on master. Probe `/tmp/agents/loophoist/optloop.py`. Surfaced adding Optional-typed coverage to the block-local scope-revoke tests (which use `str | None` instead to route around it). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A local first declared in a try's `else` body and ASSIGNED after the try emits a `goto` across its initialization.** `try: ... except E: pass else: n = 7` then `n = 9` after the try. Every other block-emitting statement revokes its declarations at the block close so the post-block assignment declares the function-scope local (`cases/control_flow/block_local_reassign_after`), but the `else` body emits UNBRACED in the enclosing C++ scope with the handlers' `goto __after_else_N` jumping past it, so a fresh declaration there is crossed by the jump -- g++: `jump to label '__after_else_1' crosses initialization of 'int32_t n'`. Site: `_emit_try_except` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py:2796`) writes the else body at the ENCLOSING `level` and appends `{label}:;` after it (`:2830`). Fix shape: brace the else body (`{ ... }` with the label outside) and scope-revoke it like the other blocks. NB that brace changes emitted C++ for every try/else case (4 snapshots: `control_flow/try_except_shapes`, `control_flow/with_exit_isinstance_class_dispatch`, `exceptions/throw_else`, `exceptions/throw_else_var`). Repro:
  ```python
  try:
      print(100 // d)
  except ZeroDivisionError:
      pass
  else:
      n = 7
  n = 9        # g++: jump to label '__after_else_1' crosses initialization
  ```
 Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent UAF, garbage output) A generator's captured pointer aiming at a local of the FACTORY function reads destroyed storage: the factory returns before the closure is ever pulled.** `def gen(n): p = Point(1); p = Point(7); i = 0; while i < n: yield p.x; i += 1` captures `p` by value into the `make_generator` closure while `p` points at a `__slot_N` local to `gen`, which dies when `gen` returns -- TPy prints garbage (`398837392 ...`) where CPython prints `7 7 7`. No scope MISMATCH occurs (the slot is reserved and consumed in the same scope), so the cross-scope reject in `use_rebind_slot` does not see it; the unsoundness is the broader "a captured pointer outlives its slot", of which the reject covers only the mismatched slice. Pre-existing and byte-identical to master. Silent: no diagnostic, garbage output. The method-generator spelling is affected identically. Fix shape: the same init-capture that would give the slot closure lifetime (filed in TODO.md), or extend the reject to any rebind slot whose pointer is captured by an escaping closure. `generators/rebind_slot_in_generator` deliberately does NOT cover this shape. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid on clang, warns on gcc) A generator's capture list is built with no dedup, so a rebound init-statement local is captured twice.** `_build_capture_list` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`) appends one capture per init-stmt `TpyVarDecl`, so `p = Point(11); p = Point(12)` before a generator's loop emits `[n, p, p, i]() mutable`. GCC only warns (`already captured 'p'`); **clang treats a duplicate capture as an error**, so the shape is a hard build failure on a supported toolchain -- and CI's gcc-only default hides it. Pre-existing. Fix: dedup by name when assembling the list. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A local declared and rvalue-rebound entirely INSIDE a nested `def` gets no rebind slot, so an alias to its first value is clobbered.** `scan_reassigned_vars` (`tpyc/prescan.py`) builds `rvalue_reassigned` as a flat per-function name set and does NOT recurse into nested defs, so the inner body inherits the OUTER function's set: the inner local gets a separate rebind slot only when its name happens to COLLIDE with an enclosing rvalue-reassigned name. Non-colliding is the common case and is wrong: `def inner(): q = Point(1); alias = q; q = Point(100); alias.bump(); return alias.x + q.x` returns 202 where CPython gives 102 (the rebind reuses `q`'s storage, so `alias` observes the new value). Silent: no diagnostic, wrong output. Pre-existing (reproduces on master). Same root cause as the `nonlocal` sibling already filed. Fix shape: make the prescan recurse per nested-def scope instead of sharing the enclosing set -- which reserves a slot for every rvalue-rebound nested-def local, not only the name-colliding ones. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A nested `def`'s local whose name shadows a resumable frame field is emitted as a write to the FRAME field, so calling the closure clobbers the generator's own variable.** Same prescan-scope root cause as the entry above: the nested body is rendered against the enclosing resumable's local classification, so `p = ...` inside the nested def lowers to `p.emplace(...)` on the frame member rather than a fresh local. Reported by the /tpy-ready second opinion with a probe; the shape's argument-evaluation order makes which wrong value surfaces nondeterministic, so treat the exact output as unstable. NOT independently reproduced here -- confirm before fixing.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) The rvalue rebind slot is allocated unconditionally, so a superseded value stays alive in the init slot until function exit instead of dropping at the rebind.** The split exists so an alias to the init value is not overwritten, but it is gated on rvalue-reassignment alone -- `needs_rebind = stmt.name in lc.prescan.rvalue_reassigned` at the pointer-local decl arms in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`, carried on `THIRPtrLocalDecl.needs_rebind_slot` and turned into the extra `std::optional<T> __slot_N;` by the `THIRPtrLocalDecl` arm of `tpyc/thir/emit.py` -- and whether anything actually aliases the value is never asked. So `r = Noisy("a"); r = Noisy("b")` with no alias emits TWO slots (`Noisy __slot_1 = Noisy("a"); Noisy* r = &__slot_1; r = &*(__slot_2 = Noisy("b"));`): `b` lands in the rebind slot while `a` sits in the init slot until scope end. Verified 2026-09-03 -- `uv run tpy` prints `alive: b / drop a / drop b` where CPython prints `drop a / alive: b / drop b`. `records/destructor_reassign` shows the three-assign form: TPy `drop b / alive: c / drop a / drop c`, CPython `drop a / drop b / alive: c / drop c`. Gating the split on the init value actually being aliased would emit ONE slot for the unaliased case, whose move-assign destroys the superseded value at exactly the CPython point -- so this is a parity fix, not just one fewer live object per rebind. It should retire `destructor_reassign`'s `no_cpython.txt` and the `no_cpython` marker any equivalent block-scoped case would need. Secondary, decide after the slot count is right: a held-back declaration always lands in the FUNCTION prologue, so a slot reserved inside an `if`/loop body outlives that body; for the unaliased single-slot form function scope is what parity wants anyway, but a genuinely block-local slot could stay in its block. Pinned by `records/rebind_slot_block_scope_drop` and `records/destructor_reassign`, whose `no_cpython.txt` markers both name this entry and are expected to be retired by the fix.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, declared) A superseded rvalue payload in a resumable per-site frame slot lives until FRAME destruction instead of dropping at the supersede.** The frame twin of the entry above: `_prescan_resumable_ptr_slots` gives each rvalue write into a pointer-form frame local its own `std::optional<T>` frame field, so when a DIFFERENT site's write supersedes the logical variable, the earlier site's payload is never revisited -- `saved = Resource(1); yield; saved = Resource(2)` prints `1 2 drop2 drop1 done` where CPython prints `1 drop1 2 drop2 done`. A same-site loop rebind is correct (the re-executed assignment destroys the prior payload). Structurally worse than sync's two-slot cap (one field per site), but chosen deliberately: the sync per-NAME shared slot carries the open alias-clobber family (the entries below), a per-site sync fix was implemented and REVERTED 2026-07-27 (see the loop-predecl entry's warning), and the frame path's incumbent was a silent UAF -- aliasing correctness won. Pinned by `generators/gen_ptr_slot_drop_timing` (`no_cpython.txt` names this entry). The shared fix with the entry above is a liveness/alias-gated slot model; both markers retire with it. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + safety-model) of the frame ptr-slot placement fix.
- **[MED small] (rejects valid, loud) A tuple-unpack of an `Own[Optional[T]]`-element call result onto a pointer-form Optional frame local fails the C++ build: the unpack temp is pointer-lifted, then the frame arm can't convert.** In a generator/async body, `saved, extra = make_pair(9)` (returning `tuple[Own[Optional[Point]], Int32]`, `saved: Optional[Point]` pre-declared) emits `auto __tup_1 = ::tpy::tuple_to_pointer<std::tuple<Point*, int32_t>>(make_pair(9));` -- the owning call result is converted to BORROW form at the unpack temp -- and the frame unpack arm then emits `saved = ::tpy::optional_to_ptr(std::get<0>(__tup_1));`, which does not compile (`optional_to_ptr` has no `T*` overload). Even if it converted, the pointer would aim into the conversion's dying temporary. The SYNC path for the same source works (it materializes the storage tuple and moves the element into a persistent rebind slot). Fix shape: form selection, not a slot patch -- the unpack temp must stay STORAGE form when any target is a pointer-form frame field (then the element copies into a per-site frame slot like the scalar rvalue writes), which intersects the mixed-Own-tuple per-element form work. Probe `/tmp/agents/probe1/main.py` (sync twin in `main2.py`). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the frame ptr-slot placement fix, which initially misread it as a silent UAF -- the toolchain catches it. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) An owning `frame_slot<T>` generator local aliased by another local and then rebound clobbers the alias -- the non-Optional sibling of the fixed pointer-form placement bug.** `p = Point(1)` (a non-Optional reference-type local, stored `frame_slot<Point>` in the frame), `saved = p`, then `p = Point(2)`: the rebind emplaces into the SAME frame slot, so `saved` observes the new object where CPython keeps the old one alive through the alias. Reproduces identically on master (pre-existing, not introduced by the ptr-slot placement fix, which covers only pointer-form locals). Same single-storage-clobber family as the sync rebind-slot entries below, at the frame's owning-slot tier. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the frame ptr-slot placement fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) The separate-rebind-slot protection against alias clobbering is missing at MODULE scope and inside a NESTED `def`.** Same single-slot-clobber family as the loop-predecl and declared-above-a-loop entries above, same mechanism (a rebind reuses the single init slot, overwriting the object an earlier alias points at) in two more scopes that never register a separate slot: (a) module scope -- `p = Point(1); alias = p; if flag: p = Point(10)` emits `p = &(__global_slot_1 = Point(10));` so `alias.bump()` then reports `alias: 11 p: 11` where CPython gives `alias: 2 p: 10`; (b) a nested `def` -- the inner body reuses the OUTER function's prescan sets, so the rebind is never classified as rvalue-reassigned at all, and `p = Point(1); a = p; p = Point(9); a.bump()` reports `a: 10 p: 10` where CPython gives `a: 2 p: 9`. Ordinary function locals are correct -- `ctx.declare_rebind_slot` reserves the separate slot for exactly this reason -- so the fix is to make these two paths reach it. Silent: no diagnostic, wrong output. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the held-back rebind-slot declaration change.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A record local declared inside a TOP-LEVEL loop body is emitted as a C++ function-local `static`, so it is constructed ONCE and every later iteration reuses the stale object.** At module scope the slot carries `static` so it outlives `__tpy_init` (`slots.global_scope`), but inside a top-level `while`/`for` body that makes the initializer run only on the first pass: `i = 0` / `while i < 3: q = Point(i * 10); print(q.x); i += 1` emits `static Point __global_slot_1 = Point(i * 10);` and prints `0, 1, 2` (the value carried over and mutated) where CPython prints `0, 10, 20`. Silent: no diagnostic, wrong output. The same code inside a `def` is correct -- only module-level loops are affected, so it is easy to miss. A loop-local at module scope needs a non-static slot scoped to the loop body (or a static slot plus a per-iteration assignment), not a static initializer. Found probing `declare_rebind_slot`'s global-scope branch for test coverage.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `match`-arm local READ after the match is pre-declared at the wrong width -- `cannot convert 'tpy::BigInt' to 'int32_t' in assignment`.** `match c: case 1: n = c + 1 ... case _: n = 0` then `return n` (with `c: int`) pre-declares the merged local as `int32_t` while the arm assigns the `BigInt`-typed expression, so g++ rejects. The loop-body flavor of the same read-after promotion picks the right type; only the match-arm branch-decl merge is wrong. Loud (toolchain-caught), pre-existing and unchanged by the block-local scope-revoke fix. Probe `/tmp/agents/loophoist/m_read.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A `for`, `with ... as` or `match`-capture binding whose target is `global`-declared writes a function-LOCAL shadow, so the module variable never changes.** `global g` then `for g in range(7, 8): pass` emits `for (int32_t g = 7; ...)`, `with CM() as g:` emits `auto g = __ctx_1.__enter__();`, and `case g:` binds an arm local -- in each the write is invisible to every other function (probes under `/tmp/agents/walrusglobal/matrix/`: TPy leaves the global at 1 where CPython has 7). Same root cause as the walrus form fixed on `fix-walrus-global-write`: only the plain-assign path consults `func.global_declarations` (`sema/statements.py`) with the matching `global_declared_vars` render arm in codegen; every other binding form defines into the function scope instead. The three lower to structurally different C++ (loop induction variable / `__enter__` result decl / arm capture decl), so each needs its own sema route + AST arm + THIR arm -- no shared emit chokepoint. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent wrong output) A walrus inside a NESTED def whose target NAME collides with a module global drops the local pre-declaration, so the lambda writes the module variable.** `counter = 5` at module level + `def a(): def inner() -> int: return (counter := 3)` -- with no `global` statement anywhere, AST emits `int32_t counter; return (counter = 3);` (a local shadow, CPython-correct) while THIR emits only `return (counter = 3);`. A non-colliding target (`(fresh := 3)`) keeps its decl on both paths, so the trigger is the module-global name collision in a nested-def body, not the walrus itself. No corpus case covered the shape; surfaced by the inverse test of `fix-walrus-global-write` (`globals/global_walrus_local_shadow`, which now uses a non-colliding name). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent UB, garbage output) A `global` statement inside a NESTED def is ignored: the write emits an UNINITIALIZED local shadow that self-initializes from itself.** `g = 1` at module level + `def outer(): def inner(): global g; g = g + 10; return g` emits `int32_t g = (::tpy::add_check<int32_t>(g, 10));` inside the lambda -- reading `g` before it is initialized -- so TPy prints a nondeterministic value (24918 observed) where CPython prints 11, and the module variable never changes. Reproduces with a plain assignment, an augmented assignment and a walrus alike, so the gap is the nested-def scope of `function_global_decls` / the codegen predecl bookkeeping, not any one binding form (the enclosing function's own `global` writes are handled correctly). Probe `/tmp/agents/walrusglobal/nested_global.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of `fix-walrus-global-write`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A binary operand is re-read AFTER a sibling operand's walrus writes it, so the left operand sees the new value.** `n = 1; return n + (n := n + 100)` yields 202 where CPython yields 102 -- C++ leaves the two operands of `+` unsequenced, and codegen renders the left operand as a bare name read rather than materializing it before the walrus assigns. Generalizes the membership/chained-comparison entry above to plain binops; affects locals and (since `fix-walrus-global-write`) `global`-declared targets alike. Probe `/tmp/agents/walrusglobal/order.py`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) A membership needle or chained-comparison operand is re-read after a sibling operand assigns to it.** `c.n in (bump(c), 1)` and `0 < a.x < bump(a)` (where `bump` writes the operand) answer TPy `False` / CPython `True`: CPython reads each operand once, before the siblings run, while TPy renders it where the write is already visible. Probes `/tmp/agents/chain-dup/{widen,nameneedle,chainwrite,subscript2,walrus4}.py`. Affects every operand shape that names storage -- a bare name, a field, a subscript, a walrus target and a ternary of lvalues were each confirmed on this branch; an operand that renders its own value (a call, a property) is unaffected, since nothing can write it. Same root as the two-operand ordering entry below and unfixed for the same reason -- a fix must capture the operand's VALUE before the sibling runs (a reference re-reads), which costs a copy on every chained compare with a call in it, to fix code that assigns to an operand mid-comparison. Implemented and REVERTED on `fix-operand-snapshot` after review: correct, but it bought a rare guarantee for four new operand predicates plus THIR node fields, and left the two-operand form still wrong, so the guarantee was incoherent. Do it with the two-operand entry, or not at all. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) Tuple-literal membership short-circuits the ELEMENTS, but CPython builds the tuple first and so evaluates every element.** Reachable for a `bytes` needle too since 2026-09-10, when the chain admitted the bytes family. `"A" in (a(), b())` runs only `a()` in TPy (the `==` OR-chain stops at the first match) where CPython runs both before `CONTAINS_OP` -- so an element's side effects are silently skipped. Probe `/tmp/agents/chain-dup/b2_probe.py` (TPy `evaluated: a`, CPython `evaluated: ab`). Distinct from the needle-vs-haystack ORDER entry above: that one is about which side runs first, this is about an element not running at all. The sibling half of the needle entry above: that one is about the needle being re-read, this one about an element never running. Both are open, and a fix for either should consider the other. A fix has to give up the OR-chain's short circuit (materialize every element, then compare) and so trades code size on the common all-literal form, which is why it is not a follow-on tweak. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A PLAIN re-assignment that widens an inferred-`Int32` variable to `BigInt` emits invalid C++ instead of a diagnostic or a coercion -- `cannot convert 'tpy::BigInt' to 'int32_t' in assignment`.** `acc = 0` then `acc = acc * 10 + n` with `n: int` (BigInt): the inferred `Int32` slot keeps its width while the RHS analyzes as `BigInt`, so g++ rejects. Reproduces for a LOCAL (`/tmp/agents/chain-dup/localwiden.py`) and a module GLOBAL (`/tmp/agents/chain-dup/globalwiden.py`) alike, in a 10-line program with no match, loop, or narrowing -- so it is the ordinary assignment path, distinct from (and broader than) the match-arm branch-decl entry above, which shares only the error text. The AUGMENTED form `acc += n` compiles and runs correctly, so the coercion the compound path applies is missing from plain assignment. CPython has one arbitrary-precision int and accepts both. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. Workaround: annotate the accumulator `acc: int = 0`. Fix shape: apply the compound path's widen-or-diagnose rule at plain-assignment re-binding, so the slot either widens with the RHS or the narrowing is reported by sema. Surfaced writing an evaluation-order test during /tpy-fix-bug of the chained-compare hidden-call double-eval. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) The nested-capture retype reject is READ-INSENSITIVE: it fires even when the outer name is never read after the nested bind, where the program was correct before.** `_reject_nested_capture_retype` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) keys on `rebound_captures`, which carries no post-bind-read condition, so `case Cat(lives=v): print(v); match b: case Dog(lives=v): pass` (Int32 outer, Int64 nested, `v` unread afterwards) is rejected although master compiled it and printed the CPython answer. Narrow: it needs BOTH an implicitly C++-convertible type pair AND no later read -- a non-convertible pair (`int`/`str`) already failed the build on master via the branch-decl hoist, and a later read is the truncation the gate exists to catch. The rejected programs are latent rather than correct (the truncating write into the shared slot does happen; only its result is unobserved), so the reject is a rename away and a future read would have made it a silent wrong answer -- that is why the gate ships read-insensitive rather than guessing. Fix shape: gate the error on the name being read after the nested bind, or restrict it to names the definite-assignment predecl would hoist anyway (a proxy for readable-after) and skip the hoist entirely when types disagree otherwise; a wrong read-analysis reinstates the silent truncation, so it needs its own verification pass. Probe `/tmp/agents/nestedmatch/r_noread.py`. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion of the nested-match capture reuse fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) A HOISTED `match` capture of a reference type drops the subject's const, so a never-mutated param subject yields `T* q;` against a `const T&` -- ill-formed C++.** `def show(h: Holder): match h: case Holder(inner=q): print(q.n)` with a post-match read of `q` emits `Inner* q;` then `q = &(__match_subject_1.inner);` where `h` renders `const Holder&`, so g++ reports `invalid conversion from 'const Inner*' to 'Inner*'`. Root cause is phase ordering: `record_stmt_borrow_binding` (`tpyc/sema/context.py:503`) derives the stmt-borrow const flag from the DECLARED type in Phase 1, but a borrowed param's const-ness is decided by mutation inference in Phase 2, so a capture of a never-mutated param reaches the hoist with const=False. Only the hoisted path is affected (a block-scoped `auto&` capture takes the subject's const-ness for free); the hoist fires via the branch-decl predecl (post-match read) or the rebound-capture predecl. A CONTAINER-typed field capture hits the same decl (`std::vector<int32_t>* q;` under a `const Holder&` subject, measured 2026-09-05), so the fix has to cover every reference type, not only records. Loud (toolchain-caught), not silent. `_route_hoists` (`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py:822`) picks the `"ptr_const"` flavor over `"ptr"` only when `_match_capture_borrows_const` (`:793`) sees a NESTED match re-seating the capture; the single-match shape stays on the Phase-1 verdict. Fix shape: settle the borrow const verdict in Phase 2 (or route the decl through `tpyc/codegen_cpp/param_const.py`'s chokepoint), then widen the re-ask to the single-match shape. Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the nested-match capture reuse. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) Mutating through a `match` class-pattern KEYWORD capture does not mark the subject param as mutating, so the emitted C++ writes through a `const` alias and fails to compile.** `def f(h: Holder): match h: case Holder(items=xs): xs.append(9)` emits `int32_t f(const Holder& h)` and then `push_back` on the resulting `const std::vector<int32_t>&` -- ill-formed. Same for a dict field (`t["b"] = 7` -> `__setitem__` on a `const ordered_map&`) and a record field (`q.n = 42`). Mutation propagation enumerates writes through names and field paths but not through a match capture's alias into the subject, so the param keeps its const-borrow verdict. CPython accepts all three (the capture aliases the matched object). Blocks a corpus case that would give the reference-typed keyword-capture family an exec+cpy mutation witness -- today that family is covered only by THIR unit pins and read-only cases, which are parity-blind. Sibling of the HOISTED-capture const entry below and probably one fix: that one loses const on the pointer where the subject IS const, this one never makes the subject non-const in the first place -- both hang on where the borrow const verdict is settled. Distinct from the sibling-arm stale-alias and nested-rebind entries: this one is the subject param's const verdict, not the capture's own binding form. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] A hoisted match capture's SIBLING arm keeps a stale sema alias/borrow fact while codegen emits a copy.** When one arm rebinds a capture name (hoisting it, `fix-match-capture-rebind-hoist`), a sibling arm binding the SAME name is emitted by codegen as an assignment into the hoisted slot -- a copy -- but sema still annotates that arm's capture `bind_by_value=False` and records `record_stmt_borrow_binding` / `nonstmt_borrow_bindings` for it (`tpyc/sema/match.py`), so the borrow fact describes an alias that codegen no longer emits. This breaks the documented "one sema fact drives both codegen and the dangle warning, so they cannot drift" invariant for sibling arms specifically. Latent: no observable divergence found -- the arm-subject-mutation dangle warning fires identically to master on the probe shape (verified: the warning is pre-existing, not introduced; it only becomes VISIBLE because the program now compiles). The risk is a future borrow-based rejection reading the stale fact. Fix shape: when a capture name is hoisted, clear the alias/borrow facts for every arm binding it (codegen's copy is the CPython-correct side). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion of the capture-rebind hoist. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `with ... as` target cannot overwrite an existing scalar local.** [`with-existing-scalar-target-rejected`] A borrowed manager whose `__enter__` returns `Int32`, used as `for b in range(3): / with gate as b: / count += 1`, rejects at `stmt.with`; CPython prints `3`. Matching the manager result and target widths does not avoid the rejection. The original predeclared/hoisted-target witness (`if flag: v = 5 else: v = 6; with Ctx(77) as v:`) was reported to emit pointer-alias assignment into a scalar, causing a C++ build error. The currently fenced loop-target form reaches `_with_target_arm` in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` without a supported scalar reassign arm; range induction does not admit or repair that binding path. Current standalone evidence `/tmp/agents/session-triage/range_with_target.py`, `range-with-target-frontend.log` and `range-with-target-cpy.log`. Recheck the historical hoisted/match-capture siblings when adding the shared scalar assignment form. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) The same `match` capture NAME bound to DIFFERENT types across arms is rejected -- the first arm's type wins.** `case Cat(lives=v): v = v + 1` / `case Dog(name=v): v = "d:" + v` errors `Invalid operand types for '+': str and int` on the second arm: the post-match scope merge (`tpyc/sema/match.py`, the arm-bindings re-define loop) only defines a name absent from `bindings_before`, so the first arm's binding type is what later arms analyze against. CPython is dynamically typed here and accepts it. Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: use distinct capture names per arm. The same one-slot-two-types family covers a capture name that reuses a local declared BEFORE the match at a different type (`v = 0` then `case Cat(lives=v)` -- `tpy::BigInt` assigned into `int32_t`, ill-formed; the pre-existing `declared_vars` bind arm, not the rebound-capture hoist, which only compares types ACROSS arms). Pre-existing (both shapes reproduce on master, unrelated to the capture-rebind hoist). A THIRD shape joined the family with the nested-match capture reuse fix and is rejected the same way: a NESTED match binding the outer arm's capture name at a different type shares one hoisted slot (a `match` is not its own scope), so `_reject_nested_capture_retype` (`tpyc/sema/match.py`) errors at the nested capture. That gate had to be added rather than inherited -- the cross-arm `capture_bind_types` agreement check sees only the current match's own arms -- and it closes a silent hole that predated the fix: where the shared slot already existed via the branch-decl hoist, an implicitly-convertible mismatch (`Int32` slot assigned an `Int64` bind) silently TRUNCATED on master (probe: `705032704` vs CPython `5000000000`); only the no-implicit-conversion pairs failed the build. Test `error_nested_capture_retype`. Workaround is the same: distinct names. NOTE the reject is broader than the numeric case that motivated it: under POLYMORPHIC dispatch a nested reuse naming a different subclass (`case Square() as p:` / nested `case Circle() as p:` off a `@dynamic` protocol subject) is the idiomatic shape and is now rejected, where master silently returned the OUTER arm's object (probe: `4` vs CPython `27`). That sub-shape has a real resolution the numeric one lacks -- bind the shared slot at the common supertype (the protocol / base type) rather than the per-arm concrete type -- so it is the first thing to fix when this entry is picked up. Fix shape: analyze each arm against its OWN pattern-binding type rather than the merged scope entry. Surfaced by the multi-arm probe during the rebound-capture hoist fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] A value-typed match capture rebound via `nonlocal name; name = ...` inside a NESTED DEF in the arm evades the capture-rebind detector, leaving it aliased -- the nonlocal write goes through the `auto&` alias and corrupts the matched object.** `case Cat(name=v): def bump(): nonlocal v; v = "rebound"` -> `written_names`/`body_writes_name` (`parse/nodes.py`) never descends into a nested def (`TpyNestedDef.sub_bodies()` is `[]`, and its writes are a separate scope reached only via `nonlocal`), so the `str`/`BigInt` capture stays bound `auto& v` and `bump()`'s write mutates `subject.name`; CPython rebinds the enclosing local, leaving the matched object untouched (probe: TPy `orig orig` vs CPython `rebound orig`, no diagnostic). Same family as the two match-capture entries above; the fix (value-vs-reference split) never fires because detection misses the nonlocal path. Fix shape: when a nested def declares `nonlocal <capture>` and writes it, count that as a name-level rebind of the outer capture. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the capture-rebind fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] A `list[Ptr[T]]` (or other container) LITERAL drops the element address-of and fails the C++ build.** `items = [Node(1)]` then `ps: list[Ptr[Node]] = [items[0]]` emits `std::vector<Node*> ps = {::tpy::__getitem__(items, 0)};` -- the element render is the `Node&` lvalue, not its address, so g++ rejects (`could not convert ... to std::vector<Node*>`). The container-literal element path has no `Ptr[T]` arm. AST-side and pre-existing, NOT a THIR divergence (dualgen IDENTICAL; THIR falls back at `expr.container_literal`). Toolchain-caught, not silent. Workaround: `ps: list[Ptr[Node]] = []` + `ps.append(items[0])`, which lifts correctly. Also why `tests/cases/tuple/borrow_tuple_ptr_element` carries `no_thir.txt` -- its `main` must build the `list[Ptr[T]]` via `.append`, which falls back at `expr.method_call`. Surfaced writing the corpus case for the borrow-tuple `Ptr[T]` element fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, latent] A borrow-form tuple param's element alias in a RESUMABLE body mis-renders as address-of the element SLOT.** `def show(p: tuple[A, A]) -> Iterator[Int32]: a = p[0]; yield a.x` emits `a = &(std::get<0>(p));` -- the element already IS the pointer (`A*`/`const A*`), so the render produces `A**` into an `A*` frame field, g++ rejects-valid. Pre-existing (reproduces with the old mutable spelling too); corpus-invisible (no resumable case aliases a borrow-tuple param element). The const half of the shape now agrees (frame field, window seeding, and alias classification all read the deep-const verdict since `fix-yield-escape-verdict`); the remaining fix is the alias-ASSIGNMENT emission arm: a pointer-repr tuple element alias must copy the element pointer (`a = std::get<0>(p);`), not take its address -- the `&`-wrap is correct only for value-storage element sources. Probe `/tmp/agents/yieldfix/w3_probe.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small, latent] A bare non-value borrow yield never climbs a field-path alias to its owning param/receiver -- the yield arm omits the `through_field=True` the return arm uses.** `b = o.f` then `yield b` (non-value elem type): the return branch marks with `through_field=True` (statements.py TpyReturn, comment names exactly this climb `b = o.f; return b -> o`), but the pre-existing non-value yield arm calls plain `mark_param_mutated(root)`, so the `"o.f" -> "o"` climb (context.py, through_field-gated) never runs and the owner stays unmarked -- the enclosing method can be wrongly inferred readonly (const receiver vs mutable `val_or_ref<T>` yield slot), the identical failure class the borrow-tuple yield fix closed. The new tuple arm three lines below DOES pass `through_field=True` -- the asymmetry is now intra-yield. Related when fixing: `mark_param_returned` has no 8a.5/field climb at all (loop-iterable + bp sources only), so `b = items[i]; return b` under-records `return_borrows_from` on BOTH sides -- **and so does the plain field alias**: `tmp = self.item; return tmp` records `return_borrows_from=frozenset()` where the direct `return self.item` records `{-1}` (verified by instrumenting `mark_param_returned`: `addr_taken_roots` yields `['tmp']` and `binding_provenance['tmp'].borrow_source_roots` is empty, so the climb has nothing to follow). Consequence beyond the yield asymmetry: `mutation_propagation` blocks readonly inference on `-1 in return_borrows_from`, so a method handing back a mutable borrow of self through a local hop can be wrongly inferred `@readonly`. The `with`-manager provenance question (`returns_borrow_rooted_at_self`) works around this with its own AST-level root walk; fixing the table would let it read the fact off `return_borrows_from` instead -- a combined "yield marking mirrors return marking" fix (this + the transitive-rule entry below) should sweep it. Surfaced by the fix-yield-escape-verdict readiness retrospective. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW-MED small, latent] `yield inner(items)` never propagates the callee's borrow contract -- the return branch's transitive rule (8b rule 3) has no yield analog.** `_analyze_yield`'s escape marking walks `addr_taken_roots(stmt.value)`, which returns `[]` for calls, so a yield of a borrowing call result marks nothing: the callee's `return_borrows_from` is consulted at RETURN sites (`tpyc/sema/statements.py` TpyReturn branch, "8b rule 3") but not at yields. Mechanism verified; the free-fn shape compiles and runs correctly (`/tmp/agents/yieldfix/transitive_probe.py`), so the observable break needs a shape where the missing mark flips a verdict -- e.g. a METHOD generator yielding `pick(self.items)` staying wrongly readonly-inferred (const receiver vs mutable yield slot), or a param verdict staying const. Fix shape: mirror rule 3 at `_analyze_yield`'s marking block (same `resolved_function_info.return_borrows_from` walk, same readonly-callee exemption). Surfaced by /tpy-fix-bug of the yield-escape tuple verdict (the non-transitive half is fixed). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small, latent] A container extended with ITSELF relies on `tpy::list_extend`'s `v.insert(v.end(), other.begin(), other.end())` with `other` aliasing `v` -- standard-UB if the vector reallocates mid-insert.** [`list-self-extend-aliases`] Three spellings reach it, all emitting `::tpy::list_extend(v, v)`: `xs += xs`, the explicit `xs.extend(xs)`, and the FIELD form `self.nums.extend(self.nums)` (the last since 2026-09-05, when the stub arg rows stopped being spelled per receiver kind; the two NAME spellings are pre-existing). Verified working on the current toolchain (g++-14/libstdc++) for both no-realloc and forced-realloc sizes, so latent, not observed; CPython doubles the list. Fix shape, closing all three at once: a one-line self-alias guard in `list_extend` (`if (&other == &v)` reserve first or copy the source) -- the hazard is the runtime helper's, not the lowering's, and fencing the field spelling alone would refuse code the name spelling compiles today. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the pending-list aug-assign fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic quality) An unsupported aug-op on a PENDING container target leaks the internal type repr in the error message.** `xs = [1, 2]; xs *= 2` errors correctly but prints `Operator '*=' is not supported for PendingList[IntLiteral(1), 2]#0` -- the pending type's debug repr, not a user-facing name (the annotated form prints `list[Int32]`). Fix shape: render pending container types through their user-facing resolution (or a `list[...]` placeholder) in diagnostics. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the pending-list aug-assign fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence, pre-existing) A local rebound BEFORE and AFTER another local borrows it silently redirects the borrow to the new value -- the TpyName-reassignment path never runs the while-borrowed check its field/subscript-target siblings have.** `a = Acc(1); a = Acc(50); c = a.peek(b); a = Acc(99); print(c.n)` prints 99 where CPython prints 50: the pre-borrow rebind makes `a` slot-resident (`std::optional<Acc> __slot_N`), `c`'s `const Acc&` binds into that cell, and the post-borrow rebind writes the same cell through the shared rebind slot. NO diagnostic (contrast `a.n = ...`, which warns "Mutation of 'a' while borrowed"). The single-rebind shape (`a = Acc(50); c = ...; a = Acc(99)`) is NOT affected -- the pre-borrow rebind is required. Reproduces via the borrow-returning METHOD spelling on master (pre-existing); the operator spelling (`c = a + b`) newly reaches it since the operator-dunder borrow-return fix. Fix shape: run the borrow-tracker while-borrowed check (`has_borrow_of_kinds`) on TpyName reassignment targets like the TpyFieldAccess arm does (expect warning churn on rebind-heavy code -- audit before enabling), or retarget/invalidate the borrow at the rebind. Probes `/tmp/agents/opreview/reb3.py` (method spelling), the double-rebind operator form per the meta-review. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the operator-dunder borrow-return fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`. Widened 2026-09-04 by the container-call rebind slot: `r = mk(1); r = mk(5); sp = r[1:]; r = mk(9)` reseats the same `__slot_2` under the live span and frees its buffer -- a use-after-free here, not only a value redirect.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid by design, tracked for the real fix) `a += b` falling back to a borrow-returning `__add__` (no `__iadd__`) is REJECTED with a located error -- CPython rebinds `a` to the returned object (aliasing).** The loud reject (sema/statements.py aug-assign fallback) replaced a silent divergence: the emitted in-place update copy-assigned the returned object's fields into `a`'s existing storage, so post-`+=` mutations of the aliased operand were invisible through `a` (TPy 1/1 vs CPython 1/77). The real fix is rebind-as-alias for aug-assign targets: promote the target to a pointer slot (the `aug_assigned` prescan set does not feed the `reassigned` set that drives `T* a` codegen) and register the borrow, mirroring the plain-assignment path. Escape hatches until then (named in the error): define `__iadd__`, or return `Own[...]` from `__add__` (the fresh-value fallback works and matches CPython). Test `error_augassign_borrow_fallback`; inverse in `op_own_return_fresh`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the operator-dunder borrow-return fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) A `__call__` with a concrete `Own[T]` param emits an `operator()` shim that forwards the param by bare name -- no `std::move` -- so the T&& delegation fails the C++ build unconditionally.** The method takes `T&&`; the shim's forward (`return __call__(x);`) passes an lvalue. The property-setter emit already handles this shape (`extension.py` moves Own-typed setter values); `_gen_call_operator` needs the same per-param `std::move` wrap. Loud, pre-existing (identical emit on master; probe `/tmp/agents/opreview/owncall.py`); adjacent to (but not introduced by) the shim-mirroring rework. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (diagnostic noise) "Mutation of 'x' while borrowed (field assignment may invalidate references)" fires on plain RECORD borrows, where a field write cannot invalidate the alias.** [`record-field-borrow-false-invalidation`] The invalidation rationale is container/view reallocation; for a `Cls&` borrow of a record, `a.n = 42` after `c = a.get()` / `c = a + b` is CPython-normal aliasing (the write is correctly visible through `c`) yet warns -- and the operator-dunder borrow-return feature now pins this noise into its own happy-path snapshots (`operators/op_borrow_return_alias` diag). Fix shape: scope the while-borrowed FIELD-assignment warning to borrows whose storage can actually move (containers, views, str/bytes buffers), keeping it for those. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (misleading diagnostic) An UNIMPORTED tpy type name used as a generic type ARGUMENT silently resolves to `?`; the error surfaces later at a use site as e.g. "Cannot index type ArrayList[?]" instead of the missing-import hint.** `al = ArrayList[Int32, 4]()` without `from tpy import Int32` compiles the construction with an unresolved type arg and errors only at `al[0]` ("Cannot index type ArrayList[?]") -- no location pointing at the subscript, no `'Int32' requires: from tpy import Int32` suggestion. Value/annotation positions get the hint (bare `Char("x")` -> "'Char' requires: from tpy import Char"; `Own` in an annotation -> parse-time "requires"), so only the expression-level subscript type-arg slot misses it. Correct rejection, wrong message + location. Fix shape: route unknown names in generic-subscript type-arg position through the same missing-import suggestion machinery instead of yielding an unresolved `?` arg. Repro `/tmp/agents/relcheck` smoke (2 lines). Surfaced by the 0.5.0 wheel-packaging smoke test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A STEPPED slice of a `bytearray` returns `bytes` where CPython returns `bytearray`.** `bytearray(b"abcd")[::2]` is typed (and emitted) as `bytes` per the stub `bytearray.__getitem__(index: slice) -> bytes` (`lib/tpy/tpy/_builtins/_bytes.py`), so downstream `isinstance`/mutation behavior diverges from CPython's fresh `bytearray`. The basic-slice overload returns `BytesView`, a separate documented view design; only the stepped form's concrete owned type is wrong. Fix shape: a `bytearray_stepped_slice` returning `Own[bytearray]` (mirror of `bytes_stepped_slice`; bytearray is a reference type, so unlike the value-typed `bytes` returns the `Own` spelling is load-bearing there). Surfaced by the operator-dunder borrow-return fix's stub-contract sweep (cpython-parity agent). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) `a is b` between two reference-type records is rejected -- "'is' / 'is not' can only compare Optional/Ptr/union types with None" -- where CPython answers identity.** Reference types have stable addresses in TPy, so `is` is expressible as an address compare; today only None/enum/bool-literal compares are allowed (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py:983`). With borrow-returning dunders/methods now genuinely aliasing, identity is only observable via mutation -- a first-class `is` would let tests and users assert aliasing directly. Value-type operands should stay rejected (no identity). Loud, pre-existing. Surfaced writing the operator-dunder borrow-return aliasing tests. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (semantics decision for mixed value/reference operands).
- **[LOW small] (accepts-invalid) A bound `self.__init__(...)` call from a NON-`__init__` method passes sema and emits `this->__init__(...)` -- a call to a nonexistent C++ member (only the real ctor exists), failing the C++ build.** Only the unbound `Parent.__init__(self, ...)` and `super().__init__()` spellings are sema-gated to inside `__init__` (`methods.py`); the bound form slips through. Loud today (g++ rejects), but note for any future fix: a naive destroy+reconstruct re-init emission would BYPASS the CPython-interop `has_views_into` guard (tp_init's registry scan protects only the boundary path), so a TPy-side re-init must either be rejected like the unbound forms or route through the same live-view check. Probe `/tmp/agents/reinit_probe.py`. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion on the borrow-view rung.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) A by-value FIELD typed as a DERIVED class emits an incomplete-type C++ error regardless of source order -- derived-class definitions are sorted after all plain records.** `class A: ...; class B(A): pass; class C: b: B` fails `field 'b' has incomplete type 'B'`: `sort_records_by_inheritance` emits every non-derived record's full definition before any derived one's, so a plain record holding a derived-typed field can never see the complete type first (moving `B` earlier in the source does not help). CPython accepts the program. Loud (toolchain-caught). Fix shape: make the record sort field-dependency-aware (a by-value field edge is as hard a dependency as a base-class edge). Probe `/tmp/.../ordprobe/main.py` (10 lines). Surfaced building the borrow-view upcast test (which it blocks -- the classifier's exact-match gate is unit-pinned in `tpyc/interop/test_export_shape_views.py` instead). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) `print(...)` writes each argument as it is evaluated, so an argument whose evaluation itself writes to stdout interleaves ahead of the earlier arguments' output.** `print("prefix:", noisy())` where `noisy()` prints `side effect` and returns 7 emits `prefix: side effect` then `7`; CPython evaluates the whole argument list first and emits `side effect` then `prefix: 7`. The call lowers to a chained `std::cout << "prefix: " << noisy()`, and C++17 sequences an overloaded `<<`'s left operand before its right, so the literal reaches the stream before the callee runs. Silent, output-only, and needs a print argument that itself writes to stdout -- a debug/logging helper nested in a print is the realistic shape. Distinct from the reflected-binop and hoisted-arg ordering entries: those reorder the *evaluations*, this one interleaves the *output* while evaluation order is correct. Fix shape: evaluate every argument into temps before the first stream write (the temp-hoist machinery already exists for other arg shapes). Repro `/tmp/agents/scopens/v_print_order.py`. Surfaced while re-verifying the with-target optional-copy entry, whose probe made the interleaving visible. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) A REFLECTED record-dunder binop (`x // y` resolving `__rfloordiv__`) evaluates the right operand before the left -- CPython evaluates left-to-right.** The `is_reverse` swap (`wl, wr = wr, wl` in `_emit_binop`, `tpyc/thir/emit.py:755`, the swap at `:792`) happens before `expand_cpp_template` embeds the operand renders positionally (`({self}).__rfloordiv__({0})`), and C++ sequences the receiver expression before the argument -- so `make_n() // make_b()` with side-effecting operands prints `make_b, make_n` where CPython prints `make_n, make_b` (reflected dispatch happens AFTER both operands evaluate, left-to-right). Confirmed against CPython over `lib/cpy` on the same source. Silent -- output-only, observable only when both operands carry side effects (no corpus case; `truediv_floordiv_distinct` uses names/literals). Same class as the membership needle/haystack entry below; the fix is an evaluation-order temp for the left operand before the swapped render. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing the record-dunder rvalue admission (2026-07-22 wave). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (silent CPython divergence) Membership with a CALL haystack evaluates the haystack before the needle -- CPython evaluates the needle first.** `needle_expr in f()` emits the haystack call's render first (the receiver of `.contains`/`.find`/`__contains__`), then the needle; CPython's bytecode evaluates the needle expression before the container expression, so when BOTH sides have side effects the observable order differs. Silent -- output-only divergence, only observable when both operand expressions carry side effects (rare; no corpus case). Both codegen paths share the shape (the AST membership arms and THIR's mirrors emit identically), so this is NOT a THIR drift -- fixing it means an evaluation-order temp (`auto&& __in_lhs = <needle>;` before the receiver render, like the tuple-literal membership arm already does) in BOTH paths, or accepting and documenting the divergence. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) probing the wave-next membership widenings; pre-existing, unchanged by that wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid) An auto_readonly accessor whose body returns a reference field via a TERNARY into `T | None` is rejected on the const twin, though the equivalent statement form compiles.** `def __getitem__(self, w: Int32) -> Rec | None: return self._v if w > 0 else None` (`_v: Rec`, a reference type) errors `Cannot pass readonly[Rec] as mutable readonly[Rec] | None in ternary branch`; the statement form (`if w > 0: return self._v` / `return None`) compiles and aliases correctly. Root cause: the implicit-auto_readonly const twin (readonly `self` => `self._v` is `readonly[Rec]`) checks the ternary return arm against the UN-projected mutable `Rec | None` return type, where the statement-return path projects const onto the return. Distinct from the mixed-arm ternary silent-copy entry below (that is a local-binding value-category copy with no diagnostic; this is a hard sema reject on a return). Loud (sema-rejected), not silent. Workaround: use the statement form. Pre-existing (unrelated to the `getitem_function_info` tagging); surfaced writing the accessor-generic-returns temporary-receiver test. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug` (project const onto the const-twin ternary return arm, mirroring the statement-return path).
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A METHOD returning a ptr-variant union (`-> Dog | Cat`) is a hard compile error -- in the body, and again at the call site.** `class Kennel: animal: Dog | Cat` with `def __getitem__(self, i: Int32) -> Dog | Cat: return self.animal` prints `error: in function '__getitem__': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.return)`; renaming the accessor to a plain `pick` rejects identically, and a method that merely relays a union PARAM compiles its body then rejects at the consumer with `(expr.method_call:method.ret_type)` (`tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:9862`/`:12870`, `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:9036`). A FREE function with the same signature (`def pick(a: Dog | Cat) -> Dog | Cat: return a`) compiles and runs, so the reject is method-specific. The old analysis still names the shape to fix: `_apply_implicit_auto_readonly` (`tpyc/sema/method_expansion.py`) wraps ANY non-value accessor return in `ReadonlyType`, and `is_ptr_variant_union` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/forms.py`) never unwraps `ReadonlyType`, so the const twin's return slot is a `std::variant<const Cat*, const Dog*>` no return row can fill. Fix mirrors the Optional arm: unwrap `ReadonlyType(UnionType)` (or teach `is_ptr_variant_union` to see through the readonly wrapper) so the ptr-variant lift applies. Not exotic -- a union-returning getter or accessor is an ordinary shape -- so worth queueing. Same accessor-return family as the `@property` pointer-repr `Optional` entry below. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + meta-review reproduction) of the accessor-generic-returns branch. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Reading an `Own[...]`-returning `@property` at a borrow-alias decl or a for-loop head binds a non-const reference to the by-value getter result -- uncompilable C++.** `@property def snapshot(self) -> Own[list[Int32]]: ...` then `s = c.snapshot` emits `std::vector<int32_t>& s = c.snapshot();` (g++: cannot bind non-const lvalue reference to an rvalue; verified by building the repro), and `for x in c.snapshot:` emits `auto& __obj_0 = c.snapshot();` -- same failure. The property-read consumers assume a borrow-returning getter (the plain `@property` case) and never consult the getter fi's `Own` return; a CONST receiver accidentally compiles the decl flavor (`const T&` lifetime-extends the temporary), which is why the shape can hide. Toolchain-caught, not silent; no corpus case exercises it. THIR fences the shape rather than mirror it (the property REF_ALIAS decl row and the property foreach leg both reject an Own-returning getter -- `decl.own_property_alias` / `foreach.own_property_iter`; the unit that pinned them went with the THIR unit suite); fixing the AST (owning capture: `auto __obj_N = ...` / a value decl, like the method-call iterable's Own leg) unfences it. Repros `/tmp/agents/thir-tail-0821/impl-rd/smoke/e_prop_mut.py` (decl, build error) and `e_prop.py` (foreach). Same accessor-return family as the `@property` pointer-repr Optional entry below. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen while widening the THIR property-position rows. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A `@property` getter returning a pointer-repr `Optional[T]` (`-> Rec | None`) emits an `std::optional<T>&`-returning accessor whose body returns rvalues/nullptr -- uncompilable C++ for any non-field-backed getter.** A getter whose body is `if self.on: return self._v` / `return None` over a plain `Rec` field emits `inline std::optional<Rec>& Holder::value() { if (this->on) { return &(this->_v); } return nullptr; }` (and the same for the const twin), so g++ reports `invalid initialization of non-const reference of type 'std::optional<Rec>&' from an rvalue of type 'Rec*'` and the `std::nullptr_t` twin. The SIGNATURE convention is the printer layer's: `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py:1581` gives a property getter the storage `std::optional<T>&` (or `std::variant<A,B>&`) return instead of the method convention (`T*`), which only holds when the body returns a stored optional FIELD; the body honours it at exactly one return row (`ret.opt_field_ref`, `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:11629`, a bare `self.f` read) and every other return takes the ordinary pointer-lift arms. Toolchain-caught, not silent. The fix must pick ONE convention for optional-returning property getters (likely the method convention: return `T*`, adjusting the property-read consumption sites symmetrically). Same accessor-optional family as the record-`__getitem__` fix on `fix-accessor-generic-returns` -- there the CONSUMER was wrong, here the EMISSION convention is. Surfaced by the accessor-generic-returns analysis (Phase 4 sibling survey). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (miscompile) A plain record pointer-local reseated from a `readonly[T]` param emits `Point* p = &(q);` off a `const Point&` -- invalid const conversion, uncompilable.** `def f(q: readonly[Point], c: bool): p = Point(1); ...; p = q` renders the address-of without const-propagating the pointer decl (`const_indirect_locals` never sees the reseat-source constness). Identical on BOTH the AST and THIR paths (byte-identical, both broken); no corpus case exercises it. Either propagate const from the reseat source into the decl (making every read `const Point*`) or reject at sema (a mutable-pointer local aliasing a readonly param is arguably a readonly-model violation -- consider the sema-error tier first). Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the escape-hoist cell.
- **[LOW small] (crash) A container literal first declared inside an if/try/with/match branch of a NESTED def crashes codegen with `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen`.** The nested def's `FunctionTrackingState` is discarded by `nested_def_scope` (`tpyc/sema/scope_tracker.py`) via `restore_function_state` without ever running `LocalTypeDeduction.resolve_all()` on it, so the nested body's pending stores -- `pending_branch_decl_maps`, and the sibling `pending_composite_exprs` / `pending_loop_vars` -- are lost unfinalized. The enclosing-function flavors are fixed (branch-decl snapshots finalized in resolve_all); this is the same class through a different lifecycle root (nested-def analysis never runs per-function finalization). Repro: `def outer(c): def inner(): if c: xs = [1, 2] else: xs = [3]; return xs[0]; return inner()`. Fix shape: run the deferred-resolution finalization for the nested state before `nested_def_scope` discards it (covers all three stores at once). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + safety-model) of `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (silent CPython divergence) `list(d.values())` / `list(d.keys())` over a dict with REFERENCE-type elements copies where CPython aliases, with NO warning -- the bound-container form of the same copy DOES warn.** `d: dict[str, Node]; vals = list(d.values()); d["a"].v = 999; print(vals[0].v)` prints `1` under TPy and `999` under CPython, and `tpyc` emits nothing; the sibling `c = list(b)` over a still-live `b: list[Node]` emits `warning: copies Node elements; use copy_iter() to make this explicit (or copy() to copy the entire container)`. Both verified at `c95406e26` and at HEAD. The divergence itself is the accepted materialization semantics (`docs` calls this out for container ctors) -- the DEFECT is that the diagnostic that makes it non-silent does not fire for a dict-view source. Suspected site: the warning gate in `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` (~855-900) keys on an lvalue source or on an rvalue whose element type carries a semantic `Ref`, and a dict-view rvalue satisfies neither; NOT runtime-confirmed, so treat the mechanism as a lead rather than a root cause. Codegen-path-independent (the shape falls back to the AST path entirely). Fix shape: extend the warning gate's rvalue arm to dict/container VIEW sources, whose elements are borrows of the parent container. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the THIR instantiation-gate wave; pre-existing, unrelated to that wave. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (crash) A container instantiation over a literal with NESTED literal elements crashes codegen: `PendingListType should be resolved before codegen`.** `a = list([[1, 2], [3]])` (also the single-element `list([[1, 2]])`) at plain function scope -- no nested def, no branch topology, so this is NOT the nested-def lifecycle entry above. The OUTER literal resolves (it is the call's arg), but the inner literals stay `PendingListType` and reach `to_cpp()` through the ctor's `@cpp_template` substitution (`_resolve_cpp_template_type_params`, `tpyc/sema/calls.py:361` -> `typesys.py:4181`) -- the instantiation path never runs the nested-literal resolution that the equivalent annotated decl (`a: list[list[Int32]] = [[1, 2], [3]]`) does. Flat element literals are fine (`list([1, 2])`); the named-local form (`src: list[list[Int32]] = [[1, 2]]; a = list(src)`) compiles. Same expected-type-into-nested-literal family as the annotated dict-literal-of-list-literals entry below. Fix shape: resolve the arg literal's nested element types before the ctor template substitution reads them. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen probes around the THIR container-literal instantiation arm; pre-existing on master. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) A NESTED list literal first declared in sibling branches (`try: xs = [[1, 2]] except ...: xs = [[3]]`) fails the C++ build at the branch slot-assign render.** The branch-decl force now resolves both nesting levels to plain `vector` (the type side is sound -- `_force_branch_decl_lists` recurses into the pending element type), but the slot-assign arm renders the nested literal as a flat brace-init against `std::optional<std::vector<std::vector<int>>>`, which trips the explicit `vector(size_type, alloc)` constructor (g++ "would use explicit constructor"). Flat literals work; a nested literal in a PLAIN decl also works (different emit arm) -- only the branch predecl slot-assign spelling is wrong. Probe `/tmp/agents/plfix/p_nested1.py`. Fix shape: render the literal through the same nested-container emit the plain decl uses (typed construction, not bare brace-init) at the slot-assign arm. Surfaced by the readiness retrospective's nested-literal probe on `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid, loud) Calling an `auto_own[Self]` method directly on a freshly-constructed temporary fails the C++ build.** `Pair[Node](a, b).first()` passes sema, selects the consuming (`&&`) overload, and moves the field -- but codegen still types the bound local as `Node&`, so g++ rejects it ("cannot bind non-const lvalue reference to an rvalue"). The named-local form (`p = Pair[Node](a, b); p.first()`) compiles: a general method call hard-codes `is_consuming_receiver=False` (`tpyc/sema/methods.py`), so only the rvalue-receiver syntax reaches the consuming overload. Fix shape: bind the consuming call's result by value (or reject the rvalue-receiver form at sema) -- decide which, the render is currently inconsistent with the overload it selected. Pre-existing on master (verified in a worktree); surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) while checking the auto_own clone-pair carve-out. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (rejects-valid) Reassigning an alias to a NESTED list element fails when the outer list is unannotated.** `m = [[Point(1)], [Point(2)]]; row = m[0]; row = m[1]` errors with `Type mismatch in reassignment to 'row': expected list[Point], got Ref[PendingList[Point, 1]#0]` -- the element's pending type never resolves before the reassignment compatibility check, so the SECOND bind compares a resolved `list[Point]` against a raw pending node. The annotated form (`m: list[list[Point]] = ...`) compiles and runs. Two defects in one: the code is valid and rejected, and the message leaks the internal repr (the same leak as the pending aug-op entry above, different trigger). Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/bugcheck/main.py`. Fix shape: resolve the subscript result's pending element type before `coerce_reassignment` compares it. Surfaced by adversarial dualgen probes around the THIR element-borrow decl arm; pre-existing on master, unrelated to that cell. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container literal first declared in a try's ELSE body (with the except-handler declaring the same name) emits assignments to an undeclared predecl slot -- g++ `'xs' was not declared in this scope` / `'__slot_N' was not declared`.** `try: ... except ValueError: xs = [3] else: xs = [1, 2]` then a post-try read: the branch-decl predecl machinery covers the handler's decl but the ELSE body's assignment renders the slot/pointer form (`xs = &*(__slot_2 = {1, 2})`) without the corresponding declarations reaching its scope. The try/except both-branch merge (decl in try body + handler) works; only the else-body topology is broken. Pending-type resolution is NOT the issue (the resolved brace-init shows in the bad emit) -- this is a predecl scoping hole in the try emit. Probe `/tmp/agents/plfix/p_try_else.py`. Surfaced pinning a cpython-parity probe during the `fix-pendinglist-branch-decls` review. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A tuple ternary whose arms carry DIFFERENT C++ tuple forms is a hard compile error.** `t = p if c else h.pair` (a borrow-form `std::tuple<Int32, Box*>` param against a storage-form `std::tuple<Int32, Box>` field) prints `error: in function 'f': this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation (stmt.var_decl:decl.slot_type)` -- the decl's slot ladder (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py:9978`) has no row for a ternary whose arms disagree on tuple form, so nothing lifts one side to the other's. The const-qualification twin is caught earlier and better, by sema: two params differing only in `readonly[...]` on an element give `Incompatible types in ternary expression: 'tuple[Int32, Box]' and 'tuple[Int32, readonly[Box]]'`. Loud either way. Fix shape: give the tuple ternary a row that lifts a storage arm via `tuple_to_pointer`, or reject the mixed pair in sema with the message the readonly twin already gets. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the wave-next13 tuple-ternary admission. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (misleading diagnostic) The per-element `Own`-coercion warning and error name the WHOLE tuple where a single element is at stake.** Rebinding a mixed tuple local to an all-borrow storage source (`p = h.pair` for `p: tuple[Own[Box], Box]`) warns `copies tuple[Box, Box] into owned storage; use copy() to make this explicit` -- but only element 0 is copied; element 1 still aliases, which the pinned case's own output shows (`elem0: 7`, `elem1: 66`). The `@nocopy` variant is worse: `cannot copy tuple[Guard, Box] into owned storage of type 'Guard'; target is non-copyable` conflates the whole-tuple SOURCE type with one element's TARGET type in a single sentence. Root cause: the tuple-to-tuple element-wise compat recursion (`_check_compat`, `tpyc/sema/compatibility.py` ~1141) passes the whole-tuple `source_expr` unchanged into each per-element check, so the generic Own-coercion message reads `get_expr_type(source_expr)` -- the aggregate -- instead of the element's own type. The sibling `warn_pointer_repr_tuple_copy` path (container append) already gets this right and appends `(tuple element i)`, so it is the fix shape: pass the element's source (or at least the index) into the per-element check. Not silent and not a miscompile, but it weakens the "warned, therefore acknowledged" premise the `tuple/mixed_own_tuple_local_realias` `no_cpython` pin rests on -- a user can reasonably read it as "the whole tuple is deep-copied". Pre-existing in `compatibility.py`; newly REACHABLE because the mixed-tuple rebind now compiles. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the mixed-tuple decl-path fix. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Param mutation inference does not reach through a TERNARY call argument, so a param mutated only via a ternary is inferred const and the C++ build fails.** `def via(b: Box, c: Box, pick: bool) -> Int32: return bump(b if pick else c)` (where `bump(b: Box)` writes `b.val`) emits `int32_t via(const Box& b, const Box& c, bool pick)` and then `bump(((pick) ? (b) : (c)))` -- g++ `binding reference of type 'Box&' to 'const Box' discards qualifiers`. Passing the same param DIRECTLY (`bump(b)`) infers `Box&` correctly, so the gap is the ternary arg specifically: `mutation_propagation` walks call args but does not descend into a `TpyIfExpr` to attribute the callee's mutation to each arm's name. Loud (toolchain-caught), no TPy diagnostic, pre-existing (reproduces at merge base). Any arg shape that wraps names in an expression is worth checking with it (an `and`/`or` arm is the obvious sibling). Workaround: bind the selected object to a local first, or use an if/else statement. Reproducer `/tmp/agents/mixdecl/y2_ternary_const.py`. Surfaced probing decl paths during the mixed-tuple borrow-position work. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) Param mutation inference does not reach a LOOP ELEMENT passed to a mutating callee, so the source param is inferred const and the C++ build fails.** `def f(*ps: Point): for p in ps: touch(p)` (where `touch(p: Point)` writes `p.x`) emits `void f(::tpy::varargs<const Point> ps)` and then `touch(p)` -- g++ `binding reference of type 'Point&' to 'const Point' discards qualifiers`. Mutating the element DIRECTLY in the loop body (`p.x += 1`) infers the mutable slot correctly, so the gap is specifically a mutation that only happens inside a callee: `mutation_propagation` attributes the callee's param mutation to the loop VARIABLE, and neither the vararg flip (`_maybe_flip_vararg_readonly`, `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) nor its sibling `_sync_inferred_const` climbs from a loop var to the container/pack it iterates. Not vararg-specific and not generator-specific -- measured on all four cells: `*args` pack and plain `list[Point]` param, each on a plain function and on a generator (the generator twin emits `touch((*p))` against the same const element). Loud (toolchain-caught), no TPy diagnostic; pre-existing (the vararg flip and the const inference both predate the frame's varargs admission). Workaround: mutate the element inline in the loop body, or take an explicitly mutable slot. Reproducers `/tmp/agents/fixround/p17_flip.py` (pack, plain fn), `p18_flip_gen.py` (pack, generator), `p19_list_sibling.py` (plain `list` param). Fix shape: mutation propagation must map "loop var over X is mutated" back to X (the same climb `_borrow_storage_root`/`loop_var_iterable` already record for borrow tracking), so both const-inference flips see it. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the resumable-frame varargs admission. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) A container literal first declared inside a TRY body of a generator/async function types the frame slot from one arm's fixed-size Array while the writes emplace a vector -- g++ "no matching function for call to `emplace`".** `async def f(n): try: xs = [n, n] except ValueError: xs = [0]` + a post-try read emits `::tpy::frame_slot<std::array<int32_t, 1>> xs;` (the size from the HANDLER's literal) against `xs.emplace(std::vector<int32_t>{n, n});` -- the write site reads the sema branch-decl snapshot (forced off the Array optimization by `_force_branch_decl_lists`, so `list[Int32]`), but the frame-slot field is spelled from `func.generator_locals`, which keeps the unforced per-decl type. The if/else and match-arm topologies are correct (their frame local carries the merged list), so the gap is the generator-locals collection not consulting the branch-decl snapshot. Loud (toolchain-caught). Repro `/tmp/agents/thir-wave/smoke13/trybody4/main.py` (`tpyc --dump-code` shows the mismatch directly). Fix shape: apply the branch-decl snapshot type when collecting generator locals (the same override `_emit_branch_decls` performs on `var_types`), so the slot and its writes agree.
