Surfaced implementing audit #10 item 5. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] An explicit `s: str = <view>` annotation is silently downgraded to view storage, binding owned-copy temporary into a `std::string_view` -- dangling.** `def use(sv: StrView): s: str = sv` emits `std::string_view s = std::string(sv);` -- the `str` (owned) annotation is overridden to view storage by the pending-view machinery (`is_view_compatible_source` returns view-safe for a view-typed source, so `initialized_from_owned=False`), yet the source coercion still materializes an owned `std::string(sv)` temporary; the result is a view into a destroyed temporary. Same for `s: str = make().strip()`. Root cause: the pending-view storage decision ignores an explicit OWNED annotation (it should force owned storage when the user wrote `str`/`bytes`), and the storage-vs-coercion choice is uncoordinated. Pre-existing; surfaced probing the view-lifetime cluster (audit #10). **Fix shape:** when the local has an explicit owned (`str`/`bytes`) annotation, resolve to owned storage unconditionally (no view downgrade); keep the owned-copy coercion. Distinct from the inferred-local promotion (#10 item 3), which routes `initialized_from_owned=True` to owned storage and is unaffected. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (precision, not unsound)** `await x` reads the awaitable's `__poll__` `is_readonly` at Phase-1 analysis time (`_analyze_await` -> `_extract_awaitable_inner`, `tpyc/sema/expressions.py`); auto-readonly is a Phase-2 fixpoint fact. A *user-defined* awaitable whose `__poll__` is only inferred `@readonly` in Phase 2 (no `@readonly` annotation, no direct mutation) reads `is_readonly=False` here, so `_mark_await_operand_mutated` over-marks the awaited operand's root -- blocking the enclosing async method's auto-readonly inference even though awaiting that awaitable doesn't actually mutate it. Over-approximation: conservative and never unsound (a method wrongly kept non-readonly, never wrongly readonly), and stdlib awaitables (`Task`/`Future`/`Event`/`SleepFuture`) all mutate in `__poll__` so they're unaffected. Fix shape: defer the await-mutation mark to Phase 2 via a call edge (mirroring `_is_self_call_deferred` for `self.method()`), or consult the Phase-2-finalized `__poll__` readonly verdict. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the await-self-mutation fix.
- **[LOW small] (by design, not a regression) Post-sema `replace_expr` injects AST that bypasses sema re-analysis.** `PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.replace_expr` (inherited from `FunctionMacroContext`, `tpyc/macro_api.py`) splices nodes after pass 7, so the injected nodes get no mutation-fact collection (no `call_edges` for new calls -> Phase-2 propagation can miss a mutating call -- `PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.note_param_mutated` is a manual escape hatch for the param-rooted mutating-call sub-case, but it only seeds `direct_mutated_params`, not `direct_structural_mutated_params`, so an emitted *structurally*-mutating call (append/insert/clear on a param) is still unrecorded), no borrow-check registration, no `deref_check` insertion, and no narrowing/readonly enforcement. The contract is documented (the caller must `set_expr_type` every emitted node and is responsible for safety), and this is inherent to the whole macro system (pre-sema `replace_expr`, builder-trace `emit_function`, and class macros already inject un-rechecked AST) -- a known limitation, not a defect introduced here. A macro that injects only value-type expressions (the shipped test) is safe. **Fix shape (future):** restrict the post-sema surface to value-type replacements (enforce via `type_of`/`set_expr_type`), or re-run the relevant sema checks over injected subtrees once the IR makes that cheap. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model) of the post-sema function-macro phase.
- **[MED, latent] A view param (`Span[T]`) stored into a field passes sema with no diagnostic -- the field dangles when the caller's buffer dies (silent UAF).** `def keep(self, v: Span[Int32]) -> None: self._s = v` compiles clean; the stored span outlives whatever backing the caller passed. At the `@export` CPython boundary the glue's copy-in vector dies when the wrapper returns, making the store an unconditional UAF on the next payload read for any exposed METHOD taking a `Span` param (property `Span` setters are rejected outright for exactly this reason -- a setter's purpose is storing -- so only the method surface remains exposed). The existing view-escape entries in this section cover the RETURN direction; this is the param-stored-into-field direction. Not expressible as a passing test (silent UAF). Fix shape: reject (or warn on) a view-typed param assigned into field storage, pending the region/lifetime model's loan-extent form. Probe: a `Span` setter body `self._s = v` compiled with zero diagnostics. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness, safety-model) of the exposed-class @property rung. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] (rejects-valid, loud) `Own[readonly[@dynamic P]]` at a call argument is a hard compile error, and the param signature still renders the abstract base by rvalue-ref.** `def park(coro: Own[readonly[Cancellable[Int32]]]) -> None` renders the param as `::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>&& coro` -- the abstract base by rvalue reference, not the erased `unique_ptr<P>` -- because the ReadonlyType wrapper defeats `is_dyn_protocol` in the Own-dyn slot key (`_dyn_own_coro_handle_arg`, `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py:8899-8919`, which reads `OwnType.wrapped` RAW with no readonly peel), so the Own-dyn erasure arm never fires. The old silent-miscompile symptom is gone: a call `park(c)` is now rejected with `expr.call:call.arg_shape.own_protocol.dyn` ("this construct is not yet supported by C++ code generation"), so valid code is refused loudly instead of emitting an unbindable argument. Dropping the `readonly` makes the same program work (`std::unique_ptr<::tpystd::coro::Cancellable<int32_t>> coro` at the signature + `::tpy::make_adapter<...>(std::move(*(c)))` at the call), so this is purely the Own+readonly composition; a signature-only program with no call still compiles, since the bogus `&&` param is never bound. Exotic shape rather than an everyday one (readonly-ness of an owned erased handle has no meaningful surface), but the message the user gets is the generic codegen-reject text, not an explanation. Related family to the readonly-protocol entries above but a distinct shape. Fix shape: either reject `Own[readonly[@dynamic P]]` params in sema with a real diagnostic, or peel the readonly in the slot key and the signature render together. Surfaced by the THIR Own-arg cell's adversarial probe (2026-07-17). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[LOW small] (latent, benign as emitted) A NARROWED `Optional[container]` field at an EQUALITY operand loses its unwrap.** `if self.lst is not None: return self.lst == self.other` (on `lst: list[Int32] | None`, `other: list[Int32]`) emits `(this->lst == this->other)`, where the unwrapped `((*this->lst) == this->other)` is the intended form -- no corpus case witnesses it. Root cause: the compare-operand sink threads `allow_whole_optional`, which suppresses the read's `narrowed_deref` flag, while the gate (`_container_compare_pair`) keys the NARROWED analyzed types and so admits the pair; the `field.whole_optional` arm then claims the read. C++ makes the emitted form compile and (for `==`/`!=` on a proven-non-None optional) agree at runtime via `std::optional`'s mixed comparison, which is why nothing has caught it. Fix shape: do not thread `allow_whole_optional` into a compare operand whose partner is a bare container (or exclude a declared-Optional/analyzed-container mismatch from the `field.whole_optional` arm at that sink). No corpus witness. Repro `/tmp/agents/cell-optfield/b7_cmp_only.py`. Surfaced by the boundary sweep of the THIR `Optional[container]`-field cell (2026-08-19). Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[MED small] `readonly` is not transitive through a value record's VIEW members: a `Span[readonly[W]]` element hands back a `W` whose `Span[Int32]` member still aliases the same backing MUTABLY.** `class W(ValueType): data: Span[Int32]` plus `def f(ws: Span[readonly[W]]) -> W: return ws[0]` emits `W f(std::span<const W> ws) { return ::tpy::__getitem__(ws, 0); }` -- the element is `const W&`, but the copy taken out of it carries `std::span<int32_t>` (the pointee is not const), so `out.data[0] = 99` writes through the readonly view with no diagnostic and the caller's buffer observes 99. `readonly[T]` const-qualifies the record OBJECT, not the storage its view members point at, and a value record's by-value copy drops the object's const-ness while keeping the members' aliases. PRE-EXISTING and not about the return: a plain local binding `w = ws[0]` launders identically, and so does the direct `ws[0].data[0] = 99`, so the gap is in the readonly TYPE rule, not in any one sink. Fix shape: propagate `readonly` into the view-typed members of a readonly record (the element type of a `Span`/`Ptr` field becomes `readonly[...]` under a readonly receiver), which needs the readonly system to rewrite member types rather than only qualify the receiver. Reproduced 2026-09-02 with `uv run tpy` (prints 99 where the readonly view promises no write); repro `/tmp/agents/paper2/bugs/roview.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
- **[HIGH small] (silent wrong output, dangling) A TEMPORARY argument or receiver of a delegated generator call dies before the embedded frame is first resumed.** [`resumable-delegate-temp-source-dangles`] A `for x in <gen call>:` with a yield/await in its body embeds the callee's frame in a `__for_src` field, and that frame BORROWS the call's arguments and receiver -- but a temporary among them is materialized in the enclosing `case S_RESUME_N: { ... }` block of the consumer's `__next__` switch (or not at all, for a view), so it is destroyed before the first `(*__for_src_0).__next__()` runs in the next case. Three reproducers, all same-module and all diverging from CPython (`PYTHONPATH=lib/cpy python3`): (a) reference-typed temporary ARGUMENT -- `def make_list() -> Own[list[Int32]]: return [11, 22]`, `def walk(xs: list[Int32]) -> Iterator[Int32]: yield xs[0]; yield xs[1]`, `def gen() -> Iterator[Int32]: yield 0; (for x in walk(make_list()): yield x)` prints `0` then two garbage integers where CPython prints `0 11 22`; this one DOES warn ("Iterator borrows from temporary argument 'xs'; the temporary is destroyed before iteration begins") yet still compiles and runs. (b) a `StrView` over a temporary `str` -- same `gen`, with `def make_str() -> str: return "abcdefgh"` and `walk(make_str()[1:4])` over `def walk(s: StrView) -> Iterator[StrView]` -- prints `start` then two blank lines where CPython prints `start bcd bcd`, with NO diagnostic: no temp is hoisted at all, the emitted `__for_src_0.emplace(walk(::tpy::str_slice(make_str(), ...)));` lets the owning `std::string` die at that statement's semicolon while the frame keeps the view. (c) a temporary RECEIVER -- `class Bag` with `readings()` yielding `self.n` and `self.n + 1`, and `for v in Bag(7).readings():` inside a resumable `gen` -- emits `Bag __tmp_1 = Bag(7); __for_src_0.emplace(__tmp_1.readings());` and prints `0 0 1` where CPython prints `0 7 8`, again with NO diagnostic. Root cause is one thing in all three: the delegated source's operands are given BLOCK lifetime (or, for a view, full-expression lifetime) while the frame that borrows them has FRAME lifetime -- the `__for_src` / `__for_r` slots are frame fields precisely because they must survive across suspensions, and the temporaries feeding them were not given the same treatment. PRE-EXISTING and reachable from ordinary same-module code; the (b)/(c) legs are silent, which is what makes it HIGH. Fix shape: hoist the temporary into a frame field alive for the loop's lifetime, exactly as `__for_src`/`__for_r` already are (materialize it in a `frame_slot<T>` emplaced in the same case block, destroyed at loop exit), which covers the receiver and the owning source behind a view alike; with that in place the warned case (a) becomes correct and the warning goes -- if the hoist is not taken for some operand shape, that shape must become a hard reject rather than a warning that still emits. Probes `/tmp/agents/dangtmp/{a,b,c}.py`. Needs `/tpy-fix-bug`.
